Alfardan Group -- Salesforce R1 Solution Design (Customer Review)

Draft for customer review -- not build sign-off.

Page objective

Give reviewers one entry point to the Release 1 Salesforce solution design: what is designed,
what we need you to confirm, and how to work through the pages.

Business scope

The full Release 1 scope for Alfardan Automobiles, Alfardan Premier Motors, and Alfardan Sports
Motors: lead management, the shared customer master, the retail sales lifecycle (quotation to
handover), test drives and trade-ins, vehicle/product/inventory data, the internal requisition
document, case management, workshop service appointments, integration context, security
framing, and reporting.

Design summary

Sixteen child pages carry the solution design. Each process page contains the end-to-end
process design, the Salesforce object/field/status design, data and integration design, and its
open items. The design is decision-led: choices that are made are stated as R1 Solution Design;
items that genuinely need input carry one of four labels -- TBP, Pending customer
confirmation, MuleSoft-owned detailed design (integration-design item), or Subject to
implementation validation.

Key design decisions (Release 1)

Ref         Decision

DEC-007     Shared Customer, Segregated Transactions --
            one shared customer profile; every transaction
            restricted to its business unit

DEC-010     Internal Requisition is a generated document
            (no custom object)

DEC-011     Test drives run on AF_TestDrive__c with manual
            scheduling -- no scheduling engine

DEC-012     AF_InvoiceSummary__c is the payment-
            tracking summary -- never the legal invoice

         9
DEC-013  (Keyloop remains legal invoice creator/source)
DEC-014
DEC-015  Six custom objects complete the retail lifecycle:
DEC-016  Vehicle Reservation, Payment, Invoice
         Summary, Credit Note, Handover, Test Drive

         Lifecycle sequence: Quote  discount
         approval  reservation  first payment 
         Sales Order document  further payments 
         balance 0  handover  delivery/Closed Won

         Payment loop: Salesforce request record 
         Finance/Cashier  values/status returned
         matched on the Salesforce reference

         No-VIN vehicles are representable pre-VIN;
         the Keyloop inventory record is created at
         Sales Order stage and the VIN linked back

Full context: Salesforce R1 Solution Overview.

How to review
1. Solution Overview -- architecture principles, ownership boundaries, and the decision

  register.
2. Data Model -- the object landscape and relationships; the field-level Data Dictionary V1.1.4

  workbook is linked there (SharePoint).
3. Process pages (3-12) -- confirm each end-to-end flow, the Salesforce behaviour, and the

  value lists against how your business units work.
4. Integration Context -- direction-level correctness of every Salesforce-side touchpoint.
5. Security & Access -- the WS-01 workshop brief: read before the security workshop.
6. Open Items & Customer Inputs -- the consolidated list of what we need from you.

How to read the reference IDs

The pages cite compact IDs so every statement traces to its source -- you can ignore them
while reading, or use them when responding:

  FUN/BUS/DAT/INT/SEC/REP/NFR -- requirement IDs from the signed Release 1 Business
  Requirements Document (V5.0).
  DEC -- Release 1 design decisions (table above).

         10
  OPN / ADB -- open questions and decision-backlog items awaiting input.
  TP / DEP -- integration touchpoints and cross-team dependencies.
  WS-01 / WS-02 -- the security and operations workshops.

01 -- Salesforce R1 Solution Overview
   Draft for customer review -- not build sign-off.

Page objective
Define the Release 1 solution architecture: principles, system ownership, the solution component
map, and the decision register that governs every detail page.
Business scope
Release 1 for the three in-scope business units -- Alfardan Automobiles, Alfardan Premier
Motors, Alfardan Sports Motors -- covering sales (lead to handover), after-sales service
interactions (cases, workshop appointments, renewals), and the shared customer master, on
Salesforce Sales/Service Cloud with Automotive Cloud.
Diagram: Diagram 02 -- Salesforce R1 Context -- see this page's attachment: 02-
salesforce-r1-context.svg .

Design assumptions
1. Keyloop (Autoline/Drive) remains the dealer management system for workshop capacity,

  vehicle inventory, vehicle ordering, payments, and the legal invoice (confirmed operating
  model).
2. All Keyloop and external system-to-system integration is delivered through the MuleSoft
  integration layer, part of the same programme delivery; Salesforce designs stop at the

                                                                                  13
  conceptual touchpoint. API contracts, payloads, retry/error handling, and status mappings are
  MuleSoft-owned detailed design, confirmed during integration design.
3. Data Cloud and Marketing Cloud are part of the wider programme delivery and are not
  detailed in this Salesforce CRM solution design page set.
4. Money never moves inside Salesforce; Finance/cashier operations stay outside (confirmed
  operating model).

Confirmed business input -- showroom and workshop value lists. Alfardan Automobiles: 6
showrooms / 4 workshops � Alfardan Premier Motors: 4 showrooms / 3 workshops � Alfardan
Sports Motors - Ferrari: 1 showroom / 1 workshop. Showroom names repeat across business
units (e.g., Alsadd, Lusail Boulevard), so showroom values are handled as business-unit-
scoped values. A showroom-to-workshop mapping is not provided and remains a new
clarification if routing requires it.

Salesforce solution design -- relationship model
  Customer: Account --< Contact (Brand Profile per brand; Related Person roles).
  Sales: Lead  (conversion)  Account + Contact + Opportunity; Opportunity --<
  OpportunityLineItem; Opportunity --< Quote --< QuoteLineItem.
  Vehicle: Product2 -- PricebookEntry; VehicleDefinition (1:1 Product2); Asset -- Vehicle (VIN
  anchor); vehicle records link to opportunities, reservations, test drives, cases, and

                                                                                  22
  appointments.
  Retail lifecycle: Opportunity --< AF_VehicleReservation__c � AF_Payment__c �
  AF_InvoiceSummary__c � AF_CreditNote__c � AF_Handover__c; AF_Payment__c 
  AF_InvoiceSummary__c (optional).
  Test drive / trade-in: Opportunity --< AF_TestDrive__c; Opportunity --< Appraisal --<
  AppraisalItem --< provider valuations / adjustments.
  Service: Account/Contact/Vehicle --< Case; Account/Contact/Vehicle --<
  ServiceAppointment.
  Supporting: Files (ContentVersion) for generated documents; Task for follow-ups;
  AF_Feedback__c (candidate) linking Case/ServiceAppointment/Account/Contact/Vehicle.

End-to-end process design
1. Capture -- a lead is created per the source table below, stamped with channel, brand, and

  campaign context.
2. Duplicate check -- on create/update, matching runs on phone, email, and QID; potential

  duplicates are flagged to the agent, who links to the existing customer rather than duplicating
  (warn-not-block).
3. Work the lead -- the agent contacts the customer within the response SLA (anchor --
  Pending customer confirmation), records interactions, and moves the status forward.
4. Qualify -- the agent completes the qualification field set (interest/vehicle context, brand,
  buying intent, contact validity) and records the outcome; disqualification requires a reason.
5. Convert -- standard conversion: Account matched or created; Brand Profile Contact created
  for the lead's brand; Opportunity created carrying brand/business-unit and source context;
  the lead is closed as converted.
6. Keyloop direction -- lead/opportunity correspondence to Keyloop sales-lead records and
  sales-activity events run through MuleSoft (MuleSoft-owned detailed design (integration-
  design item)).

Business context

Design assumptions

2. Keyloop customer references are stored on the master; whether one or many Keyloop records

Confirmed business input -- customer field governance. Group-shared identity fields: Name,
Qatar ID, Nationality, Date of birth (held on the shared Account). Business-unit-specific fields:
Contact details, Lifestyle information, Communication Preferences, Marketing Preferences
(held at business-unit/brand contact level). This split validates the Account + brand-level
Contact design: the shared Account already carries the group-shared identity, and the Brand
Profile Contacts already carry business-unit-level contact details and preferences.

Duplicate-matching rule -- Pending customer confirmation. Because contact details are
business-unit-specific, the customer must confirm whether phone/email matching runs group-
wide across business-unit contact records or only within the current business unit.
Recommendation: group-wide matching on Qatar ID + phone + email, with business-unit-
specific storage and maintenance of the values -- a match can be surfaced through the shared
Account without exposing another unit's records. This ruling affects duplicate rules, lead
conversion matching, case matching, and service-appointment customer lookup.

Roles and actors

CRM agents create/enrich the master at intake and conversion; sales consultants and service
teams consume it; edit rights on shared master fields are a WS-01 outcome.

End-to-end process design
1. Identify -- every intake (lead, case, appointment) matches on QID, phone, and email before

  creating anything.
2. Create once -- if no match, the Account is created with identification and core profile data.
3. Brand attach -- first interaction with a brand creates that brand's Brand Profile Contact (one

  per brand per Account, enforced by design) with brand-level consent.
4. Related persons -- drivers/spouses/representatives are captured as Related Person

  Contacts with their role; they can book service and appear on transactions without owning
  the profile.
5. Enrich, never duplicate -- later interactions update the shared profile under the edit model
  decided at WS-01.

Confirmed business input -- discount authority matrix based on total quotation discount,
thresholds inclusive:

  Sales Executives: up to and including 2%
  Showroom Managers / Showroom Supervisors: up to and including 3%
  Sales Managers / Brand Managers: up to and including 5%
  General Managers: up to and including 7%
  CEO: above 7%

Applies to all in-scope business units and brands for Release 1 as a working assumption
because no business-unit-specific variation was provided. Approval mechanics -- delegation,
absence cover, self-approval, exception handling, reassignment, and the final Salesforce
approval-process configuration -- remain TBP.

Roles and actors

Sales consultant (quotes, requests payments), approvers per the confirmed discount authority
matrix (approval mechanics TBP), Finance/Cashier (processes money in Keyloop -- outside
Salesforce), Sales Manager (reservation approvals).

End-to-end process design
1. Quote -- consultant builds the quotation from the selected vehicle: vehicle line,

  accessories/packages/tint/upsell lines, and the trade-in negative line where applicable;
  Customer and Bank quotations share the structure; conditional VIN by stock status with
  reissue on arrival.
2. Discount approval -- any discount routes for approval under the confirmed discount
  authority matrix (above); whether routing is single-step to the covering tier or multi-level
  escalation is part of the approval mechanics (TBP); approvers work an approval list with bulk
  actions; the quotation document is generated after approval.
3. Reserve -- reservation created against the vehicle: deposit evaluated against the matrix
  (TBP); three routing scenarios (at/above threshold  auto-flow; below threshold  manager

                                                                                  48
  approval; beyond-3-day/VIP no-deposit  approval); Salesforce calls Keyloop through
  MuleSoft to hold the vehicle and stores the confirmation reference; 3-day (no-deposit) / 7-
  day (deposit) contract types; extensions always manager-approved.
4. First payment/deposit -- consultant creates the payment request; an email/request goes to
  Finance/Cashier with the Salesforce payment reference; the cashier processes the payment
  in Keyloop; values/status return and match on the reference; the reservation contract
  generates once Paid/Verified (except the 3-day no-deposit path), after the required-
  documents check.
5. Sales Order document -- produced after the first payment/deposit; blocked for non-
  stock/on-order/in-transit vehicles until permitted; the Sales Transaction Summary generates
  in parallel at payment confirmation; special-order brands may require ordering/planning
  approval before downpayment (sequence -- Pending customer confirmation).
6. Further payments -- same loop; the Invoice Summary accumulates paid amount and
  outstanding balance against the quote total, and mirrors the Keyloop invoice status (Unpaid /
  Partially Paid / Fully Paid) with a mismatch flag.
7. Gate -- when balance = 0, the handover process may start (next page).

Salesforce solution design

Quote / QuoteLineItem -- quotation type; numeric discount + derived %; line model via
AF_LineItemType__c (vehicle / accessory / package / tint / upsell / trade-in-deduction); required
linkage to the opportunity and vehicle context. Validation intent: discount cannot bypass
approval; trade-in line must trace to an accepted appraisal.

AF_VehicleReservation__c -- statuses Requested / Pending Approval / Reserved / Expired /
Converted / Cancelled; contract type (3-day/7-day); Keyloop hold confirmation/reference;
required-documents check (Quotation, Payment Receipt where deposit, Customer ID, Approval
reference, Vehicle stock/VIN, Trade-In appraisal -- final list Pending customer confirmation);
expiry reminders on a configurable cadence; Expired/Cancelled releases the Keyloop hold.

AF_Payment__c -- amount, method, Salesforce payment reference (the external matching
key), Keyloop payment reference, proof/receipt reference, integration status, links to
opportunity/customer and (optionally) the Invoice Summary. Receipt handling and cashier
verification steps -- TBP.

AF_InvoiceSummary__c -- expected (quote) total, Keyloop invoice total, paid amount,
outstanding balance, status (Unpaid/Partially Paid/Fully Paid), legal-invoice flag = No, expected-
vs-Keyloop mismatch flag; payments as a related list (optional relationship -- deposits can
precede the invoice). Paid/balance derivations -- Subject to implementation validation.

                                                                                  49
Sales Order -- a generated document on the opportunity (AF_SOStatus__c tracks its state);
never sent to the manufacturer; vehicle ordering stays with ordering/planning in Keyloop.

Data design
Money facts are records (payments), position is a summary (Invoice Summary), and paper is
Files (quotation, contract, transaction summary, Sales Order) -- each generated document
attaches to the opportunity.

Roles and actors

Sales consultant (schedules/executes test drives, captures trade-in details), Used Car Team
(valuations), approvers per the valuation matrix (TBP).

End-to-end process design

Test drive

1. Need identified at Explore (creation trigger context shared with trade-in -- Pending customer
  confirmation).

2. Consultant manually captures date, time, and location; optionally assigns vehicle and
  consultant.

3. Test drive executes; result recorded: Completed  product feedback (sales) mandatory +
  CRM experience feedback; Refused  remarks mandatory.

4. Outcome feeds the opportunity gate. Whether booked/completed events are sent to Keyloop
  is an open question (OPN-047 -- Pending customer confirmation), as is a customer self-
  booking channel.

Trade-in

1. Trade-in initiated (automatic at Explore vs consultant-initiated -- Pending customer
  confirmation).

2. Vehicle details captured (make/model/year/VIN/mileage/condition set) plus 360� images and
  documents as Files.

3. Appraisal created; one or more valuations recorded (multiple evaluations supported); optional
  adjustments.

4. Valuation approved per the matrix (TBP); the accepted value (with validity) locks.

                                                                                  57
5. Customer decision recorded: Accepted, Refused, or Pending Customer Decision; Refused
  requires a mandatory refusal reason.

6. On Accepted, the value lands as the negative quotation line and may be applied as deposit.

Salesforce solution design

AF_TestDrive__c key fields -- auto number; lookups: Opportunity, Account, Contact, Vehicle,
Vehicle Definition, Product; Scheduled Date/Time (manual); Location/Showroom (value list
Pending customer confirmation); Assigned Consultant; Test Drive Status; Result
(Completed/Refused); Refused Remarks (mandatory on Refused -- validation); Product
Feedback (mandatory on Completed -- validation); CRM Experience Feedback; stage-gate flag
(Subject to implementation validation); Keyloop-visibility fields (dormant unless OPN-047
confirms).

Test-drive scheduling LWC (calendar view) -- TD-2

  Component: custom LWC placed on the AF_TestDrive__c record page (Lightning App
  Builder); presents a calendar/day-grid in place of the plain date/time field entry.
  Behaviour: once a Vehicle is selected on the record, an Apex controller
  ( @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true) , read-only) queries existing AF_TestDrive__c records
  for that vehicle (excluding Cancelled/Refused) and renders them on the calendar so the
  consultant sees what's already booked for that car.
  Double-booking warning: the LWC checks the selected date/time against the vehicle's
  existing bookings and triggers a visible warning wherever a double booking is detected (an
  overlapping date/time for that vehicle); the warning is non-blocking -- consistent with the
  platform's warn-not-block pattern (LM-2) -- the consultant can still proceed and save.
  Manual scheduling preserved: the consultant still freely picks the date/time -- the calendar
  is a visual aid over existing bookings plus the double-booking warning above, not a
  booking/availability engine; there is no hard, server-side block on saving an overlapping slot.
  Fields written: unchanged -- Scheduled Date/Time, Location/Showroom, Assigned
  Consultant -- the LWC only changes the input experience for date/time.
  No new objects/fields required -- reads existing AF_TestDrive__c records via the Vehicle
  lookup already on the object.

Reschedule flow -- TD-3

  Trigger: the consultant reschedules an existing test drive via a "Reschedule" action from the
  scheduling LWC (TD-2) or the record itself.
  Record model: rescheduling does not edit the existing record's date/time -- it clones it into a
  new child AF_TestDrive__c with the new Scheduled Date/Time (and Location, if changed),

                                                                                  58
  carrying over Opportunity, Account, Contact, Vehicle, Vehicle Definition, Product, and
  Assigned Consultant from the original. The new record's Test Drive Status is set to
  Confirmed.
  Original record: the parent record's Test Drive Status is set to Postponed; its Scheduled
  Date/Time, Result, and Refused Remarks are left untouched -- never overwritten. A
  Postponed record has no Result (it never executed).
  Linkage: new lookup field Rescheduled From ( AF_RescheduledFrom__c , self-lookup to
  AF_TestDrive__c) on the child, pointing to the parent; the parent's related list surfaces every
  record it was rescheduled into -- a full audit trail even across multiple reschedules (chain of
  records).
  Double-booking warning (TD-2) still applies to the new slot before the child record is
  created.
  Status model extension: Test Drive Status now includes at minimum Confirmed and
  Postponed; the full picklist (e.g. whether a separate "Scheduled" value remains for the first-
  ever booking) -- TBP at build.

Appraisal set -- standard objects: Appraisal (header, links the opportunity), AppraisalItem
(vehicle details), provider valuations (internal Used-Car-team fit -- Subject to implementation
validation), optional adjustments; accepted value + validity drive the quotation line. New fields
on Appraisal -- Customer Decision (Accepted/Refused/Pending Customer Decision) and
Refusal Reason (mandatory on Refused) -- gate release of the value into the quotation line.

Validations (design intent) -- refused remarks mandatory on Refused; product feedback
mandatory on Completed (not required for Refused or Postponed); trade-in negative line
requires an approved appraisal and Customer Decision = Accepted; refusal reason mandatory
on Refused; appraisal edits after acceptance controlled.

Data design

Trade-in vehicle detail set per DAT-018; images/documents as Files on the appraisal; test-drive
feedback retained on the record for reporting. The scheduling LWC (TD-2) reads existing
AF_TestDrive__c records scoped by the Vehicle lookup already on the object -- no new fields or
objects are introduced for the calendar view. Rescheduling (TD-3) introduces one new self-
lookup field on AF_TestDrive__c (Rescheduled From) to preserve the parentchild reschedule
chain; no new object.

Integration design

Sales consultant (runs the handover), customer (signs in person -- signing method Pending

End-to-end process design

Handover & delivery

1. Gate: Invoice Summary balance = 0.
2. Checklist: date, time, location, and required items captured on the handover record.
3. Documents: the five agreements generate in their sequence (each physically signed in

  person; regeneration protected against duplication); Traffic and Insurance forms are
  uploaded; the Delivery Note generates last once the delivery schedule is confirmed.
4. Delivery: vehicle handed over; customer sign-off recorded; Sales Order status  Delivered
  on checklist completion; a CRM experience follow-up task is created two days after delivery.

                      73
5. Close: Closed Won when handover completion and the Keyloop/delivery status confirmation
  are both in place (status names TBP).

Cancellation & credit note

1. Cancellation requires reason + evidence + management approval (matrix Pending customer
  confirmation).

2. Salesforce creates the credit-note request linked to the invoice summary/opportunity; the
  request goes to Keyloop/Finance; refund or credit retention follows finance policy (the
  customer may retain funds as credit).

3. Salesforce tracks the outcome; records are fully retained -- deletion is prohibited; the
  opportunity follows the Closed Lost path where applicable.

Salesforce solution design

AF_Handover__c fields -- date/time/location; checklist items; five agreement completion flags;
Traffic Form + Insurance Form upload references; Delivery Note flag; link to opportunity/invoice
summary. Checklist content details -- TBP.

AF_CreditNote__c fields -- linked invoice summary/opportunity/payment context; reason +
evidence reference; request status and Keyloop/Finance outcome; processed references.

Validation intent: handover cannot start below balance 0; Delivery Note cannot generate before
delivery-schedule confirmation; cancellation requires approval + reason; no record deletion.

Data design
All generated documents and uploads live as Files on the handover/opportunity; retention is total
(audit requirement).

                79
Salesforce solution design

Status model -- New  Working  Waiting for Customer  Escalated  Closed; every
transition audited (audit is a stated requirement).

SLA design -- first response 4 business hours; resolution 48-72 business hours by type
(current design anchors -- final thresholds and escalation matrix pending customer
confirmation); the clock pauses in Waiting for Customer; escalation on breach or manual trigger.
All timings respect the working calendar (values Pending customer confirmation).

Key fields -- channel, brand/business-unit identity, type + subtype, match keys
(QID/VIN/email/phone), Keyloop case reference, escalation flag, pause tracking.

Validation intent -- closure requires a resolution summary; reopen rules per policy;
classification mandatory before routing.

Routing -- placeholder: business-unit-aware queues and assignment are WS-01 outcomes; no
cross-unit case visibility (SEC-011).

WhatsApp chatbot journeys (Salesforce Messaging for WhatsApp / Salesforce chatbot) --
returning customers are recognised by their registered phone number with profile context
surfaced to the session (unknown customers are greeted generically); English/Arabic language
selection at session start persists for the session; every chatbot session creates a Case linked to
the business-unit-specific queue and WhatsApp channel with the conversation transcript
appended in real time. Supported journeys: service appointment inquiry (vehicle identification
 service type  Keyloop-sourced slot selection  appointment + self-served closure +
confirmation; no-slots offers live-agent escalation), service status follow-up, contact-us /
showroom information per business unit (self-service closure note), and transfer to a live
CRM agent (on explicit request, no slots, three unrecognised inputs, undeterminable status, or
outside working hours) routing the case to the business-unit queue with the full transcript and
customer Account context presented to the agent. A WhatsApp case converts to a Lead when
the conversation becomes a genuine sales inquiry (quick-action mapping -- design input).
Chatbot scripts, decision tree, and English/Arabic copy are business/build inputs; Einstein Bot
Arabic language pack configuration and QA are in build scope.

Case interactions as related activity; attachments as Files; feedback (candidate object) linking
case/customer/vehicle.

  conditional short-notice reminder; all sends respect the working calendar and communication
  windows.
6. Track -- workshop statuses sync inbound through the six-status model; customer-visible
  updates per your notification policy.
7. No-show -- flagged appointments get a manual check before any message.
8. Follow up & renew -- post-service follow-up plus the candidate feedback record;
  renewal/expiry follow-ups driven by Keyloop-sourced dates: service due, warranty, service
  contracts, service packages, insurance, financial-services products -- call lists one month
  pre-expiry, a warranty-renewal task 60 days pre-expiry with the selling-representative
  assignment chain, and declined-renewal sends at 7 and 3 days pre-expiry via the preferred
  channel.

Salesforce solution design

Key fields -- Keyloop appointment reference; maintenance shop (stored on the appointment);
advisor; VIN/vehicle; service type; channel; status (six-status model); no-show flag; follow-up

                                                                                  87
links.

Validation intent -- booking requires the Keyloop confirmation reference; VIN required; no
Salesforce-side slot invention.

Automation (design intent) -- reminder scheduling per the cadence; renewal call-list
generation from Keyloop-sourced dates; assignment chain for warranty renewals (original
selling representative  Sales Manager redistribution  Showroom Manager escalation).

Data design
Booking data set: VIN, contact details, relationship to owner, service type, preferred branch,
preferred slot; expiry data set: service due/last service, warranty, service contract, package,
insurance dates (Keyloop-sourced).

Confirmed business input -- workshop/maintenance-shop values per business unit:
Alfardan Automobiles: Industrial Area, Lusail Boulevard, Jery Al Samur, Industrial Area
(Motorcycles) � Alfardan Premier Motors: Industrial Area, Lusail Boulevard, Jery Al Samur �
Alfardan Sports Motors - Ferrari: Pearl. A showroom-to-workshop mapping is not provided and
is not assumed.

What is deliberately NOT selected (WS-01 outcomes)
Organisation-wide defaults � roles and role hierarchy � sharing rules � restriction rules � public
groups � queues � permission sets � field-level security � report folders. Nothing on any page
implies one of these choices.

WS-01 input list (what the workshop needs from you)
1. Brand  business-unit map.
2. Roles/personas per business unit and department (sales, after-sales, CRM, management) --

  personas received (see below); department mapping and access scopes still needed.
3. Manager and executive visibility expectations -- same-unit and cross-unit.
4. Queue model for leads and cases (per unit, per team, or hybrid).
5. Edit permissions on the shared customer master (who may change shared fields).

                                                                                  99
6. Reporting and export governance (who reports/exports across which scope).
7. Integration-user scope (what integration processes may read/write).

WS-01 inputs received

Confirmed business input received ahead of the workshop:

  28 user personas provided with business-unit assignment and a cross-business-unit access
  flag.
  Only the Chief Sales Officer, Chief Executive Officer, and System Admin are flagged cross-
  business-unit; every operational persona is single-unit-scoped.
  This supports the Shared Customer, Segregated Transactions principle (DEC-007).
  Roles, profiles, permission sets, sharing rules, queues, field-level security, report/export
  governance, and integration-user scope remain WS-01 outcomes -- the persona input
  informs the workshop; it does not select any mechanism.

Decision options to be reviewed at WS-01

Presented for discussion -- none is selected:

  Baseline visibility posture: restrictive baseline with explicit grants vs a more open baseline
  with restrictions -- evaluated per object family.
  Business-unit enforcement families: ownership-based separation, criteria-based sharing,
  and restriction-based approaches -- evaluated against the DEC-007 zones and your
  manager-visibility expectations.
  Queue models: per-business-unit queues vs team-level queues vs skill/brand hybrids for
  leads and cases.
  Reporting scopes: per-unit folders with managed roll-ups vs centrally governed dashboards
  with row-level scoping.
  Integration user: single integration identity vs per-flow identities, with least-privilege
  scoping.

Recent Build Updates (August 2026):

    Key Changes Since Initial Design:

      Lead Convert Mechanism: Switched from custom flow AF_FL_Lead_Convert to
      standard Salesforce Convert Lead with LeadConvertSettings field mappings. Person
      Account conversion enabled via blank Company field + proper default record type
      configuration.
      Additional Lead Fields: Added AF_Nationality__c and AF_DateOfBirth__c for
      proper Person Account conversion; added AF_CampaignName__c and
       AF_SLABreachLevel__c to layout for complete visibility.
      SLA Automation Fixes: AF_FL_Lead_OwnerAssignment_SLA fixed to fire on Lead
      creation regardless of owner type (previously only User-owned); added
       AF_FL_Lead_StampQualification flow for qualification timestamping; Business
      Hours Friday exclusion fixed with explicit null values.
      Round Robin Assignment: Added AF_FL_Lead_RoundRobinAssignment flow for
      BU-level lead distribution.
      Layout Updates: Company field changed from Required to Edit to enable Person
      Account conversion; removed standard "New Case" quick action (Cases out of scope).

    As-built correction -- 17 Aug 2026. The tables throughout this page (flow catalogue,
    status lifecycle, queue descriptions) describe the original design, which has drifted from
    what was actually built in several places. Rather than silently rewriting every table, the
    corrections are consolidated here -- treat any reference below to a flow/field NOT in this
    list as historical design intent, not current build state.

    Flows that do not exist (planned in the original catalogue, never built under these names):
    AF_FL_Lead_DigitalIntake , AF_FL_Lead_StampAssignment ,
    AF_FL_Lead_AssignmentNotify , AF_FL_Lead_StampFirstContact ,
    AF_FL_Lead_SetSLATargets , AF_FL_Lead_SLABackstop ,
    AF_FL_Lead_Convert (this one WAS built, then deliberately deleted 13 Aug 2026 -- see
    below).

                 119
The actual as-built Lead flow catalogue:

   AF_FL_Lead_DefaultFields -- before-save, sets Brand/City/Country defaults on
  create.
   AF_FL_Lead_DeriveBusinessUnit / AF_FL_Sub_DeriveBusinessUnit --
  derives Business Unit from Brand (FerrariSports Motors, Rolls-RoyceAutomobiles;
  other brandsUNMAPPED pending the brand matrix).
   AF_FL_Lead_OwnerAssignment_SLA -- after-save, fires on any create (User- or
  Queue-owned) and calls AF_BusinessHoursService (Apex) to compute and stamp
  all 3 SLA target fields -- this is the flow that does what the catalogue's separate
  "StampAssignment"/"SetSLATargets" entries described, combined into one.
   AF_FL_Lead_ShortWindowGuard -- before-save, create-only, gated on
   AF_LeadChannel__c = "Web" (a field populated by the future digital-integration
  only), flags a rapid re-submission as AF_IsSuppressedDuplicate__c = true .
   AF_FL_Lead_SLAEscalation -- record-triggered with 3 scheduled paths (15 min / 1
  hour / 3 day), anchored to the real SLA target fields (see corrected field names below).
  This is what the catalogue's "SLAEscalation" + "SLABackstop" entries collapse into --
  there is no separate daily-batch backstop flow live today.
   AF_FL_Lead_StampQualification -- before-save fast field update, stamps
   AF_QualifiedDate__c / AF_QualifiedBy__c when Status becomes Qualified.
   AF_FL_Lead_Reactivate -- Quick Action screen flow, clears disqualification fields
  and restarts qualification (ALF-LM-07).
   AF_FL_Lead_RoundRobinAssignment -- after-save on create, reassigns a newly
  Queue-routed Lead to an individual Sales Rep via round-robin rotation (installed as the
   RoundRobinAssigner unmanaged package -- Apex class roundRobinAssigner
  + custom object RoundRobin__c tracking the rotation pointer, patched post-install to
  exclude nested Public Groups from the rotation pool and guard against an empty
  candidate pool). Sends a Custom Notification to the new owner. This closes ALF-LM-
  04's "each agent sees only their own leads" requirement -- Leads land in a BU queue
  via the Assignment Rule first, then this flow immediately reassigns to a real person.
   AF_FL_Lead_PublishChange -- publishes AF_LeadChange__e on meaningful
  field changes, for MuleSoft to subscribe to.

Corrected field names -- the SLA target fields are
AF_SLA_Target_FirstContact__c / AF_SLA_Target_SecondCheckpoint__c /
AF_SLA_Target_FinalDisposition__c (not
_15Min__c / _1Hour__c / _3Day__c ). AF_BuyingIntent__c referenced in the Data

                                                                          120
Design table below does not exist -- the qualification field set is
AF_ContactValidity__c , Rating , and AF_VehicleOfInterest__c .

Lead Convert (ALF-LM-08) -- the custom AF_FL_Lead_Convert screen flow
referenced throughout the tables below (status lifecycle step 5, the queue table's
conflicting-match note, etc.) was built, then deliberately retired 13 Aug 2026 per explicit
customer preference for the standard Salesforce Convert Lead action instead. Conversion
now uses standard Convert with LeadConvertSettings field mappings
(LeadAccount/Opportunity); Person Account creation is driven by leaving Company
blank plus a default Person Account record type on the Admin profile. The QID-vs-
phone/email conflicting-match detection and AF_DataQualityFlag__c stamping
described in the original design were never built into the custom flow before it was retired,
and standard Convert does not replicate that logic -- this remains a genuine, real gap
against the original design (see the Account and Contact Management page for the fuller
writeup).

Second reversal -- 19-20 Aug 2026 (supersedes the Person Account / standard
Convert claims in the "Key Changes Since Initial Design" panel above, the "As-built
correction -- 17 Aug 2026" panel above, the LM-4 decision row, and the ALF-LM-08
section below). Verified live in ALFardan DEV 21 Aug 2026: 0 Person Account records,
27 Business_Account records; the custom "Person_Account" record type is now
inactive.

Lead Convert is no longer standard Salesforce Convert with LeadConvertSettings ,
and it does not create a Person Account. A new custom Screen Flow,
AF_FL_Lead_ConvertScreen (Active), now replaces the standard Convert action
entirely. It calls a new invocable Apex method,
AF_LeadConversionService.convertLeads ("Convert Lead (Match-First Business
Account)"), which:

  Matches an existing Business Account by QID, Phone, or Email (sentinel-value pattern
  to avoid blank-field false positives, the same technique used in
   AF_FL_Lead_ShortWindowGuard ); creates a new Business Account only if no match
  is found. The Business_Account record type is always used explicitly -- Person
  Account is never referenced.
  Creates or reuses a Brand Profile Contact for the lead's brand (one per brand per
  Account, same rule as originally designed).

                                                                          121
     Calls Database.convertLead() pointed at those pre-created Account/Contact
     records, so the platform's native
      IsConverted / ConvertedAccountId / ConvertedContactId / ConvertedOppor
      tunityId are set correctly -- unlike the old AF_FL_Lead_Convert flow (retired 13
     Aug), which could not touch these fields and relied on the custom
      AF_ConvertedAccount__c / AF_ConvertedOpportunity__c lookups instead.
     Those two custom lookup fields still exist on Lead but nothing in the current build writes
     to them any more -- likely dead, not confirmed removed.

   The RECORD_IN_USE_BY_WORKFLOW blocker is resolved.
   AF_FL_Lead_SLAEscalation 's pending scheduled-path actions (15 min/1 hr/3 day)
   were blocking Database.convertLead() . The fix, implemented in
   AF_LeadConversionService.clearPendingSlaScheduledActions : briefly
   reassign the Lead to its BU queue and back to the real owner within the same convert
   transaction, which cancels the pending scheduled actions (they stop matching the
   triggering flow's entry criteria) without the Lead ever visibly sitting on a queue.

   The post-convert screen renders a new LWC, afLeadConvertSummary (backed by the
   Aura-enabled AF_LeadConversionSummaryController ), showing the created/linked
   Account/Contact/Opportunity as SLDS-style cards -- DisplayText rich text was tried first
   and rejected because Salesforce's HTML sanitizer strips border/border-radius styling.

   The standard LeadConvertSettings Lead-to-Opportunity field mapping (Brand,
   Business Unit, Source of Business, Showroom, test-drive fields) is still deployed and still
   applies, since Database.convertLead() uses the same underlying engine as standard
   Convert. It does not map to Account --
   AF_Nationality__c / AF_DateOfBirth__c /QID/etc. are copied onto the new
   Account explicitly in AF_LeadConversionService.resolveAccount() , not via
   LeadConvertSettings .

LFRDN-118 -- Lead Management (Epic) � Low-Level Design ticket: LFRDN-298 -- Lead
Management LLD

Design Assumptions:

  Digital-form leads are created through MuleSoft-delivered REST calls, not the platform's
  native Web-to-Lead feature -- one intake pattern, channel-stamped per form, per decision
  LM-1.
  Keyloop-originated leads arrive through MuleSoft; Cisco telephony integrates via Salesforce
  CTI (Open CTI) directly, not through MuleSoft.
  A WhatsApp conversation converts to a Lead only when a genuine sales inquiry emerges
  from an existing Case -- it is not a raw lead-intake channel.
  Response SLA anchors, the qualification field set, and the final Lead Status value set are still
  pending customer confirmation (see Open Items).
  Object used: standard Lead -- no custom object introduced. All new fields use the AF_
  prefix. One invocable Apex class is used (business-hours SLA calculation, ALF-LM-06) -- the
  only Apex in this workstream; everything else is declarative (Flow, Validation Rules, native
  Duplicate Management, Assignment Rules).

Why not Entitlement Processes and Milestones for Lead SLA?

Entitlements and Milestones are the Salesforce-native SLA engine and should win over hand-
built automation wherever they fit -- business-hours-aware countdowns, a violation engine,

                                                                                 125
time-triggered actions, and standard milestone reporting, all declaratively. The reason they
cannot be used here is narrow: an Entitlement Process can only be applied to Case, Work
Order, or Work Order Line Item -- there is no Entitlement lookup on Lead, and no supported
way to run a milestone clock on it. This is a platform boundary, not a preference.

Option                 Business-hours aware Works on Lead        Verdict

Entitlement Process +  Yes, natively via the No -- Case / Work   Unavailable -- the
Milestones             Entitlement's Business Order / WOLI only  deciding factor
                       Hours
                                                                 Retired -- Salesforce
Workflow Rule time- No -- calendar time Yes                      has ended support for
triggers                                                         new Workflow Rules

Process Builder        No -- calendar time Yes                   Retired -- same
scheduled actions                                                deprecation path

Flow scheduled paths No -- 15 minutes       Yes                  Fails the working-
                                                                 calendar requirement
offset from a creation means 15 wall-clock                       on its own

timestamp              minutes                                   Works, but scans the
                                                                 whole object on a
Polling Scheduled Only if targets are pre- Yes                   timer and fires up to 15
Flow every 15 minutes computed                                   minutes late

Flow scheduled paths Yes -- the target      Yes                  Selected

anchored to a pre- datetime already has

computed business- the calendar applied

hours target field

Salesforce exposes business-hours arithmetic only through the Apex BusinessHours class
( BusinessHours.add() ), which has no declarative equivalent. A single invocable Apex class
computes the three SLA deadlines once, at assignment, with the working calendar applied;
those datetimes are stored on the record and the record-triggered flow's scheduled paths are
anchored directly to them. Each escalation fires at its exact deadline via the platform's own
async scheduler -- nothing polls -- and because a scheduled path anchored to a field is
automatically rescheduled when that field changes, a reassignment simply moves the deadline
with no cleanup logic needed. Recommendation for Case Management (LFRDN-133/134): use

                                                                                 126
Entitlement Processes and Milestones there instead -- HLD Case SLA requires a pause-while-
waiting-for-customer behaviour that Milestones support natively and Flow does not; both
designs should consume the same Business Hours records so one working-calendar source
drives every SLA clock.

Story-by-Story Build Detail

ALF-LM-01 -- Manual Lead Creation from Supported Channels

As a CRM user, I should be able to create leads from supported manual channels so that
prospects can be tracked and qualified.

What the system must do: Allow manual lead creation from Cisco CTI/phone, WhatsApp,
events, referrals and walk-ins. Enforce a minimum mandatory field set, capture a three-level
source taxonomy (Channel  Medium  Source), auto-capture the operating user's brand,
default the address to Doha/Qatar, and never block creation for a missing email or missing test-
drive detail.

Open items: final mandatory field matrix (pending customer confirmation); complete brand list
and per-brand model lists (TBP); walk-in definition and routing to Retail Sales (pending validation
with stakeholders).

ALF-LM-02 -- Automated Lead Creation from Digital Sources

As a system, I should create leads automatically from supported digital sources so that inbound
demand enters the CRM process immediately.

What the system must do: Create leads automatically from website forms, Meta landing pages,
Marketing Cloud journeys and online test-drive forms; send the customer an acknowledgement;
stamp channel/medium/source per the attribution matrix; and route straight into the CRM queue
with a team notification -- all without manual intervention. Decision LM-1 applies: platform Web-
to-Lead is not used -- all digital intake arrives through MuleSoft as authenticated REST calls.

Needs confirmation. The BRD requires leads to be stamped "according to the matrix shared for
Channel, Medium, and Source" -- but no such matrix has been provided. Do not build the three
picklists as independent, unconstrained fields -- an unconstrained combination (e.g. Channel =
Walk-in with Source = Google) would corrupt the attribution reporting this story exists to enable.
Once the matrix is received, implement Medium and Source as picklists dependent on Channel.

  does not set OwnerId.

Open items: number and inventory of website forms (TBP); acknowledgement template content
and sender identity (TBP); whether the acknowledgement is sent from Salesforce or Marketing
Cloud (pending).

ALF-LM-03 -- Lead Duplicate Detection at Intake

As a system, I should check lead duplicates at intake so that the team can reduce duplicate
customer records without blocking valid business activity.

What the system must do: Check every incoming lead against existing Lead and
Account/Contact records on phone, email and QID. Warn and surface the matched record --
never broadly block. Additionally support a configurable short-window block for digital leads to
stop rapid re-submission. Two different behaviours, deliberately: human-created leads get a soft
warning; machine-created digital leads get a hard short-window suppression, implemented as
two separate components so neither can accidentally change the other's behaviour.

Component           Type            Status                                            What it does
                                    New
AF_DuplicateWindow  Custom Setting                                                    Makes the
Minutes__c          (hierarchy)                                                       suppression window
                                                                                      admin-configurable
AF_IsSuppressedDupli Checkbox on Lead New                                             without a deployment
cate__c
                                                                                      Marks a suppressed
                                                                                      re-submission for
                                                                                      reporting rather than
                                                                                      deleting data

Step-by-step:

                                                                                 138
1. Build matching rules with three rule entries each (Phone, Email, QID) so a match on any one
  key triggers. Exact matching on QID and Email; Phone uses Exact with platform normalisation.

2. Extend, don't parallel-build, the duplicate rules. PROD already has active standard duplicate
  rules for Lead, Account and Contact (name/phone/email, Allow+Alert). Add the QID matching
  rule entry to those existing rules rather than deploying new rules alongside them -- two active
  duplicate rules firing independently on the same object would give an agent two separate
  alerts for one match. Keep both at Allow with Alert and Report on Create and Edit; do not
  enable "Bypass sharing rules".

3. Write actionable alert text: "A customer with this phone/QID already exists. Open the matched
  record and link to it instead of creating a duplicate."

4. Add the standard Potential Duplicates component to the Lead Lightning record page.
5. Build AF_FL_Lead_ShortWindowGuard -- before-save, create only, entry condition Channel =

  "Web": look up Lead where Phone or Email matches AND CreatedDate is within the
  configured window AND not converted; if found, set AF_IsSuppressedDuplicate__c = true
  only (does not assign OwnerId). Honour an admin override permission.
6. Route suppressed leads through the assignment rule, not the flow -- assignment rules run
  after before-save flows in Salesforce's order of execution, so an OwnerId set inside a before-
  save flow would be silently overwritten the instant the assignment rule fires. The suppression
  check is instead the first, highest-priority entry in AF_AR_Lead_Routing (see ALF-LM-04).
7. Seed the custom setting with a starting value (suggest 15 minutes) pending the business
  ruling.

Open items: short-window duration and exact suppression logic (TBP with business); group-
wide vs. business-unit-scoped phone/email matching (pending -- this ruling also governs
Contact and Account matching, see the Account and Contact Management page).

ALF-LM-04 -- Lead Routing into Shared CRM Queue

As a system, I should route leads into a shared work queue so that CRM can action new
demand consistently.

What the system must do: Route every new lead -- manual or automated -- into a shared CRM
queue on creation. Let authorised agents self-assign, give supervisors a view of all pending/in-
progress leads plus manual reassignment, give each agent a personal list view of only their own
leads, and notify on both queue arrival and assignment.

ALF-LM-05 -- Lead Qualification

As a CRM user, I should qualify leads consistently so that only genuine and viable prospects
are converted to sales opportunities.

What the system must do: Require the qualification field set to be complete before
qualification; require a recorded qualification outcome before conversion is permitted; track
qualification status on the record and in reporting; and auto-log every Cisco CTI outbound call
as an activity capturing direction, duration, outcome and timestamp.

Lead Status uses the value set New � Working � Follow-up � On-Hold � Qualified � Converted �
Disqualified. This keeps the operational working states agents actually use day to day (Follow-
up / On-Hold) while adding an explicit Qualified value, which is what the conversion gate
depends on -- there is no clean way to gate conversion without a distinct qualified state.

Open items: qualification field set and minimum criteria (pending CRM leadership); Lead Status

(TBP).

ALF-LM-06 -- Lead SLA Reminders and Escalations

As a system, I should support SLA reminders and escalations for leads so that response times
and decision windows are controlled.

What the system must do: Enforce a three-tier SLA -- reminder to the agent at 15 minutes
without first contact, escalation to agent + supervisor at 1 hour, escalation to supervisor +
manager at 3 days without a final disposition. Show SLA status visually on the record and in
queue dashboards. All thresholds are calculated against the working calendar. (See "Why not
Entitlement Processes and Milestones" under Design Decisions above for the mechanism
rationale.)

Component      Type                  Status  What it does
                                     New
AF_BusinessHoursSer Apex, invocable          Single method
vice                                         addWorkingTime(start

                                             BusinessHours.add();

Step-by-step:

1. Write AF_BusinessHoursService as an @InvocableMethod accepting a list of requests (start
  datetime, amount to add, unit, business hours name) and returning computed datetimes --
  bulkified so it is safe inside a record-triggered flow processing 200 records.

2. Build AF_FL_Lead_SetSLATargets, triggered when AF_AssignedDateTime__c is set. Resolve
  the business hours name from AF_BusinessUnit__c, call the Apex action for 15 minutes / 60
  minutes / 3 working days (unit = WORKING_DAYS, not a pre-converted minute count), write
  the three targets.

3. Build AF_FL_Lead_SLAEscalation with three scheduled paths, each anchored to a target field
  with zero offset, each re-evaluating before acting:
    Path 1 -- anchor the 15-minute target; run only if first contact is still blank  notify Owner;
    set level 1.
    Path 2 -- anchor the 1-hour target; same check  notify Owner + Supervisor; set level 2.
    Path 3 -- anchor the 3-day target; run only if Status is not Converted/Disqualified  notify
    Supervisor + Manager; set level 3.

4. Add AF_FL_Lead_SLABackstop -- a daily scheduled flow catching leads past a target whose
  breach level is lower than it should be, since deploying a new version of a record-triggered
  flow discards its pending scheduled paths.

5. Resolve supervisor/manager recipients from the role hierarchy, not hard-coded users.
6. Add the SLA indicator to Lead list views and the queue dashboard.
7. No extra logic is needed for out-of-hours creation -- business-hours arithmetic automatically

  pushes the target into the next working period.

Open items: SLA clock start point -- lead creation vs. queue assignment; this LLD assumes
assignment (pending business agreement); working-hours definition per BU and the Friday/off-
day list (TBP); reminder cadence and notification channels (pending).

ALF-LM-07 -- Non-Progressing Lead Disqualification

As a CRM user, I should disqualify non-progressing leads so that reporting and future nurture
remain accurate.

What the system must do: Offer a defined reason list, require a reason before a lead can be
closed or deactivated, retain all disqualified records and their history for re-engagement, and
make them available as Marketing Cloud nurture audiences.

                                                                                 143
Component             Type          Status  What it does

Step-by-step:

2. Write AF_VR_Lead_DisqualifyReason (see Validation rule catalogue above).
3. Remove Delete on Lead from the agent permission set so disqualified leads stay queryable

  with full field history.
4. Enable Field History Tracking on Status, Owner and the disqualification fields.
5. Build the report and hand the filter definition to the Marketing Cloud workstream.
6. Add the Reactivate action -- the BRD retains disqualified leads specifically for re-engagement

  status a re-engaged customer would need a second lead created, which is the exact

  assignment would.

Open items: final disqualification reason list (TBP by business); whether reactivation should
restart the SLA clock or exempt re-engaged leads from it (business decision).

ALF-LM-08 -- Lead Conversion to Account and Opportunity

As a CRM user, I should convert qualified leads into account and opportunity records so that
sales can continue the retail process.

What the system must do: In one operation, match or create the Account, create the brand-
appropriate Contact, create the Opportunity, carry over source/notes/vehicle-of-
interest/qualification data, allow direct assignment to a Sales Rep with no intermediate handover
task, and notify that rep. Where an existing Account matches, link -- never duplicate.

                                                                                 144
Out-of-the-box Lead Convert cannot choose the Contact's record type or reuse an existing
brand Contact under a matched Account, and exactly one Brand Profile Contact per brand per
Account is required -- this was the original reasoning for wrapping the standard convert action
in a Screen Flow. As built (13 Aug 2026), the platform's standard "Convert Lead" Flow core
action turned out not to be usable at all: convertLead is not a valid
InvocableActionType in this org's Metadata API version -- confirmed by a direct deploy
attempt, not a guess -- so it cannot be called from a Flow here regardless of the Contact-reuse
requirement. AF_FL_Lead_Convert instead performs an explicit create/link: it matches or creates
the Account (Person Account, per the ratified customer-identity model -- see the Account and
Contact Management page), creates the Opportunity directly, and does not touch
Lead.IsConverted / Status = Converted at all, because setting Status to a Converted-
mapped value via plain DML also triggers Salesforce's own automatic standard-mapping
conversion as an uncontrolled side effect (would create a second, duplicate
Account/Opportunity). Two new Lead lookup fields, AF_ConvertedAccount__c and
AF_ConvertedOpportunity__c , carry the lineage instead of the standard
Lead.ConvertedOpportunityId .

Historical -- this ALF-LM-08 section describes the 13 Aug design (custom
AF_FL_Lead_Convert flow, Person Account). As of 19-20 Aug 2026 the mechanism
changed again: see the panel near the top of this page. The paragraph below (brand-
Contact-reuse under Person Account) no longer reflects the current build -- Brand Profile
Contact reuse is back, handled by AF_LeadConversionService.

One consequence of the Person Account ratification: there is no separate brand-Contact-reuse
step in the as-built flow, since a Person Account carries its own Brand/BU context directly
( AF_Brand__pc / AF_BusinessUnit__pc ) rather than through a child Contact. Contact
records (Brand Profile / Related Person) still exist for related persons and additional brand detail,
but the conversion flow itself doesn't create or search them.

Screen Flow logic, step by step (as built):

1. Get the Lead and the Person Account record type.
2. Match the Account -- a single query on Phone, PersonEmail and AF_QID__c ( filterLogic

   1 OR 2 OR 3 , not QID-first-then-phone/email as originally sequenced). Present the match
  on a Review Match screen with "Link to this existing customer" vs. "create new" -- no ranking
  or conflict detection between the three identifiers (see the known simplification noted on the
  Account and Contact Management page's ALF-LM-09 section).
3. If creating new: a New Account Details screen captures First/Last Name, Phone, Email, QID,
  defaulted from the Lead; creates the Person Account with
   AF_Brand__pc / AF_BusinessUnit__pc from the Lead.
4. Assign the Opportunity owner -- screen to pick "Assign to Me" or a named Sales
  Representative (via a Lookup screen component), with no intermediate handover task.
5. Create the Opportunity directly (StageName = Consider,
  Brand/BU/Source/LeadSource/Description carried from the Lead, owner as selected) and a
  Task notification for that owner.

                                          147
6. Update the Lead's AF_ConvertedAccount__c / AF_ConvertedOpportunity__c lookups. Status is
  left untouched -- see the design-vs-build note above.

Pre-conversion test-drive interest. A customer can flag test-drive interest on the Lead before
any Opportunity exists to hold it. The three carried-over fields above prevent that signal from
being silently dropped at conversion: when the Explore-stage flow on Opportunity creates the
Test Drive record, it pre-populates scheduled date/time/location from the carried fields if set,
rather than starting blank.

Pre-qualification deposit path. Where a customer wants to pay before full qualification:
convert to an Account first, then record the payment -- either linked to a Keyloop
inquiry/opportunity, or as an open payment against the Account pending opportunity
assignment. The payment record itself (AF_Payment__c) is owned by the Payment Collection
epic (LFRDN-127); this design's only obligation is to permit conversion for a not-yet-Qualified
lead via a bypass branch in AF_FL_Lead_Convert guarded by a reason prompt.

ALF-LM-11 -- Lead Integration Touchpoints

As a system, I should support lead-related integration touchpoints so that inbound sources and
downstream DMS needs are handled consistently.

What the system must do: Receive inbound leads from website forms and Keyloop; use
MuleSoft as the middleware for all SalesforceKeyloop flows; support bidirectional
create/update; sync every Salesforce-side lead update back to Keyloop; and log integration
events and failures for monitoring. Ownership boundary: Salesforce owns the shape (object,
fields, external IDs, change events); MuleSoft owns the movement (endpoints, payloads, retries,
error handling, status mapping).

Component          Type            Status          What it does
                   Platform Event  New

Step-by-step:

1. Add AF_KeyloopLeadRef__c and mark it Unique; hand MuleSoft the upsert pattern (PATCH by
  external ID), which creates or updates in one idempotent call.

2. Define the platform event with a minimal payload -- record ID, object, change type, business
  unit -- not a full field copy; MuleSoft calls back for detail.

3. Build the publisher flow scoped to meaningful changes (Status, Owner, qualification fields,
  contact details) so Keyloop isn't flooded by cosmetic edits.

4. Expose the failure surface -- MuleSoft writes AF_IntegrationStatus__c = Failed, the error text,
  and ticks AF_NeedsManualReview__c; build the "Integration Failures" list view for the CRM

                                   151
  supervisor.
5. Confirm the assignment-rule header requirement from ALF-LM-04 is in the integration

  contract.
6. Agree latency expectations with the MuleSoft team as an integration NFR.

Working Calendar (Business Hours)

Every Lead SLA timer respects the working calendar, and Leads arriving outside working hours
start their clock at the next working period. Fridays and off-days are excluded.

Vehicle of Interest -- Picklist on Lead

On Lead, where a caller may only say "an SUV, maybe", a lightweight picklist including a
mandatory Undecided value is the right shape -- a lookup to the standard vehicle catalogue
would force precision the conversation does not have. The conversion flow maps this picklist to

                                                                                 160
a catalogue lookup on the Opportunity where a confident match exists (see the Retail Sales
page for the Opportunity-side decision).

Lead - Security & Access Model

Author: Yassin Elseweify -- Arcsen Technologies

Object-level access, sharing, and field-level security specific to Lead. For the shared org-wide
defaults and role hierarchy that this builds on, see the Account and Contact Management page's
Security & Access Model.

Org-Wide Default & Sharing

Object               Internal OWD            Why

Lead                 Private                 Segregated transaction --

                                             access comes from queue

                                             membership and business-unit

                                             sharing rules, not from the

                                             shared-customer exception

                                             that applies to Account

Rule    Object                  Criteria     Share with       Access
                                                              Read/Write
AF_SR_Lead_<BU Lead             AF_BusinessUnit_ Matching BU
> �3
                                _c = the BU  public group

Queues               Objects                 Members
 Queue               Lead                    Matching BU public group
 AF_Q_Leads_<BU> �3  Lead                    CRM Supervisors, all BUs
 AF_Q_Leads_Review

Queue membership grants Read/Write on records the queue owns -- this is how an agent can
work an unassigned lead before accepting it. Queue access is not transitive: accepting a lead
transfers ownership to the user, at which point the BU sharing rule keeps their colleagues'
visibility intact.

    Update -- since 16 Aug 2026. Manual "accept from the queue" is no longer the typical
    path. A new flow, AF_FL_Lead_RoundRobinAssignment (after-save, on create),

                                                                                 162
immediately reassigns most new Leads from their BU queue to a rotating individual
member of that queue's public group (invocable Apex roundRobinAssigner , rotation
pointer tracked per Object+Field+Group in the new custom object RoundRobin__c ).
Suppressed duplicates always route to the Review queue's rotation. A Lead only stays
queue-owned, pending manual acceptance as described above, when its target queue
currently has no direct User members. Once round-robin assigns an owner, the BU sharing
rule above is what keeps the rest of that owner's BU colleagues able to see the record --
this row's underlying access model is unchanged, only how ownership is initially reached.

Update -- since 16 Aug 2026 (Stage 1). "Routed to the BU queue" is now typically a brief
intermediate state, not the resting point. AF_FL_Lead_RoundRobinAssignment fires
immediately after and reassigns most new Leads from the queue to a rotating individual
member of that queue's public group -- see the Security & Access Model page for the
mechanism. A Lead only stays queue-owned pending manual acceptance when its target
queue has no direct User members yet.

Update -- 21 Aug 2026 (Stage 4). This row's wording ("Account matched-or-created,
Brand Profile Contact reused-or-created") already describes the current build accurately,
but is worth flagging as verified: as of 19-20 Aug 2026, conversion runs through a new
custom screen flow ( AF_FL_Lead_ConvertScreen ) calling the invocable Apex
AF_LeadConversionService.convertLeads , which matches/creates a Business
Account (never a Person Account) and reuses/creates a Brand Profile Contact, then calls
Database.convertLead() . An earlier build iteration (13-19 Aug) instead used standard
Salesforce Convert to create a Person Account -- that iteration is no longer live. See the
Lead Management page's top correction panel for the full history.

This section will detail the Account and Contact Management Cycle and its child stories.

LFRDN-119 -- Account Management and LFRDN-120 -- Contact Management (Epics) � Low-
Level Design tickets: LFRDN-299 -- Account Management LLD, LFRDN-300 -- Contact
Management LLD

    RATIFIED 13 Aug 2026 -- Customer identity model is Person Account, not Business
    Account. The Alfardan org has Person Accounts enabled at the platform level. CM-1 below
    originally recommended proceeding with standard Business Account + Contact
    regardless, and flagged this as a decision needing an explicit customer/architect ruling
    before Account/Contact build started. That ruling has now been made, in favour of the
    platform default: Account uses the standard Person_Account Record Type (alongside
    Business_Account for any genuine company accounts), carrying identity directly
    ( AF_QID__c , AF_Nationality__c , AF_DateOfBirth__c , Salutation -- Salutation is
    standard on a Person Account, so no AF_Salutation__c custom field was needed)
    plus a primary Brand/Business-Unit context as person fields ( AF_Brand__pc ,
    AF_BusinessUnit__pc ). This was already built out extensively (data model, permission
    sets, the Lead Convert flow) before this ruling was formally recorded here, so reversing it
    now would touch nearly everything below -- the practical decision was to ratify the built
    state rather than rebuild around Business Account.

    What did not change: brand-level detail still lives on separate Contact records (Brand
    Profile / Related Person, by category -- see CM-2/CM-3), Account is still the one
    shared/open-visibility object with everything transactional segregated (DEC-007), and the
    OWD/sharing/FLS model described below applies identically to a Person Account as it
    would to a Business Account. The CM-1 table below is left in place as the original analysis
    and superseded conclusion, not deleted, since the reasoning is still sound on its own terms
    and may matter if this is ever revisited.

Design Assumptions:

  Qatar ID (QID) is the primary unique identifier on the shared Account; an open identification
  field covers non-QID documents (passport, Omani ID, etc.).
  Group-shared identity fields (Name, QID, Nationality, Date of Birth) live on the Account;
  business-unit-specific fields (contact details, lifestyle, communication and marketing
  preferences) live on the brand-level Contact.
  The standard BusinessUnit and AccountBrand objects exist in the PROD org but are
  unused (zero records) -- brand and business-unit context is modelled with a custom flow-

                                                                                 186
  maintained picklist instead, since neither standard object integrates with criteria-based
  sharing rules or dependent picklists the way a field does.
  No Account Record Types are used -- brand/BU segmentation on the shared master would
  contradict the single-profile principle (deviation already noted in the HLD). Superseded by
  the Person Account ratification above -- Account now uses Person_Account /
   Business_Account Record Types, since Person Accounts require a Record Type by
  platform design; this is orthogonal to brand/BU segmentation, which still lives on the picklist
  fields, not on the Record Type.
  Whether phone/email duplicate matching should run group-wide across business units or be
  scoped to one business unit is not yet decided (recommendation on file: group-wide
  matching on QID + phone + email, with business-unit-scoped storage of the values).

Security & sharing model

This is DEC-007 stated as configuration, not automation: one shared profile, segregated
transactions. It applies identically whether Account is a Person or Business Account. It is
deliberately built with zero Flow or Apex -- a security model implemented in Flow is a security
model that can be bypassed.
