Story-by-Story Build Detail

ALF-AC-01 (Account portion) -- Unified Customer Profile

                        203
As a business, we should maintain a unified master customer profile with brand-specific
contact records so that customer identity is centralised while communication preferences,
consent, and contact details remain independently managed per brand.

What the system must do -- Account side: Maintain one Account per customer holding
salutation, full name as shown on QID, and QID as the primary unique identifier. Enforce QID
uniqueness absolutely -- no two Accounts may share a QID.

Step-by-step:

1. Create AF_QID__c as Unique and External ID in one step -- Unique gives the hard block the
  BRD requires; External ID lets MuleSoft upsert on it.

2. Add the remaining identity fields and lay them out in an "Identification" section.
3. Write AF_VR_Account_QIDFormat (see Validation rule catalogue above). Exact Qatar ID

  format rule is TBP -- placeholder is 11 digits.
4. Set the duplicate rule to Block on QID -- the one place in this whole design where blocking is

  correct, because a duplicate QID is definitionally a data error, not a business judgement.
  Phone/email stay on Alert. Add the QID rule entry to PROD's existing standard Account
  duplicate rule rather than deploying a second, parallel rule.
5. Configure Dynamic Forms so Individual vs. Company fields render conditionally from the
  standard Type field.
6. Set OWD to Public Read/Write, not Read Only -- FLS cannot grant record-level edit access
  under a Read-Only OWD, which would make "enrich, never duplicate" impossible for any non-
  owner. Protect identity fields with FLS instead: Read-Only for all profiles, Edit granted only via
  AF_PS_Account_CoreEdit.

Acceptance criteria coverage: a duplicate QID shows a warning and prevents a second
Account -- the Unique field constraint is what actually prevents creation (hard block); the
duplicate rule supplies the warning UI. Two components, two jobs, not two blocks.

Open items: full Account field list (pending, to be provided during solution design); exact Qatar
ID format rule (TBP); Keyloop customer cardinality -- one or many Keyloop records per Account
(pending); migration approach from Keyloop into this model (out of scope here, but the
migration plan must de-duplicate and cleanse QIDs, and define how records with no QID at all
are handled, before load -- the Unique constraint will reject anything it doesn't).

ALF-LM-09 -- Account Matching and Cross-BU Visibility Control

As a system, I should support account matching and controlled visibility so that the same
customer is reused across business units without exposing transactional records unnecessarily.

                                                                                 204
What the system must do: Surface matching Accounts during lead conversion; prompt to link
rather than duplicate; make Account profile data visible across all in-scope business units; keep
Opportunities, Cases, Service Appointments and other transactional records visible only to the
originating business unit; allow Sales to create Accounts but restrict editing of core profile data
to an authorised role.

Step-by-step:

1. Set the org-wide defaults exactly as tabled above. Verify Contact is Private and not Controlled
  by Parent -- this single setting is the difference between a compliant model and a preference
  leak across brands.

2. Create the criteria-based sharing rules on AF_BusinessUnit__c for Opportunity and Contact,
  targeting the business-unit public groups.

3. Apply field-level security -- set Name/QID/Nationality/DOB to Read-Only on all profiles, then
  grant Edit through AF_PS_Account_CoreEdit only.

4. Grant Account Create to sales permission sets while leaving core-field edit withheld.
5. Test the negative case explicitly in UAT (see the acceptance test above) -- this is the

  acceptance test for the entire security model.

As-built matching mechanism (ALF-LM-08's AF_FL_Lead_Convert ): queries Account on
Phone, PersonEmail and AF_QID__c ( filterLogic 1 OR 2 OR 3 , not QID-first-then-
phone/email as originally sequenced) and presents the match on a Review Match screen with a
"link" vs. "create new" choice. Known simplification, not yet built: the QID-vs-phone/email
conflicting-match detection and AF_DataQualityFlag__c stamping described below is not
implemented in the current flow -- it always trusts whichever single query result comes back.
This is a real gap against this page's own design and should be picked up alongside the
concurrency item below.

Simultaneous conversion by two business units. If two agents in different business units
convert leads for the same new customer at the same moment, both matching queries can run
before either Account exists, both find no match, and both create one. The Unique constraint on
AF_QID__c only catches this if both agents captured a QID; a phone/email-only match race is
not caught at all. Handling: reduce the likelihood by requiring QID capture before conversion
completes wherever practical, since QID is the one matching key with a database-level
uniqueness guarantee; and keep the residual case cheap to fix by making the standard
duplicate-management merge tooling available to CRM Supervisors, so a same-day collision is a
two-minute cleanup rather than an incident.

                                                                                 205
Exception handling -- conflicting matches. One exception path is named explicitly in the HLD:
"Conflicting matches (same QID, different phone) route to a data-quality review path." What
counts as conflicting: the incoming record's QID matches an existing Account, but the
phone/email supplied do not match anything on file for that Account (or vice versa). This is
different from an ordinary "no match" -- it's a match that disagrees with itself, more likely to
indicate a data-entry error or identity fraud than a genuine new customer. Design intent (not yet
built -- see the as-built note above): extend the lead-conversion flow so that if the QID lookup
and the phone/email lookup both return a match but to different Accounts, the flow does not
silently pick one -- it sets AF_DataQualityFlag__c = true on both candidates, presents both to
the agent with the conflict explained, and requires the agent to pick one explicitly or escalate to
the AF_Q_DataQuality_Review queue (CRM Supervisor membership) rather than defaulting.

Account merge. When two Accounts are confirmed as the same customer (through the data-
quality path above, or discovered later), the resolution mechanism is standard Salesforce
Account merge -- not a custom process. Merge automatically reparents every child record
(Contacts, Opportunities, Cases, everything keyed to AccountId) from the loser to the surviving
Account, and respects field-level security on the surviving record's values. Nothing in this
design needs to change to support it. One consequence worth testing explicitly in UAT: a merge
can bring together two Brand Profile Contacts for the same brand (one from each original
Account), which the one-brand-per-account enforcement flow does not evaluate during a
merge operation (merge is a distinct DML context) -- confirm whether post-merge cleanup of a
resulting duplicate Brand Profile Contact needs to be manual or should get its own scheduled
flow.

Acceptance criteria coverage: conversion presents the matched Account and prompts to link
(lead-conversion flow); an other-BU user sees the shared profile but not that BU's transactional
records (OWD + sharing rules); a second BU creating a lead later sees the existing Account for
reuse (cross-object duplicate rule + conversion matching).

Open items: final security model and per-object sharing rules validated by IT (pending); which
role is "authorised" for core-field edit (pending); cross-BU exception access, if any (pending);
who resolves records routed to AF_Q_DataQuality_Review, and their SLA (pending); post-merge
duplicate Brand Profile Contact cleanup -- manual or automated (subject to implementation
validation); the conflicting-match / AF_DataQualityFlag__c logic described above is designed
but not yet built into AF_FL_Lead_Convert.

ALF-AC-01 (Contact portion) -- Brand-Level Contacts

...with brand-specific contact records so that communication preferences, consent, and contact
details remain independently managed per brand.

                                                                                 206
What the system must do: Support multiple Contacts under one Account, one per brand, each
holding primary email, primary phone, preferred language, preferred communication channel
and marketing opt-in. Prevent a second Contact of the same brand under the same Account.
Permit cross-brand duplication by design. Keep opt-in consent scoped strictly to its own brand.

Ruling made: two record types by category (Brand Profile / Related Person) plus AF_Brand__c
as a field -- because the two categories genuinely need different layouts and required fields,
while brands do not.

Step-by-step:

1. Create the two record types with separate page layouts: Brand Profile shows brand, consent
  and preferences; Related Person shows role and relationship, and hides consent entirely so it
  cannot be set on the wrong record.

2. Add the field set per the Object & key fields table above, with AF_Brand__c required at layout
  level on Brand Profile only.

3. Enforce one-brand-per-account via AF_FL_Contact_BrandEnforcement_Consent , a
  before-save record-triggered flow that queries sibling Contacts on the same Account with the
  same brand and category, and raises a custom error -- declarative, immediate, no storage
  cost.

4. Write AF_VR_Contact_RoleRequired (see Validation rule catalogue above).
5. Stamp consent metadata -- the same before-save flow sets AF_OptInDateTime__c whenever

  AF_MarketingOptIn__c changes to true.
6. Verify consent isolation by test, not by automation: update opt-in on the Ferrari contact,

  confirm the Rolls-Royce contact under the same Account is untouched. Isolation is structural
  -- there is deliberately no automation copying consent anywhere.

Acceptance criteria coverage: a second Contact of the same brand under an Account is
prevented with a warning (AF_FL_Contact_BrandEnforcement_Consent); updating one brand's
opt-in leaves the other brand's unchanged (structural -- consent is per-record with no rollup).

Open items: full Contact field list (pending); composition of the BU-specific field bundles --
contact details, lifestyle, communication, marketing preferences (pending); group-wide vs. BU-
scoped phone/email matching (pending -- affects the matching rule scope here, on Lead, and
on Case); the BRD's literal ask of a Contact record type per brand is still unresolved against
the category-based approach actually built -- the brand list itself is also incomplete (only
Ferrari and Rolls-Royce confirmed), so a full per-brand rebuild isn't fully specifiable yet even
if it were decided.

The object landscape, standard-vs-custom field audit, and identity/consent design decisions for
Account and Contact.

    Ratified 13 Aug 2026 -- see the Account and Contact Management page. The two
    "proceeds with Business Account + Contact regardless" statements originally in this
    section have been superseded: the build uses Person Account for the customer master
    (Account.RecordType = Person_Account), with Contact still used underneath it for Brand
    Profile / Related Person detail exactly as this page describes. Read every "Business
    Account" reference below as historical analysis, not current state.

    Second reversal -- 19-20 Aug 2026. This supersedes the panel immediately above.
    The 13 Aug ratification of Person Account did not hold. Lead Convert was rebuilt around a
    new custom flow ( AF_FL_Lead_ConvertScreen ) calling a new invocable Apex service
    ( AF_LeadConversionService.convertLeads ), which explicitly and exclusively
    targets the Business_Account record type -- it never references Person Account. Verified
    live in ALFardan DEV 21 Aug 2026: 0 Person Account records exist; 27
    Business_Account records exist. The custom Person_Account record type is now
    inactive ( IsActive = false ) -- it still exists in the org (not deleted, not confirmed
    slated for deletion), but nothing creates records against it any more. The standard,
    platform-provided "PersonAccount" record type also still exists (as it always does once
    Person Accounts are enabled) and is separately marked active, but is likewise unused --
    zero records.

    Practical effect on this page: every "Person Account" reference below (the relationship
    table, the Account field-origin audit's Salutation note, the Verification Checklist row 5, the
    Current Org Baseline "Account record types" row, and the Net Effect table) should now be
    read as historical -- describing the 13-19 Aug build iteration, not the current one. The
    current model is Business Account + Brand Profile / Related Person Contact -- i.e. the
    original pre-13-Aug design this page's own "Design Decisions" and "Considered and
    Explicitly Out of Scope" sections were written against. Practically, that means:
    AF_Salutation__c is needed again on Account (Person Account's free native
    Salutation no longer applies to the live customer master -- verify whether this field was
    actually added back, flagged as unconfirmed);

                                                                                 214
AF_Brand__pc / AF_BusinessUnit__pc (Person-Account-only fields) are dead on the
live model, with Brand/BU context living on Contact instead as originally designed; and
DOB/Nationality copy onto the Account record directly via Apex in
AF_LeadConversionService.resolveAccount() , not via any Person-Account-
specific mechanism. Not rewriting the sections below in place, per this project's standing
correction style -- this panel is the single source of truth for "which record type is current"
until a fuller pass reconciles each section individually.

Account -- Field Origin Audit

Note. Salutation exists on Contact and on Person Accounts natively -- since the ratified build
uses Person Accounts, the master profile gets Salutation for free and no AF_Salutation__c
custom field was needed (an earlier draft of this page, written against the original Business
Account assumption, called for adding one).

    21 Aug 2026: this note is now historical again -- see the reversal panel near the top of this
    page. The live customer master is Business Account, which does not get Salutation for
    free; AF_Salutation__c is referenced as a field on the new Account created by
    AF_LeadConversionService ( AF_Salutation__c = ld.Salutation in the
    Apex), confirmed live: AF_Salutation__c exists on Account and is populated on
    existing records (e.g. "Mr.") -- it was not removed when Person Account was ratified, and
    remains in active use now that Business Account is the master again.

Standard Type field carries Individual/Company. Standard
Phone/BillingAddress/ShippingAddress exist but stay largely unused since the BRD holds
contact details at brand level. New fields: AF_QID__c (Unique + External ID),

                                  216
AF_OtherIdNumber__c, AF_Nationality__c (no standard equivalent), AF_DateOfBirth__c (standard
Birthdate exists on Contact only -- keep DOB on Account per the group-shared rule and leave
Contact.Birthdate unpopulated to avoid two sources of truth), AF_KeyloopCustomerRef__c, plus
the Person-Account-only fields AF_Brand__pc / AF_BusinessUnit__pc carrying the primary
Brand/BU context directly on the person record.

Contact -- Field Origin Audit

Contact is where the most custom design is avoided, because the BRD's brand-level
requirements map onto the core contact-point and consent framework. Standard:
Salutation/FirstName/LastName, Email, four standard phone fields, AccountId (the whole Brand
Profile model rests on this -- no junction object needed; it points at the Person Account),
Birthdate (exists but deliberately unused -- DOB is group-shared on Account),
HasOptedOutOfEmail/DoNotCall/HasOptedOutOfFax (use alongside the opt-in field, since these
are what most tools honour automatically), IndividualId, ReportsToId. New:
AF_MarketingOptIn__c/AF_OptInDateTime__c,
AF_Brand__c/AF_ContactCategory__c/AF_ContactRole__c/AF_BusinessUnit__c,
AF_PreferredLanguage__c/AF_PreferredChannel__c, AF_LifestyleInfo__c.

Design Decisions -- Standard vs Custom

Identification: PartyIdentification vs. custom fields

Multiple documents per       Standard PartyIdentification  Custom AF_QID__c /
customer                                                   AF_OtherIdNumber__c
Issue/expiry dates, issuing  Yes -- unlimited, each typed  No -- two fields, two
authority                                                  documents
Hard uniqueness on QID       Yes -- standard fields        No -- would need more
                                                           custom fields
Duplicate matching rule      No -- cannot enforce "unique  Yes -- Unique field attribute,
                             across all Accounts"          database-enforced
Integration upsert key       declaratively
                             No -- matching rules cannot   Yes -- works directly
                             traverse to a child object
                             No -- not usable as an        Yes -- External ID
                             External ID on Account

                             217
Recommendation -- hybrid. Keep AF_QID__c on Account as a Unique External ID (the
uniqueness rule, duplicate matching, and MuleSoft's upsert all depend on it being a field on the
parent), and use PartyIdentification for additional documents (passport, Omani ID, driving
licence) where expiry dates and multiplicity genuinely matter, dropping AF_OtherIdNumber__c.
Confirm at WS-01.

Consent: the standard consent framework vs. AF_MarketingOptIn__c

The core platform ships a complete consent model (Individual,
ContactPointEmail/ContactPointPhone, ContactPointTypeConsent, DataUsePurpose,
CommunicationSubscription) recording consent per channel, per purpose, per contact point,
with an audit trail, natively understood by Marketing Cloud and Data Cloud. The BRD's own ask
is a single checkbox; but if the Preference Centre (channel-level consent) is in scope, adopt the
standard framework from the start -- retro-fitting consent history later has no good answer. If
deferred beyond R1, the checkbox plus AF_OptInDateTime__c is a reasonable R1 scope,
recorded as deliberate technical debt with a named migration trigger. Cross-workstream
decision required with the Marketing Cloud team.

Related persons: ContactContactRelation vs. Related Person Contacts

ContactContactRelation models both-direction roles, start/end dates, and a person existing
independently of one Account (relevant for chauffeurs/fleet drivers relating to many customers)
-- but costs an extra object and related list to teach. Recommendation -- keep the Related
Person Contact for R1. The BRD's related persons (driver, spouse, child, authorised
representative) sit under a single customer, which Contact.AccountId already models. Revisit if
fleet/corporate becomes a Release 2 requirement.

Account & Contact - Security & Access Model

Author: Yassin Elseweify -- Arcsen Technologies

The org-wide defaults, role hierarchy, and full security skeleton that Account and Contact
anchor for the whole R1 CRM core -- since Account is the one shared, cross-business-unit
object in the model. Lead and Retail Sales pages cover only their own object-specific security
detail and link back here for the shared skeleton.

Status. Org-wide defaults, roles and role hierarchy, sharing rules, restriction rules, public
groups, queues, permission sets, field-level security and report folders are WS-01
outcomes. Everything in this page is a proposal, not a decision -- a concrete, costed
starting point for WS-01 to react to. No component here should be built until WS-01 ratifies
it.

The setting most likely to be got wrong. Contact OWD defaults to "Controlled by Parent"
in a new org. With Account now Public Read/Write, leaving Contact on Controlled by
Parent would make every brand contact -- including its marketing consent, personal
phone number, and now edit access too -- open to every business unit. It must be
explicitly set to Private. This is the single highest-risk configuration item in the whole
model.

Why Account OWD is Public Read/Write rather than Read Only: field-level security cannot
grant record-level edit access -- under a Read Only OWD, a non-owner cannot edit any field on
the record regardless of FLS, which would make "enrich, never duplicate" impossible for almost
every user of a shared master. The model instead layers the two controls to their correct roles:
OWD is open because the record is deliberately shared; FLS is restrictive because specific fields
are sensitive.

Role Hierarchy

Roles grant upward visibility -- a manager sees what their subordinates own, with no sharing
rule required. The hierarchy is mirrored per business unit so managers never see across units.

1 Alfardan Group CEO                         (approves Closed Lost, discounts 3%)
2  AF_Role_GM_Automobiles
3   AF_Role_SalesManager_Automobiles
4    AF_Role_ShowroomManager_Automobiles

14      AF_Role_Marketing

15      AF_Role_IT_Admin

Sales Manager / Brand Manager sits above Showroom Manager so the discount authority
matrix (5%) resolves naturally up the chain -- see the Retail Sales page.
General Manager (7%) and CEO (>7%) complete the approval ladder.
Marketing sits outside the BU tree -- it needs cross-BU read for campaign attribution but no
transactional write. Granted by permission set, not hierarchy.
Cross-BU executive visibility is granted by adding a user to a cross-BU public group, not by
placing them above the GMs -- that would silently grant write access too.

Profiles vs. Permission Sets

Profile-light, permission-set-driven. Profiles carry only what they must -- licence, login
hours/IP, default app, and an object baseline of "nothing". Everything grantable is granted
through permission sets, so access can be added or removed per user without cloning profiles.

On the Related Person rule. Business-unit sharing keys on AF_BusinessUnit__c, which a related
person may not carry, so a Read Only default would leave such a record editable only by
whoever happened to own it. Service staff booking appointments on behalf of related persons
need to be able to correct a stale phone number -- under Read Only, a service advisor unable to
do that would create a second contact instead, reproducing exactly the duplication this model
exists to prevent. Set to Read/Write for CRM and Service, since the record carries no consent
and no commercial data.

BU

  Report data scoping is automatic -- reports respect the sharing model, so a BU user's
  pipeline report shows only their BU with no filter required.
  Dashboards use the "run as viewer" setting so one dashboard serves all BUs while showing
  each viewer only their own data. Capacity check: "run as viewer" dashboards are dynamic
  dashboards, which most editions cap at a small number per org (commonly 5-10). Confirm
  the org's actual limit before committing to one dashboard per reporting domain.
  Export is withheld from agents at the permission-set level, and enabled for senior
  management.

      ( AF_DuplicateReviewedBy__c , AF_DuplicateReviewedDate__c ), carried test

      ( AF_FU_Opp_SetApprovalApproved , AF_FU_Opp_SetApprovalRejected ) and
      email alerts ( AF_EA_Opp_ClosedLostApproved ,
       AF_EA_Opp_ClosedLostRejected ).
      Custom Notification: AF_FL_Opp_LostRejected flow now sends both Task (for
      Activity History) and Custom Notification (real-time alert) on rejection.
      New Flow: Added AF_FL_Opp_DefaultName flow for Opportunity naming.
      Fault Handling: Enhanced error handling across screen flows
      ( AF_FL_Opp_RequestClosure , AF_FL_Opp_SalesWalkIn ,
       AF_FL_Opp_ServiceWalkIn , AF_FL_Opp_AcknowledgeDuplicate ) with
       faultConnector routing to error screens and improved error messages.
      Walk-in Flow BU Gating: Sales and Service walk-in flows now include Custom
      Permission checks ( AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn , AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn ) at flow
      start to enable per-BU configuration via permission sets.
      Test Drive Data Carryover: Lead Convert settings now properly map test drive fields
      from Lead to Opportunity ( AF_InterestedInTestDrive__c 
       AF_CarriedTestDriveInterest__c , etc.).

This section will detail the Retail Sales Cycle and its child stories.

LFRDN-121 -- Retail Sales / Opportunity Management (Epic) � Low-Level Design ticket: LFRDN-
301 -- Opportunity Management LLD

    Scope note. This page covers the standard Opportunity object only -- intake paths, the
    stage model and its gates, and the lost-sale process (LFRDN-301). Retail Sales in the BRD
    is broader than Opportunity Management: Quotation, Test Drive, Reservation, Payment
    Collection, Trade-In, Sales Order and Handover are separate epics (LFRDN-122 through
    LFRDN-130) with their own LLDs. Those objects are referenced here only as dependencies
    -- the gate fields that read from them (SyncedQuoteId, AF_InvoiceBalance__c,

                                                                                 240
AF_HandoverComplete__c) are specified so every team builds against the same interface,
but their own object models are out of scope on this page.

Design Assumptions:

  Opportunity uses one shared stage model across all business units -- no Opportunity Record
  Types. Brand-specific detail is carried by a dependent sub-stage field, kept out of cross-BU
  report groupings by convention.
  The receptionist-led walk-in creation paths (Sales Receptionist, Service Receptionist) are
  configurable per business unit, not mandated everywhere. As built (13 Aug 2026): gated by a
  Custom Permission checked at the start of each screen flow (AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn /
  AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn), granted via a small permission set attached to each business
  unit's Receptionist permission set group -- not by controlling Quick Action visibility as
  originally proposed, since Quick Action exposure isn't cleanly permission-set-controllable
  declaratively. Same functional outcome: a receptionist without the permission sees a "not
  enabled for your BU" screen instead of the intake screens.
  Quote, Invoice Summary and Handover are modelled as lookup, not master-detail, children of
  Opportunity (per the HLD) -- this rules out native Roll-Up Summary fields for the three stage-
  gate fields and drives the flow-maintained-rollup pattern used throughout this page.
  This design assumes the standard SyncedQuoteId field (populated automatically when a
  Quote syncs to its Opportunity) is an acceptable proxy for "quote accepted" at the Commit
  gate; this needs confirmation from the Quotation LLD (LFRDN-122) on whether sync only
  happens on acceptance.

Story-by-Story Build Detail

ALF-RS-01 -- Opportunity Creation from All Supported Intake Paths

As a sales-facing organization, we should be able to create opportunities from all supported
intake paths so that every valid retail sales pursuit is tracked from the correct starting point.

What the system must do: Support four intake paths -- converted lead, direct sales creation,
referral, and walk-in -- with two distinct walk-in behaviours. The Sales Receptionist creates the
Opportunity and assigns it directly to a chosen Sales Rep with a notification. The Service
Receptionist creates it, captures the preferred dealership, and assigns it to that dealership's
Showroom Manager, who receives an auto-created task with a 15-minute contact window
before reassigning to a rep.

Step-by-step (as built):

1. Add the Opportunity field set and place AF_OpportunityOrigin__c as a required field, defaulted
  by each creation path.

2. Build AF_FL_Opp_SalesWalkIn as a Quick Action on the Account record page (not a
  standalone customer-search flow) -- gate on AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn, capture
  brand/showroom/Sales Rep, create the Opportunity directly under that Account, create a Task
  for the rep.

3. Build AF_FL_Opp_ServiceWalkIn the same way, gated on AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn --
  capture brand and preferred dealership, resolve that dealership's Showroom Manager via the
  role-hierarchy lookup described above, set Owner to that manager.

4. Build AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate as a single record-triggered flow (not three branches inside the
  walk-in flows) covering every Opportunity origin: on create, check for another open
  Opportunity on the same Account + Brand -- if found, set AF_PossibleDuplicate__c and notify
  the Showroom Manager (Task), flag-do-not-block; for Service Walk-in specifically, also create
  the 15-minute contact Task; on update, if OwnerId changes on a Service Walk-in Opportunity,
  notify the new owner (Task). Uses $Record__Prior.Id IsNull to tell create from update
  within one CreateAndUpdate-triggered flow.

5. The reassignment path (Showroom Manager  Sales Rep) needs no separate component --
  AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate's update branch fires on any OwnerId change to a Service Walk-in
  Opportunity.

6. Gate the receptionist paths per BU with a Custom Permission (AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn /
  AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn) checked at the start of each flow, granted via a small permission
  set attached to that BU's Receptionist permission set group -- see the Design Assumptions
  note above for why this differs from the original permission-set-controlled-Quick-Action-
  visibility proposal.

Acceptance criteria coverage: lead conversion creates and assigns the Opportunity to Sales
directly (AF_FL_Lead_Convert, see Lead Management page); walk-in Opportunity created under
the Account with the Sales Rep notified (AF_FL_Opp_SalesWalkIn + Task); receptionist path
available only to opted-in BUs (Custom Permission gate); service walk-in assigns to Showroom
Manager, creates a 15-minute task, notifies on reassignment (AF_FL_Opp_ServiceWalkIn +
AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate).

                                                                                 262
Open items: which BUs enable the receptionist paths (pending -- the gating mechanism is built,
but no BU has been granted the permission yet); showroom  Business Unit mapping for any
brand beyond Ferrari/Rolls-Royce (TBP).

ALF-RS-02 -- Opportunity Stage Progression and Pipeline Management

As a sales user, I should progress opportunities through a controlled stage model so that sales
movement, forecasting, and reporting are standardized.

What the system must do: Enforce the stage model Consider  Explore  Select  Commit 
Take the Keys  Closed Won / Closed Lost. Allow Consider without a vehicle model or VIN. On
progression from Consider to Explore, auto-create a linked Test Drive record and a linked Trade-
In record. Require vehicle/model information from Explore onward. Support brand-specific sub-
stages without breaking cross-BU reporting.

Step-by-step:

1. Reconfigure StageName -- remove the default Salesforce stages, add the seven from the
  stage model table above, set Closed Won / Closed Lost as the closed stages with correct
  forecast categories.

2. Build the Path with per-stage guidance that states the gate in plain language, e.g. on Select:
  "To move to Commit, the customer must have a synced quotation." Prevention beats a
  validation error.

3. Write the three forward gate rules -- AF_VR_Opp_ExploreRequiresVehicle,
  AF_VR_Opp_CommitGate, AF_VR_Opp_TakeTheKeysGate (see Validation rule catalogue
  above). Keep the formula logic for each gate in exactly one authoritative place in the
  validation-rule catalogue, so anyone building from this page uses the same formula every
  time.

4. Build the two flow-maintained-rollup flows -- AF_FL_InvoiceSummary_PushBalance and
  AF_FL_Handover_PushCompletion -- as record-triggered, after-save flows on their respective
  child objects, each writing one field to the parent Opportunity. Both belong to their owning
  epic (LFRDN-127, LFRDN-130) but the target field and contract are fixed here so all three
  teams build against the same interface.

5. Build AF_FL_Opp_ExploreEntry -- trigger on update where StageName changes to Explore
  and the prior value was Consider. Create one Test Drive and one Trade-In appraisal if none
  already exists, so re-entering the stage doesn't spawn duplicates.

6. Add the brand sub-stage field as a dependent picklist, excluded from cross-BU report
  groupings by convention.

7. Sequence the dependencies -- see the Sequencing note under Relationship model above.

                                                                                 263
Acceptance criteria coverage: Opportunity saves at Consider with no vehicle model (the
vehicle rule excludes the Consider stage); moving to Explore enables test drive, trade-in and
quotation sub-processes (AF_FL_Opp_ExploreEntry); cross-BU pipeline report groups by the
unified stage model despite sub-stages (reporting on StageName; sub-stage is a separate
field).

Open items: final stage names and the brand sub-stage matrix (pending sales leadership); field
names/relationships on Quote, Invoice Summary, Test Drive, Trade-In (cross-epic agreement
needed).

ALF-RS-14 -- Lost-Sale Outcome Capture

As a business, we should capture lost-sale outcomes so that pipeline quality, reasons for loss,
and future re-engagement can be improved.

What the system must do: Allow Closed Lost at any stage. On selection of a loss reason, route
an approval to the Showroom Manager before the Opportunity formally closes. On approval,
evaluate the reason: if flagged as requiring CRM follow-up, auto-create a follow-up task; if not,
close with no further action. On rejection, leave the Opportunity exactly as it was and notify the
rep. Capture reason, competitor/alternative outcome and notes. Feed reporting and Marketing
Cloud re-engagement. Also create a review task for the Showroom Manager on closure.

Step-by-step:

1. Create AF_LossReason__mdt and populate one record per business-supplied reason, ticking
  AF_RequiresCRMFollowUp__c where the business wants CRM to chase.

2. Add the Opportunity fields -- reason, competitor outcome, notes, approval status.
3. Build AF_FL_Opp_RequestClosure as a Quick Action screen flow reachable from any active

  stage: screen captures reason (required), competitor outcome, and notes (required); on
  submit, sets AF_LostApprovalStatus__c = "Pending" only. StageName is not touched, which is
  what keeps this path deadlock-free.
4. Build the approval process with entry criteria AF_LostApprovalStatus__c = "Pending" (no
  reference to StageName anywhere in the process). Approver: Showroom Manager, resolved
  from the submitter's role hierarchy. Final approval sets status Approved; final rejection sets
  status Rejected.

                                                                                 267
5. Build AF_FL_Opp_LostApproved -- on status  Approved: set StageName = "Closed Lost";
  get the AF_LossReason__mdt record matching AF_LostReason__c; if
  AF_RequiresCRMFollowUp__c is true, create a CRM follow-up Task; always create the
  Showroom Manager review task. Because this flow runs after the approval process has
  already set the status to Approved, AF_VR_Opp_LostApprovalRequired is already satisfied
  when this flow sets the stage -- no deadlock.

6. Build AF_FL_Opp_LostRejected -- on status  Rejected: clear AF_LostApprovalStatus__c,
  AF_LostReason__c, AF_LostNotes__c, and notify the rep with the rejection comment. The
  Opportunity is exactly where it was before the request -- no stage tracking required.

7. Keep AF_VR_Opp_LostApprovalRequired as the backstop that blocks anyone from setting
  StageName = "Closed Lost" directly, bypassing the request flow -- this is what makes the
  request path the only path.

8. Hand the Marketing Cloud trigger downstream -- the re-engagement journey fires after a
  defined delay post-closure, not immediately. The delay lives in the Marketing Cloud journey,
  not in Salesforce automation; Salesforce's only obligation is to make Closed Lost
  opportunities queryable with their reason and closure date.

Acceptance criteria coverage: closing as Lost from Explore is accepted and prompts for a
reason (Request Closure action reachable from any stage; screen requires reason/notes);
reason and competitor visible in the lost-sale analysis report (report on the new fields);
marketing can filter Closed Lost within a date range for audiences (standard reporting on
StageName + CloseDate).

Open items: loss reason list and the per-reason CRM-follow-up flag (TBP by business); exact
rejection notification content (pending design confirmation); Marketing Cloud re-engagement
delay period (pending marketing team).

      Custom Notification: AF_FL_Opp_LostRejected flow now sends both Task (for
      Activity History) and Custom Notification (real-time alert) on rejection.
      New Flow: Added AF_FL_Opp_DefaultName flow for Opportunity naming.
      Fault Handling: Enhanced error handling across screen flows
      ( AF_FL_Opp_RequestClosure , AF_FL_Opp_SalesWalkIn ,
       AF_FL_Opp_ServiceWalkIn , AF_FL_Opp_AcknowledgeDuplicate ) with
       faultConnector routing to error screens and improved error messages.
      Walk-in Flow BU Gating: Sales and Service walk-in flows now include Custom
      Permission checks ( AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn , AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn ) at flow
      start to enable per-BU configuration via permission sets.
      Test Drive Data Carryover: Lead Convert settings now properly map test drive fields
      from Lead to Opportunity ( AF_InterestedInTestDrive__c 
       AF_CarriedTestDriveInterest__c , etc.).

Related scenarios on other pages: SC-10 (role-hierarchy pipeline visibility) is detailed on the
Account and Contact Management page's Security & Access Model subpage.

Open Items / Confirmations

  Confirm with the Quotation LLD (LFRDN-122) whether SyncedQuoteId sync only happens on
  acceptance, or whether the Commit gate additionally needs a status check via a flow-
  maintained field.
  Duplicate-opportunity handling -- warn or block. Resolved -- flag-and-notify, never block.
  Built as AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate.
  Field names/relationships on Quote, Invoice Summary, Test Drive, Trade-In require cross-epic
  agreement before the flow-maintained-rollup flows can be finalised.
  Final stage names and the brand sub-stage matrix.
  Loss reason list and the per-reason CRM-follow-up flag.
  New: which BUs are granted AF_CanUseSalesWalkIn / AF_CanUseServiceWalkIn -- the
  gating mechanism is built, but no BU has been enabled yet.

The Opportunity object landscape, its dependency interface with other epics, and the standard-

Data Model -- Opportunity Relationships

Relationship                             Nature

                                         Management page for the Account side

Opportunity  Handover                    Lookup child; pushes
                                         AF_HandoverComplete__c to the parent the
                                         same way

Opportunity's stage gates read fields pushed in from three other epics' objects rather than a
roll-up across the object boundary -- lookup relationships (not master-detail) rule out native
roll-up summaries here, which is why the push-flow pattern is used (see the Retail Sales page's
Design Decisions for the full reasoning).

Opportunity -- Field Origin Audit

Standard: StageName (values replaced), Amount/CloseDate/ExpectedRevenue/Probability,

Vehicle of Interest -- Lookup on Opportunity

Lookup, not picklist, on Opportunity. The vehicle needs to be a real catalogue record so
quotes and reservations can hang off it, so AF_VehicleModel__c is a Lookup to VehicleDefinition.
(On the Lead, the equivalent field is a lightweight picklist -- see the Lead Management page --
because a caller may only say "an SUV, maybe" and a lookup would force precision the
conversation does not have.) The conversion flow maps the Lead's picklist to this lookup where
a confident match exists. Align with LFRDN-125.

Implementation status update -- 16 Aug 2026. Two corrections below: the Approval

Stage names confirmed (BRD ALF-RS-02 #1). Probabilities and forecast categories proposed --
no values were given; these are a conventional retail-automotive curve and should be tuned
once historical conversion data exists. Brand sub-stages: no values proposed -- inventing them
would produce reporting built on fiction, so the field stays deployed and empty until the brand
matrix arrives.

Why not the Approval Process's own built-in email template? Tested directly, twice, with two
different HTML formats -- the Standard Approval Process's <emailTemplate> field does not
reliably deliver HTML in this org; only plain text sends through that mechanism. Since a branded
HTML email was wanted, all three notifications were built as native Flow "Send Email"
( emailSimple ) actions inside record-triggered Flows instead -- this calls
Messaging.sendEmail directly and has no such restriction. The Approval Process still keeps
a plain-text emailTemplate ( AF_ET_Opp_ApprovalRequested ) purely to replace
Salesforce's own generic default work-item notification ("X has requested your approval -- click
this link") with something readable -- Salesforce always sends some email to a newly assigned
approver and this can't be fully suppressed at the process level, only replaced. The approver
therefore receives two emails per request: one plain-text platform notification, one branded
HTML one. A user-level preference

                                       286
( User.UserPreferencesReceiveNoNotificationsAsApprover ) can suppress the
platform one entirely per-approver if wanted.

Real bugs discovered and fixed along the way (not design choices):

  Cross-object formula references to a Lookup(User)'s .Name (e.g. Owner.Name ) silently
  resolve blank in this org, in both CustomField formulas and Flow $Record formulas --
  worked around with an explicit Opportunity.AF_OppOwnerName__c formula field
  ( Owner.FirstName & " " & Owner.LastName , since even Owner.Name alone is
  rejected by the formula compiler) and explicit Get_Account / Get_Owner_User record
  lookups in each Flow instead of relying on relationship dot-walking, which was also silently
  returning blank at runtime for the Account name.
  A Screen Flow ( AF_FL_Opp_RequestClosure ) cannot be invoked programmatically --
   Flow.Interview.start() explicitly rejects the Screen Flow process type. Any
  notification logic embedded inside a Screen Flow is therefore both untestable via Apex and
  only fires on an actual UI click. The approval-request notification was moved out of the
  Screen Flow entirely into the new record-triggered AF_FL_Opp_ApprovalRequested ,
  matching the pattern already used for Approved/Rejected -- it now fires (and is testable)
  regardless of how AF_LostApprovalStatus__c gets set to Pending.
  A real bug in AF_FL_Opp_LostRejected : an element reset
   AF_LostApprovalStatus__c back to "Not Submitted" immediately after the Approval
  Process's own field update set it to "Rejected", in the same transaction -- so a rejection was
  never durably visible on the record. Removed; the reset to "Not Submitted" now belongs in
   AF_FL_Opp_RequestClosure , at the point a rep actually starts a new closure request.
   EmailAdministrationSettings.enableEmailWorkflowApproval and
   enableHtmlEmail were both false org-wide, blocking Workflow/Approval email delivery
  entirely -- fixed to true .
  A separate, pre-existing bug found via regression testing: AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate (the
  RS-01 duplicate-detection flow) read AF_BusinessUnit__c to find the right Showroom
  Manager, but a different after-save Flow is what actually sets that field -- Salesforce doesn't
  guarantee execution order between two after-save Flows on the same object, so the
  Showroom Manager lookup would intermittently read a blank BU and silently fail. Fixed by
  deriving BU directly from Brand inside AF_FL_Opp_AfterCreate itself.

Email HTML is mobile-responsive (max-width table rather than a fixed width, so it doesn't
overflow a phone screen) and branded via a shared AF_Letterhead_Alfardan Letterhead
component plus 3 EmailTemplate records ( AF_ET_Opp_ApprovalRequested ,
AF_ET_Opp_ClosedLostApproved , AF_ET_Opp_ClosedLostRejected ) -- note those

                                                                                 287
EmailTemplate records hold only the plain-text platform fallback described above; the actual
branded HTML body for each of the three real notifications lives inline in its own Flow's formula,
not in a reusable EmailTemplate, since the Approval Process/Workflow Alert path that would
consume an EmailTemplate is the one that can't deliver HTML reliably.

This document defines the instance setup and provisioning design for the Salesforce Data
Cloud implementation for Alfardan across three environments: a Developer sandbox (build), a
UAT sandbox (acceptance testing), and the Production org (go-live).

  Provisioning the sandboxes (TBC)
  Connection re-authorisation procedure per environment
  Post-setup validation checklists for all three environments

4. User Management & Permission Sets

Data Cloud uses standard permission sets to control access. All users must be assigned the
appropriate set. Do not create custom permission sets -- Salesforce strongly recommends
standard sets only, as custom sets frequently miss hidden object permissions and cause
unpredictable access issues.

4.1 Standard Permission Sets
As of September 2025, the Data Cloud Admin permission set was renamed to Data Cloud
Architect.

                 activations.

 Confirm role assignments with the Alfardan project sponsor before provisioning. Users must

Data Cloud enabled and provisioned before the deployment pipeline can be used.

 The Developer sandbox has 200 MB storage. This is sufficient for metadata and configuration
testing.

Implementation Guidelines
Follow the below guidelines for data ingestion:
1. Implementation Flow is: Data Steams creation (always make sure to configure the object

  category of each data stream as stated in this page) custom fields creation in each DMO 
  mapping of all fields from the DLO to its DMOs.

                                                                                 311
2. Do not use data bundles, each objects should have a data stream on its own.
3. Source of truth of the objects and fields should be the Automotive Cloud DD
4. Data ingestion and the data model are fully dependent on Automative Cloud, Data Cloud

  should always mirror the data model in Automotive Cloud, and any changes there should be
  applied in DC.

1. Purpose & Scope

This document defines the Salesforce Data Cloud data model for the Alfardan Group
implementation. It specifies every Data Model Object (DMO) in scope, its field definitions,
primary and foreign key relationships, formula/logic expressions, and source-to-DMO lineage,
across all three in-scope Business Units -- Alfardan Automobiles, Alfardan Sports Motors,
Alfardan Motors and Alfardan Premier Motors.

This document is the downstream companion to the Data Ingestion Solution Design. Any
change to Automotive Cloud object or field configuration cascades to this document.

 Field-level detail below reflects the standard Salesforce Automotive Cloud data model and
the standard Data Cloud Customer 360 Data Model, extended with custom fields and objects
derived from the BRD. Fields marked "(custom - TBC)" are assumed and must be confirmed
once Automotive Cloud configuration is finalized.

Important note: Every DMO in this document is also assigned one of three Data Cloud
categories -- Profile, Engagement, or Other -- shown alongside each object in the sections that
follow. Category assignment directly affects how a DMO behaves in the platform, including
which objects are eligible for Identity Resolution matching (Profile only), how engagement
history is tracked and expired (Engagement only), and how segmentation and activation logic
can reference the object. Assigning the wrong category during setup is difficult to correct after
data has started flowing, so make sure to configure it corrictly during implementation.

 Important note: Message and email engagement DMOs return the Individual Id of whichever
source record happened to be used, not the resolved Unified Individual Id. Salesforce has
confirmed there is no defined rule for which linked Individual record's value is used when
multiple records are merged into one Unified Individual during Identity Resolution.

In practice this means engagement history reliably rolls up to the Unified Individual via the DMO
relationship (Individual  Unified Individual), but you cannot rely on the raw IndividualId field
value alone to identify the person -- always join through the relationship, not the raw Id. This will
already be solved when the steps are following according to the DMO mapping in sections 8.1
and 8.2 below.

                 319
Side note: What to avoid moving forward: Never filter or match records using
IndividualId__c as if it were a reliable identifier on its own (e.g., "find engagement where
IndividualId = X"). That field can point to any one of several source records for the same
person. Always start from Unified Individual and let the relationship bring in the related
engagement records -- don't go the other direction using the raw field.

1. Overview

This document defines the Identity Resolution (IR) configuration for the Alfardan Group
Salesforce Data Cloud implementation. IR evaluates customer records against match rules,
groups records belonging to the same real-world customer into a match set, applies
reconciliation rules, and produces a single Unified Individual profile per customer -- the golden
record used for segmentation, Calculated Insights, and Marketing Cloud journeys across all
three Business Units.

For Alfardan, customer records originate from Salesforce Automotive Cloud. Per the confirmed
Account and Contact model, each customer has one shared Account (holding QID and legal

                                                                                 355
name) and a separate brand-specific Contact record per Business Unit they've interacted with
-- meaning the same real person can appear as up to three distinct Contact records before
Identity Resolution runs. IR is what stitches these brand-specific records back into one Unified
Individual.

 The BRD (Section 13.2, Functional Requirement 2) specifies Device ID as part of the highest-
priority match rule, but Device ID mapping is yet to be confirmed during build (see Open Item
IR-01).

1. Overview

This document defines 16 Calculated Insights (CI-01 to CI-16) for the Alfardan Group Salesforce
Data Cloud implementation, covering every metric listed in BRD Section 13.3 (Functional
Requirements 1-3), plus one additional insight (CI-16) added to support brand-based
segmentation across Alfardan's four Business Units.

CI-01 through CI-16 all use the Unified Individual as their dimension, making them usable
directly in the Segmentation Canvas and consistent with the journey design in the Segmentation
& Activation and Data Cloud/MCE Data Flow solution documents.

 All field names below are indicative placeholders (marked "custom - TBC") pending
confirmation of exact Automotive Cloud object/field API names during the build phase. SQL
Expressions use the DMO and field names established in that document and should be re-
validated once those are confirmed.

3. CI-16 -- Brand Engagement Flags: Design Rationale

This insight answers a specific requirement: identify every brand a customer has either
purchased from (Opportunity) or expressed interest in as a Lead, so that cross-brand and
single-brand audiences can be built as segments (e.g., "owns an Automobiles vehicle but has
never engaged with Premier Motors").
Implementation approach decided:

                                                                                 373
  Four boolean flags, one per brand, plus a numeric count and a display-only concatenated list
  -- adopted. The boolean flags are what segments actually filter on (fast, exact, reliable); the
  count identifies multi-brand customers at a glance; the concatenated list is kept only for
  reporting/display in Marketing Cloud personalisation, not for filtering.

This mirrors the same pattern used elsewhere in this Calculated Insights set for flag-style
outputs (see CI-06, which also produces a boolean-friendly preference field) and keeps
segment-building on booleans wherever possible.

 This insight is computed at the Unified Individual level, consistent with every other CI in this
document. A customer's brand history naturally spans multiple brand-specific Contacts, but that
consolidation is already handled upstream by Identity Resolution, which stitches those Contacts
into a single Unified Individual -- so CI-16 can read directly from Individual without an extra join
through Account.

4. Calculated Insight Definitions -- SQL & Logic

CI-01 -- Lifetime Value (LTV)

        BRD Reference                                BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                                     Requirement 1
        Dimension(s)
        Metric(s)                                    IndividualId

                                                     SUM(Invoice.TotalAmount) across
                                                     vehicle sale and service invoices

SQL Expression

SELECT

inv.IndividualId__c                AS IndividualId,

SUM(inv.ssot__TotalAmount__c) AS LifetimeValue__c

FROM Invoice__dlm inv

WHERE inv.ssot__Status__c IN ('Posted','Paid')

GROUP BY inv.IndividualId__c

Notes: Reflects total value across all brands and categories per BRD Acceptance Criteria item 2.
Uses Invoice as the confirmed source per the Data Model Solution's custom Invoice DMO.

 CI-01: Confirm which Invoice Status values should count as "completed" (Posted/Paid vs.
Draft/Overdue).

CI-02 -- Household Lifetime Value

                                                374
Household Lifetime Value (HLTV) is the total projected revenue or profit Alfardan expects to
generate from an entire family or residential unit over the course of their relationship with the
business.

        BRD Reference                        BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                             Requirement 1
        Dimension(s)
        Metric(s)                            AccountId

                                             SUM(LifetimeValue__c) across all
                                             Individuals (brand-specific
                                             Contacts) linked to the same
                                             Account

SQL Expression

SELECT

acc.ssot__Id__c               AS AccountId,

SUM(ci.LifetimeValue__c)      AS HouseholdLifetimeValue__c

FROM ssot__Account__dlm acc

JOIN Individual_LTV_CI ci

ON ci.ssot__AccountId__c = acc.ssot__Id__c

GROUP BY acc.ssot__Id__c

Notes: "Household" here means the shared Account, consistent with the confirmed model
where one Account can have multiple brand-specific Individuals. This is the Account-level
rollup of CI-01, not a separate calculation.

 CI-02: Confirm with the business whether "household" should also include a fleet Account's
linked drivers/contacts, or strictly the retail customer's own brand-Contacts.

CI-03 -- Last Purchased Date

        BRD Reference                        BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                             Requirement 1

        Dimension(s)                         IndividualId

        Metric(s)                            MAX(SalesOrder.EffectiveDate)

SQL Expression

                              375
SELECT

so.ssot__IndividualId__c       AS IndividualId,

MAX(so.ssot__EffectiveDate__c) AS LastPurchaseDate__c

FROM ssot__SalesOrder__dlm so

WHERE so.ssot__Status__c = 'Activated'

Notes: Feeds the Vehicle Purchase/Upselling segment entry criteria (Last_Purchased_Date >= 1

CI-05 -- Most Purchased Brand / Model / Add-Ons

        BRD Reference                   BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                        Requirement 1
        Dimension(s)
        Metric(s)                       IndividualId, Brand, Model

                                        COUNT(Asset) per Brand/Model,
                                        ranked DESC

SQL Expression                   AS IndividualId,
                            AS MostPurchasedBrand__c,
SELECT
  a.ssot__IndividualId__c
  v.Brand__c

                                        376
v.Model__c               AS MostPurchasedModel__c,

COUNT(a.ssot__Id__c)                    AS PurchaseCount,

RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.ssot__IndividualId__c

        ORDER BY COUNT(a.ssot__Id__c) DESC) AS BrandRank

FROM ssot__Asset__dlm a

JOIN Vehicle__dlm v ON v.VIN__c = a.ssot__SerialNumber__c

GROUP BY a.ssot__IndividualId__c, v.Brand__c, v.Model__c

Notes: Returns all Brand/Model combinations ranked; filter to rank 1 for "most purchased". Most
Purchased Add-Ons would follow the identical pattern joined against Contract Line instead of
Vehicle.

 CI-05: Confirm whether ranking should be by purchase count or by total spend per
brand/model, and confirm the Contract Line field that identifies an add-on vs. a standard line
item.

CI-06 -- Preferred Brand / Make / Type

        BRD Reference                       BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                            Requirement 2
        Dimension(s)
        Metric(s)                           IndividualId

                                            COALESCE(Most Purchased Brand,
                                            Lead.Brand_of_Interest) --
                                            purchase history takes precedence
                                            over stated interest

SQL Expression

SELECT

ind.ssot__Id__c          AS IndividualId,

COALESCE(mpb.MostPurchasedBrand__c, ld.Brand_of_Interest__c) AS PreferredBrand__c

FROM ssot__Individual__dlm ind

LEFT JOIN CI05_MostPurchasedBrand mpb ON mpb.IndividualId = ind.ssot__Id__c

LEFT JOIN ssot__Lead__dlm ld ON ld.ssot__IndividualId__c = ind.ssot__Id__c

AND ld.Brand_of_Interest__c <> 'Undecided'

Notes: "Preferred" is distinct from "Most Purchased" per the BRD's separate listing of the two
(Functional Requirement 1 vs. 2). Modeled here as: use actual purchase history where it exists,
fall back to stated Lead interest for prospects with no purchase yet.

                                        377
CI-07 -- Preferred Sales Representative  BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                         Requirement 2
            BRD Reference
                                         IndividualId, OwnerId
            Dimension(s)
            Metric(s)                    COUNT(Opportunity) per Owner,
                                         ranked DESC

SQL Expression

SELECT

o.ssot__IndividualId__c                  AS IndividualId,

o.ssot__OwnerId__c                       AS PreferredSalesRep__c,

COUNT(o.ssot__Id__c)                     AS OpportunityCount,

RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY o.ssot__IndividualId__c

        ORDER BY COUNT(o.ssot__Id__c) DESC) AS RepRank

FROM ssot__Opportunity__dlm o

GROUP BY o.ssot__IndividualId__c, o.ssot__OwnerId__c

Notes: Filter to RepRank = 1 for the single preferred representative. Ties (equal Opportunity
counts across two reps) are not explicitly broken -- see Open Item.

 CI-07: Confirm tiebreaker logic if a customer has equal Opportunity counts with two different
Sales Representatives (e.g., most recent wins).

CI-08 -- Preferred Branch

        BRD Reference                    BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                         Requirement 2
        Dimension(s)
        Metric(s)                        IndividualId, Dealership

                                         COUNT(Opportunity + Service
                                         Appointment) per Dealership,
                                         ranked DESC

SQL Expression

                                         378
SELECT
  IndividualId,
  Dealership__c AS PreferredBranch__c,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY IndividualId ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS BranchRank

FROM (
  SELECT o.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, o.Dealership__c AS Dealership__c
  FROM ssot__Opportunity__dlm o
  UNION ALL
  SELECT sa.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, sa.Dealership__c AS Dealership__c
  FROM ServiceAppointment__dlm sa

) combined
GROUP BY IndividualId, Dealership__c

Notes: Combines sales-side (Opportunity) and service-side (Service Appointment) branch visits
into one preference signal, since a customer's preferred branch is likely the same across both.

CI-09 -- Preferred Time Slot (Service Appointments)

BRD Reference  BRD Section 13.3, Functional
               Requirement 2
Dimension(s)
Metric(s)      IndividualId, TimeSlotBucket

               COUNT(Service Appointment) per
               time-of-day bucket, ranked DESC

SQL Expression

SELECT
  sa.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
  CASE
    WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM sa.ssot__SchedStartTime__c) < 12 THEN 'Morning'
    WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM sa.ssot__SchedStartTime__c) < 17 THEN 'Afternoon'
    ELSE 'Evening'
  END AS PreferredTimeSlot__c,
  COUNT(sa.ssot__Id__c) AS SlotCount,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sa.ssot__IndividualId__c
          ORDER BY COUNT(sa.ssot__Id__c) DESC) AS SlotRank

FROM ServiceAppointment__dlm sa
GROUP BY sa.ssot__IndividualId__c, PreferredTimeSlot__c

                                                                                 379
Notes: Time-of-day buckets (Morning/Afternoon/Evening) are an assumed granularity
 CI-09: Confirm desired time-slot granularity with the business (e.g., 3 broad buckets as
modeled here, or specific hour-long slots matching actual booking availability).

CI-10 -- Frequency of Purchase

BRD Reference             BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                          Requirement 3
Dimension(s)
Metric(s)                 IndividualId

                          COUNT(Sales Order) / months
                          active

SQL Expression

SELECT
  so.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
  COUNT(so.ssot__Id__c) /
  NULLIF(DATEDIFF('month', MIN(so.ssot__EffectiveDate__c),
                 MAX(so.ssot__EffectiveDate__c)) + 1, 0) AS FrequencyOfPurchase__c

FROM ssot__SalesOrder__dlm so
WHERE so.ssot__Status__c = 'Activated'
GROUP BY so.ssot__IndividualId__c

Notes: NULLIF prevents division by zero for single-purchase customers. Full-history calculation
-- see Open Item on whether a rolling window is preferred instead.

 CI-10: Confirm whether Frequency of Purchase should be calculated over full history or a
rolling window (e.g., trailing 5 years), since automotive purchase cycles are much longer than
typical retail.

CI-11 -- Service Revenue

BRD Reference             BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                          Requirement 3

Metric(s)                 SUM(Invoice.TotalAmount) WHERE
                          Invoice.Type = 'Service' TBC

  SUM(inv.ssot__TotalAmount__c) AS ServiceRevenue__c

CI-12 -- VAS Opportunities

BRD Reference  BRD Section 13.3, Functional
               Requirement 3
Dimension(s)
Metric(s)      IndividualId

               COUNT(Contract Line) WHERE line
               item is a value-added service

SQL Expression

SELECT
  c.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
  COUNT(cl.ssot__Id__c) AS VASOpportunitiesCount__c

FROM ssot__Contract__dlm c
JOIN ContractLine__dlm cl ON cl.ssot__ContractId__c = c.ssot__Id__c
WHERE cl.IsVAS__c = true
GROUP BY c.ssot__IndividualId__c

Notes: Assumes a boolean IsVAS__c flag distinguishes value-added-service line items
(extended warranty, accessories, service packages) from standard contract lines.

CI-13 -- Feedback Score

BRD Reference  BRD Section 13.3, Functional
               Requirement 3

               381
Dimension(s)                         IndividualId
Metric(s)
                                     AVG(feedback rating) across Test
                                     Drive and Case feedback

SQL Expression

SELECT
  IndividualId,
  AVG(Rating) AS FeedbackScore__c

FROM (
  SELECT td.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, td.FeedbackRating__c AS Rating
  FROM TestDrive__dlm td
  WHERE td.FeedbackRating__c IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, c.FeedbackRating__c AS Rating
  FROM ssot__Case__dlm c
  WHERE c.FeedbackRating__c IS NOT NULL

GROUP BY IndividualId

Notes: Assumes a numeric FeedbackRating__c field exists on both Test Drive and Case.

CI-14 -- Campaign Interaction Score

BRD Reference                        BRD Section 13.3, Functional
                                     Requirement 3

Dimension(s)                         IndividualId

Metric(s)                            Weighted sum: Open = 1, Click = 3,
                                     Campaign Member Responded = 5

SQL Expression

SELECT
  IndividualId,

                                     382
  SUM(Weight) AS CampaignInteractionScore__c
FROM (

  SELECT ee.IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
      CASE ee.EventType__c WHEN 'Open' THEN 1 WHEN 'Click' THEN 3 ELSE 0 END AS

Weight
  FROM EmailEngagement__dlm ee
  UNION ALL
  SELECT me.IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
      CASE me.EventType__c WHEN 'Read' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS Weight
  FROM MessageEngagement__dlm me
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cm.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId,
      CASE cm.ssot__Status__c WHEN 'Responded' THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS Weight
  FROM CampaignMember__dlm cm

) combined
GROUP BY IndividualId

Notes: Weighting values (1/3/5) are placeholders TBC.

 CI-14: Confirm the relative weighting the Marketing team wants for opens, clicks, and
campaign responses -- the values used here are a reasonable starting point, not an agreed
scale.

CI-16 -- Brand Engagement Flags (Account-Level) -- NEW

BRD Reference  Not in BRD -- added to support
               brand-based segmentation, per
               Section 3 above

Dimension(s)   IndividualId

Metric(s)      Boolean flag per brand (Alfardan
               Automobiles / Alfardan Sports
               Motors / Alfardan Premier Motors /
               Alfardan Motors), plus
               BrandEngagementCount and a
               display-only BrandEngagementList

SQL Expression

SELECT
  ind.ssot__Id__c AS IndividualId,
  MAX(CASE WHEN brand_source.Brand = 'Alfardan Automobiles' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
    AS IsEngagedAutomobiles__c,
  MAX(CASE WHEN brand_source.Brand = 'Alfardan Sports Motors' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
    AS IsEngagedSportsMotors__c,
  MAX(CASE WHEN brand_source.Brand = 'Alfardan Premier Motors' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
    AS IsEngagedPremierMotors__c,
  MAX(CASE WHEN brand_source.Brand = 'Alfardan Motors' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1
    AS IsEngagedAlfardanMotors__c,
  COUNT(DISTINCT brand_source.Brand) AS BrandEngagementCount__c,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT brand_source.Brand, ', ') AS BrandEngagementList__c

FROM ssot__Individual__dlm ind
JOIN (

  -- Purchase history: Opportunity.Brand__c
  SELECT o.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, o.Brand__c AS Brand
  FROM ssot__Opportunity__dlm o

                                                                                 384
  WHERE o.Brand__c IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  -- Lead interest: Lead.Brand_of_Interest__c, excluding 'Undecided'
  SELECT ld.ssot__IndividualId__c AS IndividualId, ld.Brand_of_Interest__c AS Brand
  FROM ssot__Lead__dlm ld
  WHERE ld.Brand_of_Interest__c IS NOT NULL
   AND ld.Brand_of_Interest__c <> 'Undecided'
) brand_source ON brand_source.IndividualId = ind.ssot__Id__c
GROUP BY ind.ssot__Id__c

Notes: UNION (not UNION ALL) is used deliberately in the inner query to de-duplicate a brand
appearing in both Lead and Opportunity for the same Individual before counting. The four
boolean flags are what brand segments should filter on directly (e.g.,
"IsEngagedPremierMotors__c = true AND IsEngagedAutomobiles__c = false" for a single-
brand-only audience). BrandEngagementList__c is for personalisation/display only -- do not
filter segments on this field.

Prerequisite: MC Business Unit Setup

1. Overview

This document defines the segmentation strategy and activation target configuration for
Alfardan Automotive's Data Cloud implementation. Segments are built on the Unified Individual
profile and activated into the three SFMC child Business Units for journey execution.
Note: The Brand__c field (or equivalent Division attribute) must be populated in CRM before
segments can be correctly scoped per BU. All activation targets below are provisional on that
field being confirmed.

5. Create an Activation for a Data 360 Target
After you create a segment in Data 360, you can publish it to a Data 360 activation target.

Required Editions

            Available in: All Editions supported by Data 360. See Data 360 edition
            availability.

User Permissions Needed     One of these permission sets:
To activate a segment:        Data Cloud Architect

                          393
                                                       Data Cloud Activation Manager

 1. In Data Cloud, click Segments and select a segment.
 2. From Activations, click New.
 3. Select the data space.
 4. Select the Data Cloud activation target.
 5. For Activation Membership, select a data model object (DMO).
 6. Click Continue.
 7. If you want to include contact points in this activation, click Select next to the contact points

   for your activation.

   When you add a contact point, select an existing path or click Edit to add, reorder, or delete
   sources and change source types and priority for each contact point.
 8. Click Next.
 9. To activate more attributes, click Add Attributes.

   You can add two types of attributes to your activation.
    a. Direct Attribute--Attributes of the Activation Membership DMO.
    b. Related Attribute--Attributes from any object in the DMO if a path to that object from the

      Activated On object exists and all the relationships along that path are either 1:1 or N:1.
      When you use a Data Cloud activation in an activation-triggered flow, flows support
      related attributes only up to two levels deep.
    c. Calculated Insights--Add your Calculated Insights metrics to the activation, and apply
      dimension filters for more granular insights.
    d. Drag up to 100 additional attributes to the canvas. If you select different columns with
      similar information, all the unique combinations are added to the output.

      To provide a unique attribute name, click the Edit icon.
    e. Save your changes.
10. To include campaign-specific data, expand Campaign Data, and click Add Data.

   You can include details such as campaign ID and description, target audience characteristics,
   products flagged for promotions, and geographic distribution. You can add up to 20 unique
   name-value pairs. Each campaign attribute forms a new column in the activated payload and
   the data extension in Marketing Cloud Engagement.
    a. You can modify or remove campaign attributes when editing an activation. To remove all

      campaign attributes, choose the Remove All option from the Add Data dropdown menu.

                                                                                  394
   You can also manage campaign-specific data through the Activation Connect APIs.
11. To use the same audience for multiple fixed-size campaigns across different channels with

   varying budgets, expand Provisional Audience Limiting, then click Rank Attributes.
    a. Drag up to three attributes to the canvas in your preferred hierarchy for ranking. You can

      rearrange the attributes by dragging them up or down.
    b. Select the sorting order (ascending or descending) for each attribute and the attribute

      path, then click Save.
    c. To remove an attribute, select the dropdown menu, then click Remove Attribute.
   For ranking attributes, you can include direct attributes and calculated insights.
12. To limit the audience for this activation, enter a number from 1-10,000. The audience is
   selected randomly. If you've ranked attributes, the audience is prioritized based on the
   ranking.
13. Click Next.
14. Enter a name and description for your activation.

MC Busines Unit Setup

Overview
This document outlines the configuration of Business Units (BUs) within Salesforce Marketing
Cloud for Alfardan, including environment separation, Data Cloud integration, and configuration
standards required to support production and UAT activities.

Data Integration Approach

  Integration will be handled via Salesforce Data Cloud Activation Targets.
  MC Connect will NOT be implemented.
  Data will be written directly into Marketing Cloud Data Extensions (DEs).

Governance & Data Flow

  All BUs will be connected to the same Data Cloud tenant.
  Data synchronization will be controlled via DE-based activation targets.
  No direct CRM synchronization layer will exist.

Structure: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Enterprise 2.0 -- 1 Parent + 4 Child Business Units,
one Child BU per brand:

BU                     Maps to
Parent/Enterprise BU   Alfardan Group (admin, shared
                       assets, enterprise reporting)
Child BU 1             Alfardan Automobiles
Child BU 2             Alfardan Sports Motors (Ferrari)
Child BU 3             Alfardan Premier Motors
Child BU 4             Alfardan Motors

This mirrors the CRM-side model in the BRD (�8.9): one shared customer entity underneath,
with the operational/transactional layer segregated by BU. In MC, the "transactional layer"
equivalent is sending, content, and journeys -- that's what gets segregated per Child BU. The
"shared profile" equivalent is identity resolution -- that stays upstream in Data Cloud, not in MC.

Overview - How data flows Data Cloud  each BU

1. Data Cloud holds one unified customer profile, but the brand association (which
  vehicle/opportunity/case belongs to which BU) is already on the transactional data coming
  from Automotive Cloud.

2. Build segments in Data Cloud filtered by that brand attribute -- e.g. "Sports Motors - Lead
  Nurture".

3. Configure four separate Marketing Cloud activation targets in Data Cloud, one per Child
  BU, each using that BU's own Installed Package/API credentials (not one activation fanned
  out to all four).

4. Each BU only ever receives its own brand's audience into its own Data Extensions.
Note: a customer who owns vehicles from two brands will legitimately exist as two separate
subscriber/contact records (one per BU), each governed by that BU's own consent and
journeys.

Headers and Footers

To disable the standard preference footers for emails, go to Setup > Feature Settings > Email
Optional Features:

From Setup: Navigate to Email Optional features

Turn off the toggle for:
1. Profile Link Check
2. Physical Address Check
3. Unsubscribe Link Check

In the above steps we turn off the standard headers and footers created on salesforce and we
customize our own footers this helps eliminate the errors when sending the emails and ensuring
Alfardan branded and customized emails.

To Customize the footer of the Org We will Navigate to Setup and then click on Account Once
we land on the account We will Click on Edit and then for the header we will leave it as it is.

For the Footer:

4. Data Extension Definitions -- Detail

4.0 Real-Time Data Actions -- Event DE Design Decision
The Data Cloud and MCE Data Flow Solution Design states that SEG-01, SEG-02, and SEG-05
pass attributes directly in the Journey Builder API entry event payload and do NOT use a Data
Extension. This section adds a refinement: an Event DE alongside that direct API call, for audit
and testability -- the DE is not the trigger mechanism.

Option A -- Direct API Payload Only (original design)

 Architecture: Data Action fires directly to the Journey Builder API entry event. No DE
involved at any point.
 Pros: Simplest possible path -- one fewer object to configure per Business Unit.

 Cons: No landing record to inspect if a journey doesn't trigger as expected. Debugging
requires MCE API call logs rather than a queryable DE. No straightforward way to test the Data
Action's output before going live.

Option B -- Direct API Payload + Shadow Event DE (adopted)

 Architecture: Data Action fires to the Journey Builder API entry event AND writes the same
payload to a dedicated Event DE (DE-01/02/03), in parallel. The DE is a landing/audit copy, not
the entry mechanism -- the direct API call is still what triggers journey entry.
 Pros: Queryable record of every real-time event for troubleshooting and reporting. Matches
Salesforce's own recommended pattern for real-time Data Actions. Makes DA-01/02/03
independently testable in MCE before wiring them into a live journey.

 Cons: One additional DE to create manually per Business Unit for each of the 3 real-time
flows (12 DEs total across 4 BUs).

Decision

ADOPTED -- Option B. The audit/testability benefit outweighs the modest setup overhead,
particularly during initial build and UAT when confirming Data Actions fire correctly matters
more than minimizing object count. This is a refinement to the existing design, not a

                                                                                 427
contradiction of it -- journey entry still happens via the direct API call, exactly as
documented in the Data Cloud and MCE Data Flow Solution Design.

Overview

This section covers the solution design of the 6 journeys detailed in the BRD.
General note: the wait days between each activity in each journey are easily customizable and
to be confirmed during implementation. The email and WhatsApp message content are TBP by
Alfardan Marketing teams during implementation.

1. Journey Overview

This journey manages leads generated from digital campaigns. On entry, the customer receives
an email; if the email bounces, the customer is retargeted via WhatsApp and added to a Call List
for manual follow-up. If the email does not bounce, engagement is evaluated - if the customer
opens the email and fills the associated form, they are added as a Campaign Member/Lead in
Salesforce and sent an acknowledgement email.

BRD Requirement Summary

                                                                                 450
 Trigger when a lead is generated from a digital campaign.

 If an email is sent but bounced, send a WhatsApp message and add the lead to the Call
List.

 If an email is not bounced, evaluate whether the email was opened and the form was filled.

 If the form is filled, add the person as Campaign Member / Lead in Salesforce and send an
acknowledgement email.

engagement email, revives the lead if engagement is detected, and creates a task for the lead
owner.

 For Inactive Lead journeys, trigger 30 days after a lead has been rejected or gone inactive.
 Send a re-engagement email.
 Revive the lead if engagement is detected.
 Create a task for the lead owner.
