1. Journey Overview

This journey drives repeat vehicle purchases among recurring-model customers. It triggers 1
year after a customer's last invoice, evaluates recurring-purchase eligibility, sends an upselling
email with a brochure link, retargets via WhatsApp if unopened, and creates a new Opportunity
in Salesforce if the customer engages.
BRD Requirement Summary
 Trigger the Upselling Journey when 1 year has passed since a customer's last vehicle
invoice (Calculated Insight Last Purchased Date).

                                                                                 468
 Evaluate whether the customer is a Recurring Model Customer before entry.
 Send an upselling email with a vehicle brochure link.
 If the email is not opened, retarget via WhatsApp after 3 days.
 If the customer clicks the brochure link via email or WhatsApp, create an Opportunity in
Salesforce and assign it to a Sales Representative.
 If the customer does not engage after retargeting, the customer exits the journey.

1. Journey Overview

This journey supports Sales Representative follow-up on newly created Opportunities. On entry,
a Call Task is assigned to the Sales Representative. If the Rep indicates No Response from the
prospect, the system sends a follow-up email with a time-slot selection link, retargets via
WhatsApp if unengaged, and ultimately marks the Opportunity Closed Lost if no response is
received, triggering the Closed Lost Opportunity Journey.

BRD Requirement Summary

                                         472
 Trigger when an Opportunity is created in Salesforce Automotive Cloud.
 Assign a Call Task to the relevant Sales Representative upon journey entry.

 Evaluate whether the Sales Representative has indicated No Response from the prospect.
 If No Response is indicated, send a follow-up email with a preferred time-slot selection link.

 If the customer clicks the link and selects a slot, create a new Call Task assigned to the
Sales Representative.
 If the customer does not open or click within the configured window, retarget via
WhatsApp.
 If no response is received after the configured follow-up period, mark the Opportunity
Closed Lost and trigger the Closed Lost Opportunity Journey.

Configuration steps

1. Under Contact Builder go to the all contacts tab create new mobile list to import the
  Whattsapp contacts to opt in in order to recieve the whatsapp messages

2. Create an import activity that map the status of these contacts from the master Data
  extension to the WhatsApp mobile list to manage opt ins and opt outs

3. Map the essential fields
4. If locale field is not added, please add it to the main DE and set default to eg.

Phone           _MobileNumber
ContactId       _ContactKey
locale          _Locale

5. Map the optional fields where opt out status need to be filled in order to send whatsapp to the
  customer and to be delivered Opt out status id should be

First Name      _FirstName
Last Name       _LastName
OptOutStatusID  _OptOutStatusID
OptInDate       _OptInDate

After setting the import activity create an automation that runs on daily basis to include the
import activity and update clients status

Create an Import Definition in Contact Builder

Create an import definition in Contact Builder to bring contact data into Marketing Cloud
Engagement.
1. From Contact Builder, click Create and select the destination for your dat`a.

                                                                                 493
 2. To import from a data extension, click Select Source and select DC_Audience_Base.
   Navigate to the data extension and click Save. Use a sendable data extension within the
   import definition.

 3. For Destination, select the data extension or chat messaging app and channel that receives
   the imported information.

 4. Select how you want to handle the existing information.
 5. Under Import Options, select any import options, and then click Next.

    a. To continue importing even if bad data is encountered, select Skip rows in the import file
      with bad data.

    b. To treat values between double quotes as text, select Respect double quotes as a text
      qualifier.

    c. To ensure that numeric values match the chosen locale value, select Normalize numbers
      based on locale.

 6. Map the attributes in your CSV file to the attributes in your account.

   You can map by header row, ordinal, or manually. To skip the first row when mapping
   attributes, click Import File has Column Headers.
 7. Click Next.
 8. Enter a name for the new import definition.

   An import activity can't have the same name as an import activity that was deleted in Contact
   Builder.
 9. Enter a brief description of the import definition.
10. Enter the pattern used to create the import file.

   You can enter a specific file name or use a wildcard to get the most recent version of a file in
   the import definition. For example, if the file name always includes the most recent date, click
   Wildcard and enter wildcards for the year, month, and day:
   filename%%Year%%%%Month%%%%Day%%.
11. Under Import Qualifications, select whether you want to import the most current information
   or skip the last import.
    a. To skip the import process when less than a certain amount of time elapsed since the last

      import, select Skip if last export was less than X hours ago. Enter the number of hours in
      the text field.
    b. To import the most current information possible, select Fail if file is older that X hours.
      Enter the number of hours in the first text field. You can also add a system buffer time in
      the second text field to give the system time to account for servers in different time zones.

                                                                                  494
12. Enter the email address where you want to receive notifications.
13. Click Create.

Mulesoft Network Architecture

Introduction

Overview
This document contains all the information needed about Cloudhub which is the deployment
option used for Mulesoft.
Scope
This document will be covering:
1. System Diagram
2. Public Ips
3. SSL Certificates
4. Firewall Configuration
5. Authentication Methods
6. Load Balancer
7. Backup Options
8. Privilege of Access

VPC System Landscape

System Diagram

System Overview

                                                                                 496
  Anypoint VPC (Virtual Private Space) is a private and isolated network hosted inside
  Cloudhub and can be connected to private intranet as one single private network.
  The VPC configuration exposes the DNS record including the IP addresses of all the workers,
  the DNS record cannot be accessed from outside the Anypoint VPC.
  Each Anypoint VPC allows the configuration of firewall rules to check inbound connections
  directly to the deployed workers.
  Four firewall rules are created by default-- two rules that allow your private address space to
  connect through ports 8091 and 8092, and two rules that allow external requests proxied by
  CloudHub's shared load balancer through ports 8081 and 8082.
  All traffic that is not allowed in a firewall rule is blocked by default.
  The diagram is shown with a shared load balancer; however a dedicated load balancer could
  be configured, which allows the use of custom certificates and enforcing two-way SSL client
  authentication.

Connectivity
IPsec Tunnel

  Using an IPsec tunnel with network-to-network configuration to connect the on-prem data
  center to the Anypoint VPC or private space depending on CloudHub version used.
  An IPsec VPN tunnel is generally the recommended solution for VPC to on-premises
  connectivity, as it provides a standardized, secure way to connect. This method also
  integrates well with existing IT infrastructure such as routers and appliances.

               Cloudhub 1's VPC connection to on prem network via IPsec Tunnel.

                                                                                 497
          Cloudhub 2's Private space connection to on-prem network via IPsec Tunnel

Anypoint VPN

Use Anypoint VPN to create a secure connection between your MuleSoft Virtual Private Cloud
(VPC) and your on-premises network. You can create multiple site-to-site VPNs if required.
Requirements for
For more information, this is the link for the documentation for Mulesoft VPN that list additional
details as well as requirements for creating the VPN:

  Anypoint VPN | MuleSoft Documentation
  Create an Anypoint VPN Connection | MuleSoft Documentation

  Cloudhub 2.0.

                      c1.eu1.cloudhub.io

being used in the sandbox is covering the following domains:

  *.internal-sy8bdx.deu-c1.eu1.cloudhub.io
  *.sy8bdx.deu-c1.eu1.cloudhub.io

Firewall Configuration

Private Space
  By default, all traffic to private space is blocked unless explicitly allowed in a firewall rule.
  The following rules are created automatically when a private space is created:
    Two rules for inbound connections from any host: (HTTPS: port 443, HTTP: port 80)
    Two rules for outbound connections from any host: (HTTPS: port 443, TCP: all ports)
  Ports:
    Ports for inbound traffic are not configurable:
       Post 80 for HTTP
       Port 443 for HTTPS
       Other ports below 1024 are not allowed

This is the current firewall configuration for the private space, this can be configurable to
comply with the security requirements by specifying the restrictions on inbound and outbound
sources.

                                                                                 499
VPC
In CloudHub's default configuration, all applications are hosted in a multi-tenant cloud balanced
by a publicly accessible load balancer.
When you create an Anypoint Virtual Private Cloud (Anypoint VPC), you can add your own
firewall rules to allow specific IP ranges and ports to reach your workers.

  By default, all traffic to the VPC is blocked unless explicitly allowed in a firewall rule.
  The following rules are created automatically when a VPC is created:

    Two rules for inbound connections from any host: (HTTPS: port 8082, HTTP: port 8081)
    Two rules for inbound connections from within the local VPC: (ports: 8091 and 8092)

Authentication Methods

                                                                                 500
The authentication method that is being used is Basic Authentication to access the experience
level APIs exposed to external clients.
Multiple security policies could be established as well, including:

  OAuth 2
  IP Allowlist and IP Blocklist
  JWT Validation
  Client-Id enforecement

Load Balancer

Ingress Load Balancer managed by Cloudhub 2.0 is used.

Backup Options

MuleSoft does not store data or contain records, all data that passes through MuleSoft should
be stored and backed up in other systems.

VPN Capabilities

Cloudhub 2.0 private space supports multiple routing types.
  Dynamic (BGP)
  Static

Check Cloudhub 2.0 VPN and determine what VPN approach suits your enterprise.

1. Executive Summary
This document defines the MuleSoft integration solution design for Alfardan Group's Salesforce
Automotive Cloud Release 1 implementation. The integration layer connects Salesforce (the
customer engagement and process orchestration platform) with Keyloop Autoline/Drive (the
Dealer Management System) via MuleSoft, deployed on Anypoint Platform with CloudHub 2.0 as
the runtime.

                                                                                 503
The scope covers integration across six modules, each detailed on its own page under Section
3 (Integration Designs): Lead Management (web-form and Salesforce-initiated lead sync, plus
inbound Keyloop lead events), Account & Contact Management (customer sync, keyed by QID
at the Account level), Vehicle Management (the sellable inventory catalog, Keyloop's separate
vehicle/Asset ownership record used for trade-ins and post-handover, and vehicle-scoped
Service Reminders / Contract Renewal queries), Opportunity Management (inquiry creation,
sales activity logging for test drives and finance quotations, internal requisitions, and payment
events), Order Management (the sales order lifecycle -- create, update via five distinct Keyloop
endpoints, confirm, cancel), and AfterSales Management (service appointments and Case
Management -- the latter currently blocked pending Keyloop's confirmation of API feasibility
for syncing inquiries/complaints). Three business units are in scope: Alfardan Automobiles,
Alfardan Premier Motors, and Alfardan Sports Motors (Ferrari).

MuleSoft serves as the middleware layer for essentially all Salesforce-to-Keyloop integration
flows. All public web-form intake -- lead capture, service appointment requests, and
complaints/inquiries -- is exposed through a single shared Forms eAPI and routed through the
standard three-layer stack. Two of these flows -- the service appointment request web form
and the complaints/inquiries web form (both under AfterSales Management, Section 6) --
terminate at the Salesforce System API without reaching Keyloop, since the appointment-
request handoff and Case Management's Keyloop side are not yet designed/available
respectively. The design follows API-led connectivity principles with a three-layer architecture
(Experience, Process, System) to maximise reuse, enforce separation of concerns, and provide
a governed integration surface.

2. Business Objectives

1. Standardize lead, case, service appointment, and retail sales processes across the in-scope
  automotive business units while preserving brand-specific operational needs.

2. Implement Salesforce Automotive Cloud as the primary customer engagement and process
  orchestration layer for CRM, service, and retail sales journeys.

3. Enable controlled integration with Keyloop Autoline/Drive via MuleSoft while minimizing
  manual re-entry and improving data consistency.

4. Provide a scalable Release 1 foundation that can later be extended to other Alfardan business
  units and future capabilities.

Design Principle: All Salesforce-to-Keyloop communication flows through the three-layer stack.
The two web-form flows noted in the Executive Summary (service appointment request,
complaint/inquiry) also flow through the full stack via the shared Forms eAPI and the After Sales
Transactional pAPI, but terminate at the Salesforce System API without reaching Keyloop -- the
Process API layer makes no Keyloop call for either. No direct system-to-system calls bypass
MuleSoft. This ensures auditability, centralized error handling, and a single point of governance.

5. Keyloop Event Architecture

Keyloop uses a webhook-based event subscription model. Events are pushed from Keyloop to
MuleSoft via HTTPS POST to an exposed listener endpoint. No message broker (Anypoint MQ)
is required for Keyloop event ingestion.

5.1 How It Works

1. MuleSoft exposes two endpoints per event subscription: an Authentication URL (AUTH0
  client_credentials flow) and a POST URL (event receiver).

2. Keyloop authenticates against the Auth URL to obtain a bearer token.
3. Keyloop POSTs events as CloudEvents (structured JSON) to the receiver URL using the

  bearer token.
4. MuleSoft System API receives the event, transforms it, and passes it up the API-led stack.

5.2 Notification Types

Type                    Payload                             Follow-up Required
Notification            Resource ID only
                                                            Yes -- callback GET to
Integration             Full resource payload               Keyloop REST API for full data

                                                            No -- data is complete in the
                                                            event

Note on discrepancy: this table reflects Keyloop's general platform event catalogue (source
predates this session's module work). It is not fully consistent with what Keyloop confirmed
during this project's own vendor discussions: despite "Vehicle" appearing here, Keyloop
specifically confirmed no webhook/event exists for vehicle inventory in this engagement --
3.3 Vehicle Management's Flow 1 uses scheduled polling instead, not an event. Always defer to
the module-specific page for this project's confirmed behavior over this general table.

Event Gap (corrected): as of this design, Keyloop has confirmed inbound webhook events exist
for Leads (3.1 Flow 3) and Accounts (3.2 Flow 3). A Service Appointment status-change event
is confirmed by Keyloop to exist, but its schema is undocumented ("TBP") -- 3.6 Flow 5 is built
by analogy with the confirmed Lead/Account event pattern and is explicitly flagged as a
speculative design pending Keyloop documentation. Keyloop has confirmed no webhook exists
for Vehicle Inventory changes (3.3 uses scheduled polling) or Sales Orders (3.5 Order
Management has no inbound flow at all -- outbound only). Payment events are conditional on a
virtual payment provider that Keyloop is still assessing feasibility for (3.4 Flow 4 -- a business
gap, not a confirmed capability). Case Management (part of 3.6) has no Keyloop API in either
direction; Keyloop is checking the doability of bidirectional inquiry/complaint sync.

1. Business Context

Online forms, Keyloop DMS, and Salesforce are the three sources of lead data for Alfardan
Group. MuleSoft acts as the integration middleware ensuring leads created in any of the three
channels are visible and consistent across all systems. Leads submitted via web form are
created in Keyloop first, then upserted into Salesforce keyed by the returned Keyloop lead ID
(Flow 1). Lead updates in Salesforce are synced to Keyloop in real-time (Flow 2). Leads created
or updated directly in Keyloop are pushed to Salesforce via webhook events (Flow 3). All lead
records carry the field AF_KeyloopId on the Salesforce Lead object as the cross-system
reference -- Keyloop is the source of this ID in every case except Flow 2, where SF Apex/Flow
captures it directly from the callout response. Every Keyloop sAPI call in this module resolves its
AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic rather than repeating that logic per
flow.

2. Integration Flows

Flow 1 -- Web Form  Keyloop  Salesforce (Inbound)

External web forms submit lead data to a MuleSoft-hosted endpoint on the shared Forms eAPI
-- the same Experience API used by the AfterSales service appointment and complaint/inquiry
web forms (see 3.6). MuleSoft first attempts to create the lead in Keyloop; if Keyloop reports the

                                 531
lead already exists, MuleSoft reuses the existing Keyloop leadId instead of treating it as an
error (see I-003). Either way, the resulting leadId is used to upsert the lead into Salesforce as
the external ID -- the same upsert pattern used by Flow 3 ( PATCH
/sobjects/Lead/AF_KeyloopId/{keyloopLeadId} ). This ensures every web-form lead
carries a Keyloop reference from the moment it is captured, reuses a single Salesforce write
pattern across the module, and lets Keyloop's own duplicate detection prevent duplicate SF
Leads.

Attribute      Detail
Trigger
Pattern        HTTP POST from web form to
MuleSoft Flow  Forms eAPI

Keyloop API    Real-time inbound -- create in
               Keyloop, then upsert in Salesforce

               Forms eAPI  Customer Master
               pAPI  Keyloop sAPI  Salesforce
               sAPI

               POST /leads/sales-lead (create)

Phase 1 -- Form Submission & Validation

  Step 1: Web form POSTs to POST /api/v1/leads on the Forms eAPI. Payload contains:
  firstName, lastName, phone, email, leadSource, vehicleOfInterest, testDriveFlag.
  Step 2: Forms eAPI performs schema validation -- mandatory fields: firstName, lastName,
  and at least one of phone or email. If validation fails  return HTTP 400 Bad Request with
  error detail immediately. No retry.
  Step 3: Forms eAPI forwards validated payload to Customer Master pAPI.

Phase 2 -- Create Lead in Keyloop

  Step 4: Customer Master pAPI transforms the form payload to Keyloop Sales Lead API
  format. Sets: externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE ,
   externalReference.application = LEADMANAGEMENT (see I-002 -- no SF Lead Id
  exists yet for externalId at this point).
  Step 5: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication
  logic before calling Keyloop.
  Step 6: Keyloop sAPI calls POST /leads/sales-lead with Authorization: Bearer {token}
  and transformed payload.

                                                                                 532
Response handling:

  Success (HTTP 201): Keyloop creates the lead and returns leadId . Proceed to Phase 3
  using this leadId .
  Lead Already Exists: Keyloop reports a duplicate (exact status code and response shape
  TBC -- see I-003) and returns the leadId of the existing matching lead. This is not treated
  as an error -- proceed to Phase 3 using the existing leadId so the Salesforce upsert
  resolves to the correct existing record instead of creating a duplicate SF Lead.

Phase 3 -- Upsert Lead in Salesforce

  Step 7: Customer Master pAPI transforms the original lead payload to SF Lead object format,
  keyed by AF_KeyloopId = {keyloopLeadId} (the ID returned by Keyloop -- new or
  existing, per Phase 2 response handling).
  Step 8: Customer Master pAPI calls the Salesforce sAPI upsert endpoint: PATCH
   /sobjects/Lead/AF_KeyloopId/{keyloopLeadId} -- the same single-call upsert
  used by Flow 3. Salesforce resolves create vs. update internally; no separate lookup call is
  needed.
  Response handling: HTTP 201 Created (with new SF Lead Id in body)  record was
  created. HTTP 204 No Content  an existing record matched and was updated
  (expected when Phase 2 returned an existing leadId ).
  Step 9: Salesforce sAPI returns the outcome (and SF Lead Id, if created) to Customer Master
  pAPI.
  Step 10: Customer Master pAPI returns success (SF Lead Id + AF_KeyloopId ) to Forms
  eAPI.
  Step 11: Forms eAPI returns HTTP 201 Created to the web form with the SF Lead Id and
   AF_KeyloopId .

Phase 4 -- Error Handling

  Validation Error (Step 2): Return HTTP 400 to form immediately. No retry. Log error.
  Keyloop Error (Step 6 -- 5xx / timeout): Retry with exponential backoff -- attempt 1 (5s),
  attempt 2 (15s), attempt 3 (45s). After 3 retries: dead-letter payload to Object Store v2 (key:
   lead-form-{timestamp} ), fire ops alert.
  Keyloop Business Error (Step 6 -- 4xx, excluding Lead Already Exists): No retry. Dead-
  letter immediately. Fire ops alert.
  Keyloop Lead Already Exists (Step 6): Not an error -- reuse the returned existing leadId
  and continue to Phase 3.

                                                                                 533
AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401 Unauthorized): Handled per the shared Keyloop
Authentication logic -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire, retry the Keyloop call once.

Salesforce Error (Step 8 -- 5xx / timeout): Retry with exponential backoff -- attempt 1 (5s),
attempt 2 (15s), attempt 3 (45s). After 3 retries: dead-letter payload to Object Store v2, fire
ops alert.
Salesforce Business Error (Step 8 -- 4xx): No retry. Dead-letter immediately. Fire ops alert.

Flow 2 -- Salesforce  Keyloop (Outbound)

When a Lead is created in Salesforce, an outbound callout is triggered to MuleSoft. The
Customer Master pAPI transforms the payload, acquires an AUTH0 token, and calls the Keyloop
Sales Lead API to create the lead. The returned Keyloop leadId is included in the
synchronous response to the SF callout -- Salesforce Apex/Flow is responsible for capturing it
and storing it as AF_KeyloopId on the Lead record (see A-005). The field
externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE is always set to prevent echo loops on the
return event.

Attribute  Detail

Trigger        SF Flow / Apex callout on Lead
Pattern        create

               Real-time outbound
Keyloop API
               Salesforce eAPI  Customer
               Master pAPI  Keyloop sAPI 
               Keyloop DMS

               POST /leads/sales-lead (create only
               -- no update path outbound)

Phase 1 -- SF Trigger & Experience API

  Step 1: Lead is created in Salesforce by a user or an automated process.
  Step 2: Salesforce Flow / Apex trigger fires a synchronous HTTP callout to POST
   /api/v1/leads/sync on the Salesforce eAPI. Payload includes all Lead fields required to
  create a lead in Keyloop.
  Step 3: Salesforce eAPI validates the payload and forwards to Customer Master pAPI.

Phase 2 -- Payload Transformation & AUTH0 Token Acquisition

  Step 4: Customer Master pAPI transforms SF Lead payload to Keyloop Sales Lead API
  format. Sets: externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE ,
   externalReference.application = LEADMANAGEMENT ,
   externalReference.externalId = SF Lead.Id .
  Step 5: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication
  logic before calling Keyloop. This is the same shared token management used by every
  Keyloop sAPI call across all modules -- see that page for the scheduled refresh, Object Store
  v2 caching, and expiry-handling details.

Phase 3 -- Keyloop API Call

  Step 6: Keyloop sAPI calls POST /leads/sales-lead with Authorization: Bearer {token}
  and transformed payload.

Response handling:

  Success (HTTP 201): Keyloop returns leadId . Proceed to Phase 4.
  Keyloop Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout / network): No retry. Return HTTP error immediately to
  the SF callout via Salesforce eAPI. SF Apex/Flow owns failure handling (e.g. sets
   Integration_Status__c = Failed and manages its own retry).

               535
  AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401 Unauthorized): Handled per the shared Keyloop
  Authentication logic -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire from AUTH0, retry the Keyloop call
  once. If the retry also fails, return HTTP error to the SF callout.

Phase 4 -- Response to Salesforce

  Step 7: Keyloop sAPI returns leadId to Customer Master pAPI.
  Step 8: Customer Master pAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to Salesforce eAPI, including
   leadId in the response body.
  Step 9: Salesforce eAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to the SF callout with leadId . SF
  Apex/Flow captures leadId from the response and stores it as AF_KeyloopId on the
  Lead record.

Flow 3 -- Keyloop  Salesforce (Inbound Event)

When a Lead is created or updated directly in Keyloop by a DMS user, Keyloop fires a webhook
event to the MuleSoft Keyloop eAPI. MuleSoft first validates the AUTH0 token on the incoming
request, then applies echo prevention by checking externalReference.provider . If the
record was originated by MuleSoft/SF, the event is silently discarded. If it originated in Keyloop,
MuleSoft fetches the full lead record via GET /leads/{id} and upserts it into Salesforce.

Attribute                                                                                       Detail
Trigger
                                                                                                Keyloop Lead.Created /
                                                                                                Lead.Updated webhook event

                                                                                          536
Pattern        (CloudEvents 1.0)
MuleSoft Flow
Keyloop API    Real-time inbound via Keyloop
               webhook

               Keyloop eAPI  echo check 
               Customer Master pAPI  Keyloop
               sAPI  Salesforce sAPI

               Webhook event � GET /leads/{id}

Phase 1 -- Webhook Receipt & AUTH0 Validation

  Step 1: Keyloop fires Lead.Created or Lead.Updated event via HTTP POST to POST
   /api/v1/keyloop/events/leads on the Keyloop eAPI. Payload follows CloudEvents 1.0
  structure containing: id , type , source , time , data.id (Keyloop lead ID),
   data.externalReference.provider .
  Step 2: Keyloop eAPI validates the incoming AUTH0 Bearer token. Call AUTH0 JWKS
  endpoint to verify token signature and expiry.
  If token invalid or expired  return HTTP 401 Unauthorized to Keyloop. Keyloop will retry
  per its own retry policy.
  If token valid  proceed to Phase 2.

Phase 2 -- Echo Prevention

  Step 3: Keyloop eAPI reads data.externalReference.provider from the event
  payload.
  If provider = SALESFORCE  this event was triggered by MuleSoft writing to Keyloop on
  behalf of SF. Discard event silently. Return HTTP 200 OK to Keyloop to acknowledge
  receipt and prevent redelivery.
  If provider is empty or any value other than SALESFORCE  lead originated in Keyloop.
  Proceed to Phase 3.

Phase 3 -- Full Lead Fetch from Keyloop

  Step 4: Keyloop eAPI extracts data.id (Keyloop lead ID) from the event payload and
  passes it to Customer Master pAPI.
  Step 5: Customer Master pAPI calls Keyloop sAPI to fetch the full lead record: GET
   /leads/{id} .
  Step 6: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication
  logic before calling Keyloop.

                                                                                 537
  Step 7: Keyloop sAPI calls GET /leads/{id} .
  Success (HTTP 200): Full lead payload returned. Proceed to Phase 4.
  Error (5xx / timeout): Retry 3x (5s  15s  45s). After 3 retries: dead-letter (Phase 5).
  Error (404 Not Found): No retry. Log warning. Discard event (lead may have been deleted).
  Return HTTP 200 to Keyloop.

Phase 4 -- Salesforce Upsert

  Step 8: Customer Master pAPI receives full Keyloop lead payload.
  Step 9: Customer Master pAPI transforms Keyloop lead to SF Lead object format, keyed by
   AF_KeyloopId = {keyloopLeadId} .
  Step 10: Customer Master pAPI calls the Salesforce sAPI upsert endpoint: PATCH
   /sobjects/Lead/AF_KeyloopId/{keyloopLeadId} . Salesforce resolves create vs.
  update internally by matching on the external ID field -- no separate lookup call is needed.
  Response handling: HTTP 201 Created (with new SF Lead Id in body)  record was
  created. HTTP 204 No Content  an existing record matched and was updated.
  Step 11: Salesforce sAPI returns the outcome (and SF Lead Id, if created) to Customer Master
  pAPI.
  Step 12: Customer Master pAPI returns HTTP 200 to Keyloop eAPI.
  Step 13: Keyloop eAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to Keyloop to acknowledge event and prevent
  redelivery.

Phase 5 -- Dead-Letter Handling

  Step 14: On any unrecoverable error: Customer Master pAPI stores payload in Object Store
  v2. Key: lead-inbound-{keyloopLeadId}-{timestamp} . Value: event payload, error
  message, HTTP status, retry count, flow name, timestamp.
  Step 15: Ops alert triggered.
  Replay: Ops team calls MuleSoft admin endpoint: POST
   /api/v1/admin/replay/{messageId} . MuleSoft reads payload from Object Store v2
  and re-enters from Phase 3 (Step 4).

Echo Prevention -- Global Rule: Applies to all bidirectional modules. MuleSoft always sets
externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE when writing to Keyloop on behalf of
Salesforce. On inbound events, if provider = SALESFORCE , the event is discarded and
HTTP 200 is returned to prevent redelivery loops. Dependency D-001 must be confirmed with
Keyloop to validate this field is returned in event payloads.

6. Assumptions & Open Items
  A-001: Keyloop Sales Lead API supports POST (create) and GET (retrieve) operations for lead
  records.
  A-002: Lead source values from Salesforce can be mapped to equivalent values in Keyloop.
  Mapping table to be confirmed.
  A-003: The externalReference.provider field is returned in Keyloop outbound Lead
  event payloads. Echo prevention logic depends on this. ASSUMED
  A-004: AUTH0 client credentials and Keyloop API audience values will be provided by the
  Keyloop team and stored in Anypoint Secrets Manager prior to development.
  A-005: SF Apex/Flow is responsible for capturing leadId from the MuleSoft callout
  response (Flow 2) and storing it as AF_KeyloopId on the Lead record. MuleSoft does not
  write this field back to Salesforce.
  A-006: AF_KeyloopId is configured as an External ID field on the Salesforce Lead object,
  enabling the Salesforce upsert API ( PATCH
   /sobjects/Lead/AF_KeyloopId/{keyloopLeadId} ) used by Flow 1 and Flow 3.
  A-007: Flow 1 does not perform its own email-based deduplication before calling Keyloop.
  Instead, duplicate detection is delegated to Keyloop: if Keyloop's create call reports the lead
  already exists, MuleSoft reuses the existing leadId to upsert into Salesforce rather than
  creating a duplicate SF Lead (see I-001 for the unconfirmed response contract). ASSUMED
  A-008: Flow 1's Experience API is the shared Forms eAPI, also used by the 3.6 AfterSales
  service appointment and complaint/inquiry web forms -- a single public web-form intake
  layer across the whole solution. This does not change Flow 1's process/system-layer logic,
  which remains as designed.
  D-001: Keyloop to confirm externalReference.provider is included in outbound event
  payloads. Dependency for echo prevention across all bidirectional modules. OPEN
  I-001: Exact contract for Keyloop's "lead already exists" response on POST
   /leads/sales-lead needs to be confirmed with the Keyloop team -- specifically the
  HTTP status code (e.g. 409 Conflict) and the response field containing the existing leadId .
  Flow 1's Phase 2 response handling depends on this. OPEN
  I-002: AUTH0 token acquisition, caching, scheduled refresh, and expiry handling for all
  Keyloop sAPI calls in this module are centralized in the Keyloop Authentication page -- refer
  there rather than this page for token-management detail.

3.2 Account & Contact Management Integration

                       Master pAPI  Salesforce sAPI � Keyloop sAPI

Status                 CONFIRMED

1. Business Context

Alfardan maintains a unified customer profile in Salesforce: one Account record per customer
(master profile, keyed by QID) with one Contact record per brand -- Alfardan Automobiles,
Alfardan Premier Motors, Alfardan Sports Motors (Ferrari) -- holding brand-specific
communication details and consent, per BRD �9.1. Keyloop Autoline/Drive holds the parallel
customer record in the DMS. MuleSoft keeps the Account master data -- name, QID, address,
sensitive identification details -- synchronized bidirectionally between Salesforce and Keyloop.
Keyloop's customerId represents the whole person across all Alfardan brands and maps to
the Salesforce Account, not to a brand-specific Contact. Brand-specific Contact fields (email,

                                                                                 546
phone, preferred language, communication channel, marketing opt-in consent) are Salesforce /
Marketing Cloud concerns only and are not synchronized with Keyloop (see A-002). All Account
records carry the field AF_CustomerId as the cross-system reference. Every Keyloop sAPI
call in this module resolves its AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic rather
than repeating that logic per flow.

2. Integration Flows

Flow 1 -- Salesforce  Keyloop (Create Customer)

When a new Account is created in Salesforce, an outbound callout is triggered to MuleSoft. The
Customer Master pAPI transforms the payload, acquires an AUTH0 token, and calls the Keyloop
Customer API to create the customer. The returned Keyloop customerId is included in the
synchronous response to the SF callout -- Salesforce Apex/Flow is responsible for capturing it
and storing it as AF_CustomerId on the Account record (see A-005). The field
externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE is always set to prevent echo loops on the
return event.

Attribute      Detail
Trigger
Pattern        SF Flow / Apex callout on Account create
MuleSoft Flow
               Real-time outbound
Keyloop API
               Salesforce eAPI  Customer Master pAPI 
               Keyloop sAPI  Keyloop DMS

               POST /customers (create only -- no update
               path via this endpoint)

Phase 1 -- SF Trigger & Experience API

  Step 1: A new Account (customer) is created in Salesforce, e.g. via lead conversion or a direct
  sales-created record.
  Step 2: Salesforce Flow / Apex trigger fires a synchronous HTTP callout to POST
   /api/v1/accounts/sync on the Salesforce eAPI. Payload includes Account master fields:
  Salutation, Full Name (as shown on QID), QID, secondary ID (Omani ID / Passport / other
  nationality document), and address (see I-004 -- whether Keyloop validation also requires a
  dedicated Nationality ID, separate from QID, is pending confirmation).
  Step 3: Salesforce eAPI validates the payload and forwards to Customer Master pAPI.

Phase 2 -- Payload Transformation & AUTH0 Token Acquisition

                                                                                 547
  Step 4: Customer Master pAPI transforms the SF Account payload to Keyloop Customer API
  format. Sets: externalReference.provider = SALESFORCE ,
   externalReference.application = ACCOUNTMANAGEMENT ,
   externalReference.externalId = SF Account.Id .
  Step 5: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication
  logic before calling Keyloop.

Phase 3 -- Keyloop API Call

  Step 6: Keyloop sAPI calls POST /customers with Authorization: Bearer {token} and the
  transformed payload.
Response handling:
  Success (HTTP 201): Keyloop creates the customer and returns customerId . Proceed to
  Phase 4.
  Keyloop Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout / network): No retry. Return HTTP error immediately to
  the SF callout via Salesforce eAPI. SF Apex/Flow owns failure handling.
  AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401 Unauthorized): Handled per the shared Keyloop
  Authentication logic -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire from AUTH0, retry the Keyloop call
  once. If the retry also fails, return HTTP error to the SF callout.

Phase 4 -- Response to Salesforce

  Step 7: Keyloop sAPI returns customerId to Customer Master pAPI.
  Step 8: Customer Master pAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to Salesforce eAPI, including
   customerId in the response body.
  Step 9: Salesforce eAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to the SF callout with customerId . SF
  Apex/Flow captures customerId from the response and stores it as AF_CustomerId on
  the Account record.

Flow 2 -- Salesforce  Keyloop (Update Customer)

When Account master fields are updated in Salesforce, an outbound callout is triggered.
Because Keyloop exposes three separate update endpoints depending on which data changed,
SF Apex/Flow first determines which section(s) were modified -- core profile, address, or
sensitive details -- via before/after field comparison, and includes changed-section flags plus
only the changed values in the callout payload. The Customer Master pAPI calls the
corresponding Keyloop endpoint(s), one or more in a single transaction, and aggregates the
results.

  SF Apex/Flow decides whether to retry the failed section.

  Authentication logic -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire from AUTH0, retry the failed call
  once.

Phase 4 -- Response to Salesforce

  Step 8: Customer Master pAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to Salesforce eAPI with the per-
  section outcome.

1. Business Context

Vehicle inventory -- in-stock, in-transit, and ordered vehicles -- is managed in Keyloop
Autoline/Drive as the source of truth. Salesforce mirrors this inventory using the standard
Product2 object (with PricebookEntry for pricing), not a custom object, so that Sales
Representatives can search and reference real records when building Quotations, Reservations,
and Sales Orders. Keyloop exposes no webhook or event for vehicle inventory changes -- unlike
Lead Management or Account Management -- so a scheduled job pulls the full inventory from
Keyloop on a regular cadence to keep Salesforce current (see A-003). Custom or placeholder
vehicles created in Salesforce are pushed to Keyloop on demand. Per the Keyloop vendor
sync, Keyloop confirmed the proposed API approach for the inventory-vehicles touchpoints
(Flows 1-2, and the related Reserve/Cancel Reservation flows on 3.4 Opportunity
Management) but flagged them as complex, requiring additional implementation effort --
both teams will continue working together on these as needed (see A-010).

This module also covers Keyloop's separate vehicle resource -- a distinct entity from
inventory-vehicles , used for trade-ins and for a specific physical vehicle's ownership
record once it leaves sellable stock (e.g. after customer handover). On the Salesforce side, this
maps to the standard Asset object, distinct from the Product2 record that represents the same
vehicle while it was sellable inventory (see A-006). Update from the Keyloop vendor sync: it is
now confirmed that, following vehicle handover, the inventory-vehicle automatically
converts into a vehicle record and is automatically linked to the owning customer -- no
additional API call is required (I-006, RESOLVED). This changes the shape of Flows 3-5 below:
Flow 3 no longer checks whether conversion happened (that's now guaranteed) -- it instead
retrieves the auto-created vehicle record by VIN so Salesforce can capture its Keyloop
identifier. Flow 4 (explicit POST /vehicle creation) and Flow 5 (explicit relation creation) are
now scoped to trade-ins only, since post-handover conversion and customer-linking both
happen automatically in Keyloop.

Flows 6-9 (Service Reminders and Contract Renewal) were moved to this page from 3.6
AfterSales Management per explicit user direction, since they are keyed by AF_VehicleId
and query vehicle-scoped data. Their Process API was reassigned from After Sales
Transactional pAPI to Vehicle Master pAPI so this page remains internally consistent (one page

                                                                                 553
= one Process API). Only the exposure/routing changed -- the underlying business logic is
unchanged from how it was designed on 3.6. Every Keyloop sAPI call in this module resolves its
AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic rather than repeating that logic per
flow.

2. Integration Flows

Flow 1 -- Scheduled Inventory Sync (Keyloop  Salesforce)

MuleSoft polls Keyloop's inventory-vehicles endpoint on a scheduled interval and upserts each
vehicle into Salesforce as a Product2 record (with an associated PricebookEntry for price),
keyed by AF_VehicleId . This keeps the Salesforce catalog current for quoting, reservation,
and search without requiring a live Keyloop call on every Sales Representative interaction.

Phase 1 -- Scheduled Trigger & AUTH0 Token Acquisition

  Step 1: Anypoint Scheduler fires the sync job on the configured interval.
  Step 2: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication

  inventory sync; it is separate from the Authentication page's own scheduled token-refresh job
  -- this step is the standard on-demand token resolution used by every Keyloop sAPI call.

Response handling:

               554
  Success (HTTP 200): Page of vehicle records returned. If more pages remain, repeat Step 3
  until the full catalog has been retrieved.
  Keyloop Error (5xx / timeout) on a page: Retry that page with exponential backoff (5s  15s
   45s). If still failing after 3 retries: abort the run for that page, dead-letter the page reference
  to Object Store v2, fire ops alert. Already-processed pages remain applied.
  AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401): Handled per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic
  -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire from AUTH0, retry once.

   Content  existing Product2 updated.
  Step 6: Price is written to the associated PricebookEntry (Pricebook2 TBC -- see I-003).
  Per-record Salesforce error: Log the failed vehicle record and continue the run (does not
  abort the batch). Included in the run's failure count.

Phase 4 -- Run Completion

  Step 7: The sync job logs a run summary (records processed, created, updated, failed) and
  fires an ops alert if the failure count exceeds a configurable threshold.

Flow 3 -- Retrieve Converted Vehicle Record by VIN (Salesforce  Keyloop)

Before creating an explicit vehicle record for a handed-over vehicle (Flow 4), Salesforce checks
the current state of the corresponding inventory-vehicles record in Keyloop. This exists
specifically because it's unresolved whether Keyloop auto-converts an inventory-vehicle to a
vehicle record after handover, or whether that conversion must be triggered explicitly (see I-
006, a longstanding open question with Keyloop). Per the Keyloop vendor sync, it is now
confirmed that on vehicle handover the inventory-vehicle automatically converts into a
vehicle record and is automatically linked to the owning customer -- no explicit conversion
call is required (I-006, RESOLVED). This flow's purpose changes accordingly: instead of
checking handover status, it now retrieves the auto-created vehicle record by VIN, so
Salesforce can capture the Keyloop vehicle identifier and store it on the corresponding Asset.
The Salesforce callout supplies the VIN as a query parameter; because Keyloop's GET
/vehicle endpoint is not confirmed to support server-side filtering by VIN, the Vehicle
Master pAPI fetches the vehicle collection and applies a DataWeave transform to filter and
return only the record matching the supplied VIN.

  create, use Flow 3's GET /vehicle + DataWeave VIN filter rather than a separate ad hoc
  call.

Phase 3 -- Keyloop API Call

  Step 4: Keyloop sAPI calls POST /vehicle with Authorization: Bearer {token} and the
  transformed payload.
Response handling:
  Success (HTTP 201): Keyloop creates the vehicle record and returns a vehicle identifier.
  Proceed to Phase 4.
  Keyloop Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout / network): No retry. Return HTTP error immediately to
  the SF callout. SF Apex/Flow owns failure handling.
  AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401): Handled per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic
  -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire, retry once.

Phase 4 -- Response to Salesforce

  Step 5: Keyloop sAPI returns the vehicle identifier to Vehicle Master pAPI, which returns
   HTTP 200 OK to Salesforce eAPI, which returns it to the SF callout. SF Apex/Flow captures
  it and stores it as AF_VehicleId on the Asset record -- MuleSoft does not write this field
  back, consistent with every other module (see A-007). This reuses the same field name
  already used on Product2 for inventory-vehicles, on a different object -- not explicitly
  reconfirmed with the user for this specific case, flag if incorrect.

1. Business Context

As a Sales Representative progresses an Opportunity in Salesforce, several things are synced
with Keyloop. First, the Opportunity itself is created in Keyloop as an inquiry, reusing the same
POST /leads/sales-lead endpoint that Lead Management uses. Per the Keyloop vendor
sync, Inquiry is confirmed as a custom object in Alfardan's Keyloop instance, distinct from
Sales Lead -- see Flow 1 and I-001 for the confirmed POC approach. Second, as the customer
progresses through the sales process, key milestones -- a test drive being booked, a test drive
being completed, or a finance quotation being made -- are logged to Keyloop as sales activities
via a single shared endpoint, POST /activities/sales-activities , with the specific
milestone identified by the classification.activityType field in the payload rather than
by separate endpoints (see Flow 2). Quotation approach confirmed per the Keyloop vendor
sync: the quotation itself is sent to Keyloop only as a Sales Activity notification
( FINANCE_QUOTATION_MADE ) -- Keyloop does not require the quotation to exist as its own
record. Full quotation details (line items, pricing, terms) are instead included in the Sales Order
payload at Sales Order creation -- see 3.5 Order Management, Flow 1 (see I-002, RESOLVED).
Third, when an accessory or PDI requirement is added to an Opportunity Line Item and
approved, an Internal Requisition Form is logged to Keyloop as a repair job (see Flow 3). Fourth,
assuming a virtual payment provider is configured to relay Keyloop payment events (currently a
business gap still under confirmation with Keyloop, see A-006), MuleSoft would receive
payment status updates from Keyloop and sync them to Salesforce -- Keyloop has since
confirmed a direct payment-event integration is not feasible; see Flow 6 (struck through)
and A-006/I-005 for the current status and alternatives under consideration. Every Keyloop
sAPI call in this module resolves its AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic
rather than repeating that logic per flow.

2. Integration Flows

When an Opportunity is created in Salesforce, it is synced to Keyloop as an inquiry so that the
DMS has a corresponding sales-lead record to attach later activities and, eventually, a sales
order to.

1. Business Context
Once a deal is ready to progress past quotation and reservation, the Sales Representative
generates a Sales Order in Salesforce. Unlike other modules, the Sales Order is not tracked on a

                                                                                 580
separate Salesforce object -- per explicit user direction, the Keyloop-returned sales order
reference is stored directly on the Opportunity as AF_KeyloopOrderId , consistent with the
BRD's characterization of the Sales Order as an internal Salesforce document rather than a
customer- or OEM-facing record. This module covers four outbound actions against Keyloop:
creating the sales order, updating it (routed to one of five distinct endpoints depending on the
change being made -- see Flow 1), confirming it, and cancelling it. Per the Keyloop vendor
sync, the quotation itself is not sent to Keyloop as its own record (see 3.4 Opportunity
Management, I-002) -- instead, the full quotation details (line items, pricing, terms) are
carried in the Flow 1 create payload below, since Sales Order creation is the point at which
Keyloop first needs that detail. BMW and JLR special orders require an internal vehicle
ordering/planning team approval before downpayment collection can proceed -- this approval
gate is native Salesforce process logic and out of scope for this integration SDD, but its exact
sequencing is still to be confirmed with Alfardan (see I-004). Keyloop also confirmed the
proposed API approach for this module's vehicle-inventory-adjacent touchpoints (Flow 1)
but flagged them, along with the related 3.3 Vehicle Management touchpoints, as complex,
requiring additional implementation effort -- both teams will continue working together on
these as needed (see A-004). Every Keyloop sAPI call in this module resolves its AUTH0 token
per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic rather than repeating that logic per flow.

2. Integration Flows

Flow 1 -- Create Sales Order (Salesforce  Keyloop)

When the Sales Order is first generated in Salesforce, it is created in Keyloop via a single create
call -- the payload includes the full quotation details (line items, pricing, terms) captured earlier
in the Opportunity's quotation stage, since Keyloop does not hold the quotation as a separate
record (see 3.4 Opportunity Management, I-002, and Business Context above). Subsequent
updates do not reuse that same endpoint -- Keyloop exposes five distinct endpoints for
different kinds of changes, and MuleSoft routes to the correct one via a Choice router based on
an action field supplied from Salesforce. If the deal includes a trade-in, Keyloop requires that
vehicle to already exist as a vehicle record before it can be attached to the sales order --
that creation step is covered by 3.3 Vehicle Management Integration, Flow 4 (Create Vehicle
(Asset) Record), not this page (see D-001).

Phase 1 -- SF Trigger & Experience API

  Step 1: SF Flow/Apex fires a synchronous HTTP callout to POST
   /api/v1/opportunities/{AF_KeyloopId}/orders on the Salesforce eAPI. For
  Create, the payload carries the order details (vehicle, trade-in reference if applicable, pricing,
  customer/invoice parties) plus the full quotation details captured during the Opportunity's

                                                                                 582
  quotation stage -- line items, pricing, and terms (see Business Context above). For
  Update, the payload additionally carries the routing action field plus the relevant change
  details (e.g. the inventory vehicle or trade-in reference being added/removed, or the updated
  order information).
  Step 2: Salesforce eAPI validates the payload and forwards to Order Transactional pAPI.

Phase 2 -- Payload Transformation, Routing & AUTH0 Token Acquisition

  Step 3: For Create requests, Order Transactional pAPI transforms the payload directly to
  Keyloop sales-order format. For Update requests, a Choice router inspects the routing action
  field and directs the transformed payload to the matching endpoint per the mapping table
  above -- no endpoint is called speculatively, exactly one is selected per request. If a trade-in
  is being added, MuleSoft assumes the trade-in vehicle record already exists in Keyloop --
  it does not create it inline (see D-001).
  Step 4: Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication
  logic before calling Keyloop.

Phase 3 -- Keyloop API Call

  Step 5: Keyloop sAPI calls the selected endpoint -- POST /sales-orders for Create, or
  the Choice-routed endpoint for Update -- with Authorization: Bearer {token} and the
  transformed payload.

Response handling:
  Success, Create (HTTP 201): Keyloop creates the sales order and returns salesOrderId .
  Proceed to Phase 4.
  Success, Update (HTTP 200 / 204): Keyloop applies the change against the existing order.
  No new ID is returned. Proceed to Phase 4.
  Keyloop Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout / network): No retry. Return HTTP error immediately to
  the SF callout. SF Apex/Flow owns failure handling.
  AUTH0 Token Expired mid-call (401): Handled per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic
  -- invalidate cached token, re-acquire, retry the Keyloop call once.

Phase 4 -- Response to Salesforce

  Step 6: Keyloop sAPI returns the outcome (and salesOrderId , for Create only) to Order
  Transactional pAPI.
  Step 7: Order Transactional pAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to Salesforce eAPI, including
   salesOrderId in the response body for Create.

                                                                                 583
Step 8: Salesforce eAPI returns HTTP 200 OK to the SF callout. For Create: SF Apex/Flow
captures salesOrderId from the response and stores it as AF_KeyloopOrderId on the
Opportunity record -- MuleSoft does not write this field back (see A-003). For Update: there
is no new ID to capture; SF Apex/Flow updates its local order/line-item state to reflect the
applied change.

1. Business Context

This module covers Service Appointments and Case Management. Service Appointments:
Sales/Service Representatives check availability and book confirmed appointments directly in
Keyloop (Flow 2); Keyloop is the source of truth for workshop capacity, and pushes status
updates back to Salesforce as work progresses (Admitted, Started, Ready for Pickup, etc. --
exact status values TBC). Per the Keyloop vendor sync, the required status-update event and
its delivery via webhook are now confirmed (see Flow 5, I-003). A public web form also lets
customers submit an appointment request via the shared Forms eAPI (the same Experience
API used by 3.1 Lead Management's web-form flow), routed through the After Sales
Transactional pAPI -- but the request is captured in Salesforce only (Flow 3), it does not call
Keyloop directly; how/when a web-submitted request becomes an actual Keyloop booking is not
yet designed (see I-010). Case Management -- per the Keyloop vendor sync, Keyloop
confirmed that sending Salesforce Case records to Keyloop (outbound) is not feasible (see
A-008, I-009, updated from the earlier "checking doability" status); we will need to assess
whether the aftersales case-handling process can proceed without this integration touchpoint
(see I-011). Until that assessment happens, a complaint/inquiry web form creates Cases directly
in Salesforce with no Keyloop involvement (Flow 6) -- via the shared Forms eAPI and After
Sales Transactional pAPI, the same routing used by Flow 3. Every Keyloop sAPI call in this
module resolves its AUTH0 token per the shared Keyloop Authentication logic rather than
repeating that logic per flow.

Service Reminders (formerly Flows 6-8) and Contract Renewal (formerly Flow 9) moved to
3.3 Vehicle Management per explicit user direction, since they are keyed by AF_VehicleId
and query vehicle-scoped data. Their Process API was reassigned from After Sales
Transactional pAPI to Vehicle Master pAPI on the new page -- see that page's Business
Context and A-008/A-009 for detail. Only the exposure/routing changed; the underlying
business logic is unchanged.

6. Assumptions & Open Items

  A-001: Service Appointments are represented on the standard Salesforce
  ServiceAppointment object, with AF_KeyloopAppointmentId as the external-ID field --
  explicit user decision this session.

  A-002: Flow 3 (web form appointment request) does not call Keyloop -- per explicit user
  direction (reversing an earlier design within this same session), it creates a request-only
  ServiceAppointment in Salesforce, matching Flow 6's Salesforce-only pattern. Only Flow 2
  (internal, rep-assisted booking) calls Keyloop's POST /appointments . Flow 3 is exposed
  via the shared Forms eAPI and routed through the After Sales Transactional pAPI for
  architectural consistency with the rest of the module, but the pAPI still makes no Keyloop call.
  How a web-submitted request becomes an actual Keyloop booking is undesigned (see I-010).

  A-005: No Salesforce sAPI write endpoint is required for Flows 1, 2, and 4 -- they're fire-and-
  forget outbound calls (IDs captured directly by SF Apex/Flow, no Mule writeback). Flows 3, 5,
  and 6 are the exceptions (all write directly to Salesforce, none via Mule writeback of a
  Keyloop ID).

  A-008: Case Management is blocked -- Keyloop has no confirmed API for syncing aftersales
  inquiries/complaints in either direction. Per this session, Keyloop is now specifically checking
  the doability of providing APIs and events to support this bidirectionally (both Salesforce 
  Keyloop and Keyloop  Salesforce), not just one direction. Update from the Keyloop vendor
  sync: Keyloop confirmed that sending Salesforce Case records to Keyloop (outbound, SF
   Keyloop) is not feasible. The inbound direction (Keyloop  Salesforce) was not addressed
  in this update and remains an open question. Flow 6 (web form  Case, via Forms eAPI

resolved either way.
A-009: Flows 3 and 6's Experience API is the shared Forms eAPI -- the same public web-

the After Sales Transactional pAPI (rather than skipping straight to the Salesforce sAPI) is an
explicit user decision for architectural consistency -- it does not add a Keyloop call to either
flow; the pAPI's business logic for these two flows remains "call Salesforce sAPI only".
I-002: OPEN -- the source data notes Keyloop exposes multiple endpoints for fetching
service appointment data and flags a need to verify which are to be used; POST
/appointments/availability (Flow 1) was confirmed, but whether other appointment-

I-003: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED -- per the Keyloop vendor sync, the required status-update

Keyloop Authentication (AUTH0 Token Management)

Keyloop Authentication (AUTH0 Token Management)

Applies To      All Keyloop sAPI touchpoints --
                Lead Management, Account &
                Contact Management, Vehicle
                Inventory, and all future modules

Auth Mechanism  OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant
                (AUTH0)

Token Storage   Object Store v2

Status          CONFIRMED

1. Purpose

This page centralizes the AUTH0 token acquisition, caching, scheduled refresh, and expiry-
handling logic shared by every Keyloop sAPI call across all integration modules. Individual
module SDDs -- 3.1 Lead Management, 3.2 Account & Contact Management, 3.3 Vehicle
Inventory, and future modules -- reference this page rather than repeating the logic inline. Every
Keyloop sAPI operation must resolve a valid token via the logic described here before making
any Keyloop API call.

2. Token Storage Model
  Object Store v2, key: keyloop-auth-token
  Stored value: { access_token, token_type, expires_at } , where expires_at =
  fetch time + AUTH0's expires_in - 60s safety buffer
  A single shared token is used -- Keyloop's client_credentials grant is application-level, not
  per-user or per-brand (see A-001)

3. Flow 1 -- Scheduled Token Refresh (Proactive)

A scheduled job keeps a valid token in Object Store v2 ahead of expiry, so that synchronous
Keyloop calls in every module almost always read a cached token instead of waiting on a live
AUTH0 round trip.

Attribute       Detail

                605
Trigger        Anypoint Scheduler -- interval TBC
               (see I-001), must run more
Pattern        frequently than the token's lifetime
MuleSoft Flow  minus the safety buffer
AUTH0 API
               Scheduled, proactive

               Scheduler  Keyloop sAPI (Auth) 
               AUTH0  Object Store v2

               POST
               {AUTH0_DOMAIN}/oauth/token
               (client_credentials grant)

Phase 1 -- Scheduled Trigger & Expiry Check

  Step 1: Anypoint Scheduler fires the refresh job on the configured interval.
  Step 2: Keyloop sAPI reads the current cached token (if any) from Object Store v2.
  If a token exists and its expires_at is still comfortably in the future (outside the refresh
  window)  no-op, exit.
  If missing, or expires_at falls within the refresh window  proceed to Phase 2.

Phase 2 -- Token Acquisition

  Step 3: Keyloop sAPI calls AUTH0: POST {AUTH0_DOMAIN}/oauth/token with body
   grant_type=client_credentials , client_id={CLIENT_ID} , client_secret=
   {CLIENT_SECRET} , audience={KEYLOOP_API_AUDIENCE} . Credentials are read from
  Anypoint Secrets Manager.

Response handling:

  Success (HTTP 200): AUTH0 returns access_token and expires_in . Proceed to
  Phase 3.
  Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout): Retry with exponential backoff (5s  15s  45s). If still failing
  after 3 retries: keep the existing cached token if it has not yet expired (best effort -- on-
  demand callers keep working); if the existing token has already expired, no valid token is
  available until the next scheduled attempt or an on-demand fetch succeeds (see Flow 2). Fire
  an ops alert in either case.

Phase 3 -- Cache Update

  Step 4: Keyloop sAPI writes { access_token, token_type, expires_at = now +
   expires_in - 60s } to Object Store v2, overwriting any existing value.

                                                                                 606
4. Flow 2 -- On-Demand Token Resolution (Used by Every Keyloop sAPI Call)

Before any Keyloop API call -- in Lead Management, Account & Contact Management, Vehicle
Inventory, or any future module -- Keyloop sAPI resolves a valid token using this shared logic.
This is the step referenced as "Keyloop sAPI acquires an AUTH0 token" in every module's flow
phases.

Attribute      Detail
Trigger
               Any Keyloop sAPI call, immediately
Pattern        before the outbound request
MuleSoft Flow
               Synchronous, in-line

               Keyloop sAPI (Auth)  Object Store
               v2  [AUTH0, if needed]  calling
               flow's Keyloop request

Phase 1 -- Cache Lookup

  Step 1: Keyloop sAPI reads the token from Object Store v2 (key: keyloop-auth-token ).
  If present and expires_at is in the future  use this token, proceed directly to the calling
  flow's Keyloop request.
  If missing or expired  proceed to Phase 2.

Phase 2 -- Inline Fallback Acquisition

  Step 2: Keyloop sAPI calls AUTH0 directly (same request shape as Flow 1 Phase 2).

Response handling:
  Success: Cache the new token (same as Flow 1 Phase 3), then proceed to the calling flow's
  Keyloop request.
  Error (4xx / 5xx / timeout): No valid token is available. Propagate the error up to the calling
  flow, which handles it per its own error-handling convention (e.g. outbound flows return the
  error to the SF callout; inbound flows dead-letter per their own rules).

Phase 3 -- Mid-Call 401 Handling

  Step 3: If the calling flow's Keyloop request still returns 401 Unauthorized despite a
  token that appeared valid (e.g. clock drift, early revocation)  invalidate the cached token
  immediately, re-acquire per Phase 2, and retry the original Keyloop request once.
  Step 4: If the retried request also fails, propagate the error per the calling flow's own error-
  handling convention. This is the "AUTH0 401 mid-call" rule referenced across Lead

                                                                                 607
  Management, Account & Contact Management, and Vehicle Inventory.

1. Overview

This SDD's architecture has 3 Experience APIs, 5 Process APIs, and 2 System APIs (see 1.
Overview & Architecture, Section 4). Concrete HTTP endpoint paths exist at every tier --
Experience (what SF Apex/Flow or a web form calls), Process (internal orchestration, invoked by
the Experience layer), and System (what MuleSoft actually calls on Salesforce or Keyloop). The
5 Process APIs are never published externally via API Manager -- they sit behind the
Experience layer and are invoked only by other Mule applications within CloudHub 2.0 -- but
each still needs its own design-first RAML contract, since API-led connectivity treats every tier
as its own Mule application with a real HTTP interface, whether or not that interface is
gatewayed for external consumers. Section 3 below lists the proposed internal endpoint design
for each Process API, resource-named distinctly from the Experience layer's channel-specific
paths.

3. Process APIs (internal orchestration -- not externally published, but each has its own
RAML design)

No Process API is exposed via API Manager for external consumers -- every one is invoked
internally, from the Experience layer or (for Keyloop-originated events) from the Keyloop eAPI.
That doesn't exempt them from a design-first RAML contract: each is still its own Mule
application called over HTTP within CloudHub 2.0, so each needs a real resource/method
interface, built and versioned like any other API-led tier. Paths below are proposed internal
resource design -- canonical, domain-oriented naming distinct from the Experience layer's
channel-specific paths -- pending review before being carried into each module's own API
Specification section.

5. Maintenance Note
This page is a point-in-time aggregation, not a live rollup -- if a module page's API Specification
section changes (new flow, endpoint correction, a flow renumbered or moved to a different
module, as happened with Service Reminders/Contract Renewal moving from 3.6 to 3.3), this
page needs a manual re-sync. Treat each module's own API Specification section as
authoritative if the two ever disagree. The Process API paths in Section 3 are a proposed RAML
design pending carry-over into each module's own API Specification section -- until that
happens, this page is the only place they're documented.

5. Data Protection
  No credentials or secrets stored in integration payloads or logs
  PII (customer names, QID, phone, email) is transmitted over TLS-encrypted channels only
  Log masking applied to all sensitive fields in MuleSoft Runtime Manager logs
  Data at rest in CloudHub 2.0 is encrypted per Anypoint platform defaults

                                            Route to dead-letter queue; generate alert
 After Max Retries

3. Dead-Letter Handling

                                                                                 628
  Failed messages after retry exhaustion are persisted to a dead-letter store (Object Store v2 on
  CloudHub 2.0)
  Each dead-letter entry contains: timestamp, source system, target system, operation, error
  code, error message, full payload
  Integration support team reviews dead-letter entries daily
  Replay capability: dead-letter messages can be resubmitted after root cause resolution

4. Alerting & Monitoring

Alert                     Trigger                    Channel

Integration Failure       Any message routed to dead- Email to integration support

                          letter queue               team

Authentication Failure    3 consecutive auth failures to Email + Slack (if configured)
                          Salesforce or Keyloop

SLA Breach                API response time exceeds  Anypoint Monitoring
                          P95 target (> 3s for on-   dashboard alert
                          demand, > 30s for batch)

Webhook Delivery Failure  Keyloop webhook POST       Email to integration support
                          returns non-2xx 5 times    team
                          consecutively

5. Monitoring Dashboards
  Anypoint Monitoring: Application performance, error rates, response times per API
  Custom Dashboard: Integration-specific metrics -- messages processed, success/failure
  rates by module, dead-letter queue depth
  Salesforce: Integration log custom object for business user visibility of sync status per record

6. Global Error Handler Pattern
Every MuleSoft application implements a global error handler that:
1. Catches all unhandled exceptions
2. Classifies the error (transient / business / system / data)
3. Applies the appropriate retry or dead-letter policy
4. Logs the error with correlation ID, source, target, payload hash, and stack trace
5. Returns a standardised error response to the caller (HTTP status code + error body)

Coding Guidelines

Apex PMD
Use Apex PMD to help you follow best practices:
Apex PMD is a great extension to warn you about Apex code not following best practices.

With the recommended settings below, your code should:
  never have a PMD error (if you commit with a PMD error, the pipeline checks won't pass)
  neverhave a PMD warning unless justified (or false positive)

Trigger Framework
Use a trigger framework is used to make sure that triggers are logicless and are limited to 1
trigger per object.
https://github.com/mitchspano/apex-trigger-actions-framework

  Bypass mechanism:
    Any user bypass mechanisms should rely onCustom Permissions.
    (this is true for Apex triggers, but also for validation rules, flows, etc.)
    For any Validation rule to do a byPass by User/Profile, we create a custom hierarchy setting,
    a custom checkbox per Account.
    Those permissions can be easily checked in Apex
    usingFeatureManagement.checkPermission('CustomPermissionName')
    See also:https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
    us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_class_System_FeatureManagement.htm

  Naming conventions for the bypass permissions:
    Trigger Bypass:
    Naming Rule: Bypass<TriggerName>
    Example:BypassOpportunityTrigger

                                                                                 643
  Must be implemented on all triggers

  Method Bypass:

  Naming Rule:Bypass<TriggerOrClass><Methodame>

  Example:BypassOpportunityCalculateMargin

  Implemented on methods that may require bypass for data migration or integration

  purposes.

Apex Best Practices

As perApex Best Practices: The 15 Apex Commandments, anyprocessing performed in the
trigger handler must be bulkified.
Keep the Apex code easy to read and to maintain:
 1. RULE #1: use Meaninful Nameswhen naming anything (classes, methods, variables, ...). Make

   your intentions explicit!
 2. Follow the Salesforce Naming Conventions
 3. Respect theApex Best Practices: The 15 Apex Commandmentsand theSuccess Cloud

   Coding Conventions
 4. Need inspiration? Use theApex Recipes
 5. Use JavaDoc /ApexDocconvention to commentallpublic classes and methods.

   Improperlydocumented public classes methods will beflagged by PMD. The Apex Javadoc
   extension is here to help!
 6. Keep the methodssmalland easy to understand ("Extract till you Drop"):
 7. If there is a need to scroll to view the full method, it's probably too long and should be
   refactored
 8. Use Service and Helper classes to reuse code across the app
 9. Refactor methods that are flagged by Apex PMD because of their cyclomatic complexity
10. Use the safe navigation operator (?.) to replace explicit checks for null references.
11. Use a consistent indentation
12. The mostimportantrule is:Don't mix spaces and tabs in the same class!
13. When you create a new class from scratch: usetabas preferred indentation (because white
   spaces are not excluded from theApex character limit). Anda lot of smart peopleuse tab
14. Render the indentation in VS codeto make sure it's consistent, and use the VS code toolbar
   to pick a consistent indentation.
15. Don't hardcode text and numerical values that needs to the referenced in the Apex Code:
16. If it's a text that is meant to be visible by end-users (example: an error message)  store it in
   a custom label.

                                                                                  645
17. Else, if there is a chance that the value would change in the future (example: number of
   records to display on a custom component)  store it in a Custom Metadata.

18. Else, if the value is never expected to change (example: status code for a successful HTTP
   GET callout), declare an Apex Constant:

19. By default: at the beginning of the Apex Class that owns the service or method which need
   access to this constant.

20. Else, if the constant needs to be reused in multiple classes: in a dedicated Constant class. Try
   to keep this class as small as possible to preserve HEAP when calling it.

Lightning Web Components

 1. Use Lightning Web Components (LWC)instead of the legacy Aura Components (except for
   unsupported components).

2.  Skill-up: Read the Step Up Your LWC Skills - Part 1 andPart 2 blog posts.

 3. Learn how to troubleshoot performance issues: TRAINING: Troubleshooting Lightning

 Component Performance using Chrome's Developer Tools

 4. Need inspiration? Use the LWC Recipes

5. FollowLightning Web Components Performance Best Practices.

 6. When components are meant to be used in Screen Flows, followLWC Best Practices for
   Screen Flows.

 7. Use theSalesforce Lightning Design System (SLDS): Unless specified otherwise, do not write
   your own CSS   whenever a similar result can be achieved using the SLDS

 8. UseLightning Data Service:To work with data and metadata for Salesforce records, use
   components, wire adapters, and JavaScript functions built on top of Lightning Data Service
   (LDS) and User Interface API.

 9. Use the GraphQL Wire Adapterto query records without using Apex.
10. Calling Apex from LWC:Call Apex only if you cannot use the Lightning Data Service or

   theGraphQL Wire Adapter.
11. Forreadoperations you should use@wire.
12. Forwriteoperations, or to control when the method invocation occurs, useimperative Apex.

                                                                                  646
13. Enable Client-Side Caching: if the component needs to use Apex to retrieve data that is
   stable (i.e. not rapidly changing),annotate the Apex method
   with@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)to improve runtime performance. To setcacheable=true,
   a method must only get data, it can't mutate/change data (i.e. no DML)

14. Always test your components onboth desktop and mobile form factors(using Device Mode in
   Chrome for instance).Neverassume that your components will always be displayed on
   desktop. Implement an alternative layout on mobile if using componentsunsupported for
   mobile use(such as lightning:datatable)

15. Fix all errors and relevant warningsdisplayed by ESLint (in VS Code) before committing
16. For component with complex logic in their controller, it is a good practice toUnit Test

   Lightning Web Components with Jest. See also "Test Lightning Web Components".

   Error handling in LWC:
WatchtheLWC Error Handling Best Practicespresentation:

   https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_sdRQJuAeys

You can use the errorPanel Ligthning Recipe to display unexpected errors with conditional
rendering:

                    1 <template>

                  10
                  11    <!-- YOUR COMPONENT -->
                  12

                  14
                  15 </template>

See also "Error Handling Best Practices for Lightning Web Components"
 https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2020/08/error-handling-best-practices-for-lightning-
web-components.html
