Code Security

  Learn how to write secure code:

   Start bythistrail: https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/security_developer

    If working on a community implementation, read the Secure Coding Guidelines for
    Communities

  sharing:
    You shouldalwaysdeclare a sharing mode on all the Apex classes (except Apex test
    classes).
    By default, most classes should be declared with sharing
       (Note: depending on the customer context, a valid exception could be the Trigger
       Handlers, where you often want to ensure a consistent behaviour in the trigger, by using
       awithout sharinghandler)
    If you need to bypass sharing in only a subset of the queries or DML operations, do not
    declare the whole class without sharing. In this situation, usewithout sharingin an inner
    class, used only by to the operations that needs to bypass sharing.
    If inherited sharing is needed, use theinherited sharingkeywords.

  CRUD and Field level security:
    See this Reference Doc: User context vs System context - Secure Apex coding
    Any query and DML operation used in a Visualforce or Lightning Components (through
    @AuraEnabled methods) should by default respect the user permissions:
    In SOQL queries, use theWITH USER_MODEclauseto throw an exceptionin the user lack
    access to all fields:https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
    us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_enforce_usermode.htm
    Use theSecurity.stripInaccessibleApex methodto remove fields inaccessible to the current
    user(no exception throw):https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
    us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_with_security_stripInaccessible.htm
    In to DML operation, leverage User Mode to enforce CRUD and FLS when
    relevant:https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
    us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_enforce_usermode.htm

                                                                                 648
Platform Cache
It is a good practice to usePlatform Cacheto improve performances when data (used in Apex)
meet any of those criteria:

  Reused throughout a session
  Stable (not rapidly changing)
  Otherwise expensive to retrieve
To handle cache misses gracefully and keep the code lean, use theCacheBuilder
Interface:https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_platform_cache_builder.htm

Testing Best Practices
Follow Testing Best Practices described here:https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-
us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_testing_best_practices.htm

More specifically:
1. TDD is often the right approach, especially when developing Apex Triggers and/or Batches.
2. There is usually no excuse for having a test coverage below90%. Aim for a coverage > 95%.
3. Make sure thatalltest methods contains anassertion(the purpose of a test method is to

  actually verify something).

                                                                                 649
 4. Avoid DML operations in unit tests. It's extremely important to have a test suite that execute
   as fast as possible (see also "Pure Unit Testing in Apex").

 5. Test methods should be annotated@isTest(instead of the legacytestMethod)
 6. Use TestDataFactoryclass, with utility methods to create and define any test data that is

   shared with more than 1 test class
 7. In the test class, perform the data initialisation in a@testSetupmethod
 8. Never use@seeAllData=true unless absolutely required
 9. To isolate the data setup process limits, enclose the test call within theTest.startTest() and

   Test.stopTest() block. It is required when testing asynchronous Apex.
10. Use Static Ressourceswhen testing HTTP Callouts (it is much easier to update when a third-

   party web-service signature changes)
11. Run tests as a test user (using"runAs" method), so that the test behaviour is not dependant

   on the actual user launching the test.
12. Do not duplicate code for testing purpose: the test classes can access private methods and

   variables when they are  annotated with@TestVisible.
13. When creating the test data, relate recordsusing external Idswhen possible (instead of

   querying the parent records with SOQL)

Boilerplate Test Class:
@isTest
privateclassMyServiceClass_Test{

 @testSetupstaticvoidsetup(){
   //call the appropriate setup methods from the TestDataFactory
 }

 @isTeststaticvoidmyFirstTest(){
    //pick the test user created in setup()
    UsertestUser= [SELECT Id FROM User WHERE ...];
   System.runAs(testUser){
      //perform -optional- additionnal setup here

                                                                                  650
     Test.startTest();
     //perform what needs to be tested here
     Test.stopTest();
     //check result, using the Assert class
     Assert.areEqual(expectedResult,actualResult,'Shortexplanation');
   }
 }
}

Test Data Factory Class
  The Test Data Factory is a utility class used to generate test data.
  The Test Data Factory contains a list of public static methods to generate test records.
  Methods should allow the creation of multiple records (Bulk test data creation).
  Methods should allow the creation of records without inserting them.
  Test methods have the following structure:

/**
@description ...
@param ...
...
@return ...
*/
public static List<SObject> createSObjects(Integer numberOfRecords, ..., Boolean doInsert) {

  List<SObject> results = new List<SObject>();
  for (Integer i = 0; i < numberOfRecords; i++) {

    results.add(new SObject(
       Name = 'Test Name ' + i,
       ...

                                                                                 651
    ));
  }
  if (doInsert) {

    insert results;
  }
  return results;
}

Example of Test Data Factory method to create test contacts:

/**
@description
@param
@param
@param
@return
*/
public static List<Contact> createContacts(Integer numberOfRecords, List<Account> accounts,
Boolean doInsert) {

  Id recordTypeId = Utils.getRecordTypeId('Contact',
Constant.RT_CTC_CUSTOMER).RecordTypeId;

  List<Contact> results = new List<Contact>();
  Integer accountsSize = accounts.size();

  for (Integer i = 0; i < numberOfRecords; i++) {
    results.add(new Contact(
       Lastname = 'Test' + i,
       AccountId = accounts[Math.mod(i, accountsSize)].Id,

                                                                                 652
       RecordTypeId = recordTypeId,
       Email = 'test' + i + '@test.com'
    ));
  }

  if (doInsert) {
    insert results;

  }

  return results;
}

MuleSoft Project Framework Guidelines

This document provides detailed guidelines for implementing a robust MuleSoft project
framework. It covers logging, error handling, dashboards, security, and MUnit testing.
Project Setup

Interface XML File

This is the primary XML file that defines all the flows specified in the RAML file. It must not
contain any logic implementation. Each flow should only include the logging framework
implementation and a flow reference to the corresponding sub-flow.

                                                                                 674
Global XML File

This file should hold all project-level configurations, including but not limited to:
  HTTP Listener
  HTTP Request
  Connectors
  Secure Properties
  ...etc.

No configuration elements should exist outside this file to ensure maintainability and
consistency.

                                                                                 675
Features Folder

Located under src/main/mule , this folder should contain subfolders for each interface,
such as:

  Customer Interface
  Item Interface
  ...etc.
Each subfolder should include the respective sub-flow XML files, which are referenced in the
Interface XML file. These sub-flows must contain the core business logic implementation,
adhering to the logging framework standards.

                                                                                 676
Properties Folder

This folder is dedicated to holding environment-specific properties files for all environments
configured in Anypoint Platform (e.g., Dev, UAT, Production). Each file should include the
unique configuration values for its respective environment, such as:

   apiId

  Credentials
  HTTP Request configuration values
  ...etc.

                                                                                 677
Logging Framework
   Logging is critical for monitoring, debugging, and auditing. The logging framework will vary
   based on the type of API.
  Experience APIs:
   Log at the start and end of each flow.
   Logs should include flow name, timestamp, and payload details in JSON format.
  Process APIs:
   Log at the start and end of each flow.
   Log the payload before making any HTTP requests.
   Log the HTTP responses received from external systems.
  System APIs:
   Log at the start and end of each flow.
   Logs should include flow name, timestamp, and payload details in JSON format.

Error Handling
   A robust error-handling mechanism ensures that errors are managed gracefully and
   consistently across the application.
  Global Error Handler:
   Implement a global error handler to manage common errors (e.g., HTTP, database,
   validation).
   Set appropriate HTTP status codes for each error type.
   Log errors in JSON format, including error type, description.
  User-Friendly Error Messages:
   Return user-friendly error messages in the response payload to help consumers understand
   and resolve issues.

                                                                                 678
Dashboards
   Dashboards provide real-time visibility into the performance and health of your MuleSoft
   applications.
  Anypoint Monitoring:

                                                                                 679
   Use Anypoint Monitoring to create custom dashboards for tracking key metrics such as API
   usage, error rates, and response times.

  Alerts and Notifications:
   Set up alerts for critical metrics (e.g., high error rates, slow response times) to proactively
   address issues.
Security
   Security is a critical aspect of any MuleSoft project. Follow these best practices to secure
   your APIs and data:
  Client ID Enforcement:
   Enforce client ID validation for all APIs. This is a long-term security measure that does not
   require frequent updates.

  OAuth 2.0 (Optional):
   Implement OAuth 2.0 for additional security if required. Note that OAuth certificates expire
   and will need periodic renewal.
  Data Encryption: Secure Properties Generator
   Encrypt all passwords in configuration files.
   Implement payload encryption for sensitive data in specific cases, if required.

                                                                                 680
MUnit Testing
   Munit is the testing framework for MuleSoft applications. Follow these guidelines to ensure
   comprehensive testing:
  Endpoint Testing:
   Each endpoint should be covered with both success and failure test cases.
   If an endpoint has multiple paths (e.g., different query parameters or payloads), each path
   should be tested with a different test flow.
   Failure Test Cases should be implemented using `Try' node and in the Error Handling section
   should contain an `On Error Continue' component to avoid test case failure.
  Mocking External Systems:
   For Experience,Process APIs and System APIs, mock the responses of any external HTTP
   requests to simulate real-world scenarios.
   Ensure that mocked responses cover both success and error cases.

Success Response Test Flow Example

                                                                                 681
Failure Response Test Flow Example

Add pipeline documentation

                                                                                 682
Frameworks

  Apex Design Pattern: Overview - fflib
    Apex enterprise patterns framework will be used:
       Service layer will be developed as per the Salesforce guidelines, using fflib for the unit of
       work implementation.

       Domain layer will be developed to handle the trigger methods, as well as the SObject
       Specific implementations.

       Selector layer will be developed keeping in consideration unifying the methods to ideally
       have only one method for each object when possible. This reduces the variants of the
       selector methods, and conditions as well as fields/field sets can be passed dynamically
       into the methods as parameters.

                                                                                 683
Triggers:
  Triggers will be implemented using the domain handler on fflib.
  Record triggered flows will need to be developed for all the use cases unless there is
  complexity that cannot be handled by flows.
  Triggers to have a check prior to execution
    Object metadata Checkbox (Unique per Object)  ObjectAutomation_Enable
  Handler methods to have a check prior to execution
    Object handler Checkbox (Unique per Object per Operation)  ObjectOperation_Enable

Flows:
  All flow types can be utilized for this project:
    Record triggered.
    Screen Flows.
    Auto-launched.
  We should ideally have only one record triggered flow per object, these flows are mainly
  the orchestrator (Service Flow), then child subflows that will handle different scenarios
  should be developed and called from the main flow, ensuring maintainability, scalability and
  reusability, as well as ensuring the order of execution is followed and there is an ability to
  track the behavior consistently.
  Flow Trigger explorer to be used to organize the order or execution.
  Flows to have a decision element prior to execution to check the object automation
  checkbox)

                                                                             684

Logging:
  Nebula logger to be utilized for logging purposes.
    Documentation: Nebula Logger Documentation
  Easily add log entries via Apex, Lightning Components (lightning web components (LWCs)
  & aura components), Flow & Process Builder to generate 1 consolidated, unified log
  Manage & report on logging data using the Log__c and LogEntry__c objects
  Leverage LogEntryEvent__e platform events for real-time monitoring & integrations

                                                                             687
 Enable logging and set the logging level for different users & profiles using
 LoggerSettings__c custom hierarchy setting
 In addition to the required fields on this Custom Setting record, LoggerSettings__c ships
 with SystemLogMessageFormat__c, which uses Handlebars-esque syntax to refer to fields
 on the LogEntryEvent__e Platform Event. You can use curly braces to denote merge field
 logic, eg: {OriginLocation__c}\n{Message__c} - this will output the contents of
 LogEntryEvent__e.OriginLocation__c, a line break, and then the contents of
 LogEntryEvent__e.Message__c
 Automatically mask sensitive data by configuring LogEntryDataMaskRule__mdt custom
 metadata rules
 View related log entries on any Lightning SObject flexipage by adding the 'Related Log
 Entries' component in App Builder
 Dynamically assign tags to Log__c and LogEntry__c records for tagging/labeling your logs
 Plugin framework: easily build or install plugins that enhance the Log__c and LogEntry__c
 objects, using Apex or Flow (not currently available in the managed package)
 Event-Driven Integrations with Platform Events, an event-driven messaging architecture.
 External integrations can subscribe to log events using the LogEntryEvent__e object - see
 more details at the Platform Events Developer Guide site
Learn more about the design and history of the project on Joys Of Apex blog post
